column5: Accepted; amended by ADR-0052: the project-owned, dependency-free public model contract remains; MAF is the reference implementation infrastructure behind an isolated boundary and must not leak into bOps.Abstractions.
Provenance note (written at V0.9.1; no code change).
column12: Provenance only; no prescription.

column5: bOps.Abstractions is dependency-free permanently (absolute rule); a project-owned model contract moves on the project schedule, not a third-party library's; Microsoft.Extensions.AI is not a dependency of the contract.

IChatModel, ChatTurn, ModelToolCall, ModelRequest, ModelResponse, ChatModelDescriptor and ModelUsage are defined in bOps.Abstractions and owned by the project; provider packages translate to and from vendor SDK/HTTP calls so a vendor or Microsoft.Extensions.AI break touches exactly one adapter.

Rejected: depending on Microsoft.Extensions.AI in Abstractions (couples audit/replay/policy shapes B1/B8 to a third party), or mixing abstraction-based and raw-HTTP providers (one consistent IChatModel is required, D-007 tool-calling shape).
Every provider package implements the same project-owned IChatModel directly; bOps.Abstractions has zero external dependencies.
Accepted; backfill note (written V0.9.1 for a V0.1 decision hardened at V0.3 by ADR-0015).
column12: Provenance only.

column5: Original plan left Critical=forbidden enforceable only by convention (policy.yaml could assign another mode); risk must be a declarative tool property decided by policy, never a command blacklist (principle 2).

Five ordered risk levels Read/Low/Medium/High/Critical declared once per tool in ToolManifest, never inferred from name or arguments; three modes Automatic/Approval/Forbidden are what the policy engine maps risk (or tool override or package ceiling) onto; Critical is Forbidden unconditionally and not configurable, enforced twice: PolicyConfigLoader rejects any other Critical mode loudly at load time and PolicyEngine.Evaluate checks Critical first, before any config lookup.

Rejected: three coarse levels (per-package ceilings need all five); a command blacklist (core would name tools, violates A1); a configurable break-glass override for Critical (rejected permanently: the answer to "but I need it" is that the operation happens outside bOps, by hand).
Risk is legible before running; no shipped tool declares Critical (first candidates scheduled for V1.6/V1.8); the invariant is what makes those versions safe to build.
column12: Roadmap fact; the invariant itself is carried by C02:critical-forbidden.

column5: Accepted; backfill note (V0.1 shared adapter, V0.8 Anthropic native adapter).
column12: Provenance only.

column5: OpenAiCompatibleChatModel cannot live in bOps.Abstractions (dependency-free, provider-agnostic) nor be copy-pasted across packages; Anthropic Messages API is not Chat-Completions-shaped.

bOps.Packages.Providers.OpenAiCompatible is a plain shared library implementing IChatModel once, including the JSON-schema-in-prompt fallback for models without reliable native tool calling; OpenRouter, Ollama, LlamaCpp, OpenAi and DeepSeek are thin IModelProviderPackage wrappers; Anthropic implements IChatModel natively against the Messages API.
Rejected: one adapter per provider with identical wire format; one universal adapter spanning Chat Completions and Messages; placing the adapter in Abstractions (HTTP dependency, provider defaults).
A new OpenAI-compatible provider is a thin package, not a new adapter; the Anthropic adapter is the single place native tool_use/tool_result blocks are handled, kept separate from the shared shape.
Accepted; backfill of principle 7 and rule A8 (in force since V0.1).
column12: Provenance only.

column5: Original plan placed an ISystemProvider inside a Service package; following it would make the core know ISystemProvider and make adding an OS mean forking a package; same question for LLM providers.

Exactly two package extension points, IToolProvider and IModelProviderPackage (later extended by ISkillProvider : IToolProvider, ADR-0025), identical for first- and third-party packages; operating systems are packages (System.Windows, System.Linux, later macOS) contributing complete ITool implementations selected by the registry platform filter; no ISystemProvider, no IServiceProvider2; shared OS-family code lives in a plain class library (System.Core), never a cross-package service contract (A9).

Rejected: packages contributing platform services to other packages; provider selection by runtime switch (core would need OS/provider-specific branches, violating A1); ChatModelRegistry resolves by provider id from registered IModelProviderPackage with zero hardcoded provider names in bOps.Runtime.
Windows and Linux packages ship complete independent tool implementations sharing only inert formatting/manifest code from System.Core; six provider packages exist as proof of the pattern.
column12: Restates the decision; invariant carried by C02:os-as-packages.

column5: Accepted; restates D-001; V1.4 remote transport does not supersede it.
column12: Provenance only.

column5: Local-only vs controller+remote agents; building remote at V0.1 would delay the first working version for an unneeded capability.
column12: Rationale only.

column5: bOps runs locally on the machine it administers (until V1.4 remote transport); the contract is remote-capable by construction: NodeId on every TaskState, PlanStep and AuditEvent (A3) though only NodeId.Local exists; IToolRegistry and ICapabilityProbe resolved per node, not process-wide singletons (A4); policy evaluated on the node that executes (A5); IAuditSink writes node-local first, aggregation separate (A6); the tool boundary crosses only as a serializable ToolCallResult (A2), never a Stream, live Process or non-transportable type.
Rejected: controller+remote agents from V0.1; SSH-based remote execution layered onto local tools (it would be the generic execution tool S1 forbids under another name).

A2-A6 are the entire difference between adding remote transport and rewriting the runtime; a Control Plane may send a node only typed objectives, never raw commands, and the node re-checks policy, approval and entitlement locally regardless of what the controller says.
Accepted; backfill of D-003 (loader design is ADR-0020).
column12: Provenance only.

column5: PublishAot=true and dynamic loading of third-party assemblies are technically incompatible; principle 7 depends on dynamic loading; AOT would also constrain Docker.DotNet and ORMs.
column12: Rationale; the resulting rule is in Decision.

column5: Drop PublishAot; ship self-contained with partial trimming; dynamic package loading via AssemblyLoadContext is the capability kept.
Rejected: two hosts (lite AOT + full); AOT with only static first-party packages (kills closed-source third-party distribution, which the open-core plan needs).
Startup ~80 ms vs ~15 ms and tens of MB binary are accepted; bOps.Abstractions stays fully reflection-loadable for the loader.
column12: Cost figures are historical; reflection-loadable requirement is carried by C05:hosts-packaging.

column5: Accepted; amended by ADR-0039 (model-call timeout vs cancellation, failure classification, runtime-owned bounded retry with one audit event per attempt, sanitized reason, launcher backstop).

S9 requires every model call audited whatever the outcome; C1 requires nothing thrown to escape an iteration; the original loop caught only ModelProtocolException and wrote the audit event only after a successful call, so a failed call left no trace.
column12: Defect narrative; the resulting rules are in Decision/Consequences.

column5: ModelCallOutcome {Success, Failure} with required Outcome and optional ErrorMessage on ModelCallAuditEvent; CallModelAsync audits a Failure (exception message) for any non-cancellation exception then rethrows; RunAsync catches any exception from the model call (not only ModelProtocolException) and ends the task Failed - defense in depth for C1; providers still wrap failures in ModelProtocolException for a meaningful message.
Rejected: bool Succeeded (outcomes are explicit enums); reusing ToolOutcome; keeping the narrow ModelProtocolException catch (the loop would still crash on any unwrapped provider exception).

Every model call, successful or not, produces exactly one ModelCallAuditEvent (since refined to one per attempt by ADR-0039); a misbehaving IChatModel cannot crash the loop; shape change accepted under the old 0.x rule.
column12: Per-call event refined to per-attempt (C01:model-failure-retry); 0.x remark is expired (G1-09).

column5: Accepted; amended by ADR-0052: PLAN/REPLAN and bOps execution-state semantics stay authoritative; HARDEN-8 custom model-facing history becomes migration code superseded by the MAF context layer; persisted raw evidence, evidence addressability and task-budget semantics remain.
V0.1 asked the same open question each iteration, so original approach and changed mind were indistinguishable in code, audit and TaskState.
column12: Rationale only.

column5: PlannedStep and AgentPlan (revision, rationale, ordered intended steps with description and optional expected tool) live in bOps.Abstractions; a plan step is a stated intention, never a tool call with arguments.

Every task opens with a dedicated CreatePlanAsync call (JSON plan, no tool calling, parsed leniently) with one bounded corrective retry on malformed reply; if still unparseable the task proceeds with an empty plan rather than failing (C1 applies to planning).
column12: Malformed-REPLAN behavior is amended by ADR-0046 (transactional replan: second malformed candidate fails the attempt).

column5: Each per-step call carries the plan's remaining steps but the runtime never auto-executes a planned step's tool: the model proposes the concrete call with real arguments every time (principle 1).

After a step the runtime replans (ReplanAsync, revision N+1) when authorization was PolicyDenied or UnknownTool (and UserRejected, ADR-0015), outcome was Timeout, or the model proposes a tool call after every step of the current non-empty plan was attempted; a plain tool Failure never triggers a replan.
column12: Trigger set extended: UserRejected (ADR-0015), argument-validation second failure and deviations (ADR-0047), EntitlementDenied (ADR-0036).

column5: AgentRunnerOptions.MaxReplans (default 3) bounds replanning; exhaustion ends the task as ReplanLimitReached, distinct from PolicyBlocked and MaxStepsReached.
TaskState.Plans holds every plan revision, distinct from Steps (tool-call iterations); PlanStep.PlanRevision is nullable.
Planning and replanning model calls are audited like step calls through the same CallModelAsync path; StepIndex is -1 for the initial plan and the triggering step index for a replan.

Rejected: a Plan field in ModelResponse (changes provider wire contract, conflates whole-task and now questions); runtime executing PlannedStep.ExpectedTool directly (weakens principle 1 to approve-a-checklist-and-free-run); replan every step; replan on any Failure; a separate AgentPlanner project; a model-call-kind audit field (deferred, bops.plan_revision span attribute instead).
Planning history is first-class auditable TaskState; tests needed leading plan response; shape change accepted under 0.x rule.
column12: Consequence narrative; 0.x remark expired.

column5: AF-05 (2026-10-11) removed the three-tier BoundedHistory, the BOPS_HISTORY/v1 block, Agent:VerbatimHistorySteps and K=0 rebuild, replaced by the MAF context layer; still in force: raw persisted evidence and addressability (EvidenceRead/v1 with a runtime-authored evidence index), MaxTotalTokens, MaxAttemptDuration, ContextOverflow classification with one bounded aggressive recovery (goal/plan prompt caps kept), deterministic persisted-state-only rebuild on resume.

HARDEN-8 governs planning, replanning and non-final step token enforcement; once a step enters the ADR-0042 final-answer path ADR-0042 §§6 and 13 govern completion, disclosure and final-step ModelCalls and MaxTotalTokens is not re-evaluated after the original final answer or an admitted disclosure re-ask.
Verbatim window K=3 (0-15), 12 compact records of 256 code units, 512-unit archive aggregate, replan representation of bounded archive/compact/recent history.
column12: Removed by AF-05 (ADR-0052); replaced by the MAF context layer. Not a current rule.

column5: Evidence-id format ev1:<task-guid-N-lowercase>:<step-index>; retrieval primitive EvidenceRead/v1 is an exact model text reply, no registered operational tool; at most 4,000 UTF-16 chars per read and four reads per executable step or one replan call.

column2: HARDEN-8 decision summary: overflow, budgets, contracts
column5: ContextOverflow retries once only when compactable history exists; Agent:MaxTotalTokens=350000 cumulative; Agent:MaxAttemptDuration=01:00:00 active time excluding approval waits (nullable opt-out); additive TaskTerminalKind.AttemptDurationBudget, PlanStep.VerificationStatus and metadata-only EvidenceReadAuditEvent; persisted evidence is never modified; HARDEN-9 digest source unchanged; no tool-schema filtering.

Model-facing history derived each call from persisted completed PlanSteps: K verbatim steps, 12 compact records (grammar s,e,r,t,a,o,f,c,v,nr,no capped at 256 units, argument digest = first 12 hex of SHA-256, no raw evidence or tool text), one archive aggregate (512 units) with fixed addressability statement; byte-identical rebuild after every step and on resume; fail closed if required fields do not fit.
column12: Removed by AF-05 and replaced by the MAF context layer (ADR-0052 §context); the surviving properties (deterministic rebuild from persisted state; typed data only, no tool text) are carried by C01:context and C04:persisted-evidence-immutable.

column5: Evidence id is derived, never persisted: lowercase N-format task id plus nonnegative PlanStep.Index; the current task id is supplied by Runtime, never trusted from model text; resolver rejects another task id, an absent index, a step without a tool call and non-canonical ids; exactly one persisted tool-call step must match; digest step index i maps to ev1:<current-task-id>:i.

EvidenceRead/v1 is one JSON object with exactly five case-sensitive keys (runtime, evidenceId, source result|observation, integer offset, integer length) in assistant text, never a provider tool call; fences or prose invalidate it; native/fallback adapters pass it to Runtime; a response mixing tool calls and an EvidenceRead claim is invalid; replan parsing recognizes a valid read first without spending the malformed-plan re-ask; in initial planning a valid read is audited NotAllowedInPhase and a malformed claim Malformed (null indexes), neither reads, both use the single corrective re-ask; claim detection is limited to a top-level runtime key.
column12: Subject to ADR-0052 evidence cleanup (see DOC-02-effective-rules E-EVID).

column5: source=result reads exactly persisted ToolCallResult.Output, source=observation exactly PlanStep.Observation; null source is UnavailableSource, empty is valid; offsets in UTF-16 units, length 1-4000, offset==length is EndOfEvidence, negative/past-end/surrogate-splitting is OutOfRange; errors disclose no contents; replies use fixed markers and existing escaping with at most 256 units overhead; fragment lives only in that logical call and is never copied into future history; each read request consumes one of four slots per step or replan call (provider retries and overflow recovery do not reset); a fifth attempt performs no read, audits LimitExceeded once and terminates the task Failed/RuntimeFailure with a bounded synthetic non-tool failure step.
column12: The fifth-read RuntimeFailure termination is amended by ADR-0052 (D-048): exhausting the local read budget no longer terminates the task.

column5: One metadata-only EvidenceReadAuditEvent per attempted read (TaskId, nullable StepIndex/PlanRevision, bounded EvidenceId, Source, Offset, RequestedLength, ReturnedLength=0 on rejection, closed ResultCode Success|EndOfEvidence|Malformed|InvalidId|CrossTaskRejected|MissingStep|UnavailableSource|OutOfRange|LimitExceeded|NotAllowedInPhase|AttemptBudgetInterrupted) audited once before continuation or termination, never containing retrieved evidence.

The limitations digest builds from persisted steps only, never compact records or retrieval turns; compaction is not a limitation; Observation and Result.Output are never rewritten so the shortening predicate stays meaningful; the evidence rule and step digest remain on every call including continuations; reading a range never erases a partial/shortened limitation; digest is a fixed prompt cost (rule 2,000 chars, digest 4,608).

New tool-call steps persist a nullable PlanStep.VerificationStatus populated directly from the runtime verification outcome (null = absent/unknown, legacy rows included); it is never parsed from Observation text; Observation suffix is never rewritten.

ReplanAsync receives the goal, the current plan revision only (deterministic projection of at most 2,048 characters), bounded history and the directly triggering step verbatim even at K=0; no earlier plan revisions or rationale history.
column12: History composition is now owned by the MAF context layer (ADR-0052); the plan projection and triggering-step rule remain.

column5: ContextOverflow is never retried with the same request; at the Runtime caller boundary the first overflow rebuilds aggressively and retries exactly once only when compactable history exists (never for initial plan or a call without compactable history), goal and plan projections capped at 2,048/1,024 units by deterministic head/tail, both attempts keep ADR-0039 records, a second overflow terminates with the classified reason, provider retries never multiply this retry, the rest of that logical call stays aggressive.
column12: Mechanism now MAF-based after AF-05; the one-retry invariant and prompt caps remain per the 109-117 status note.

column5: Agent:MaxTotalTokens=350000 is a finite emergency ceiling (nullable explicit opt-out, validated positive, no clamping); known prompt+completion usage of every model attempt (failed, retried, planning, steps, replans, disclosure asks, EvidenceRead continuations, overflow retries) counts cumulatively across resumes; exhaustion is strictly TokensUsed > MaxTotalTokens; absent usage stays null so TokensUsed is a lower bound, never an estimate.

A planning, replanning or non-final response that crosses the cap persists exactly one synthetic non-tool PlanStep carrying the crossing call's ModelCalls (excluded from evidence resolution, from the limitations digest and from final-marker matching), executes no proposed tool and ends BudgetExceeded/TokenBudget; an original final answer is the ADR-0042 exception and completes normally even if it crosses the cap, and an admitted disclosure re-ask keeps all its ModelCalls on the final step.
column12: Disclosure re-ask was replaced by deterministic append (AF-05H, ADR-0042); the final-answer exception remains.

column5: Agent:MaxAttemptDuration=01:00:00 nullable (non-null positive, at most 24 h), VerbatimHistorySteps validated 0-15; TimeProvider-based active time starting at attempt admission, paused immediately before awaiting human approval and resumed after the decision; model calls, planning, EvidenceRead processing, retry waits and tool execution consume it; a dedicated attempt-budget cancellation signal distinct from caller cancellation and provider/tool timeouts stops in-flight work, persists the interruption record and ends BudgetExceeded/AttemptDurationBudget without retry or replan.
column12: VerbatimHistorySteps no longer exists (removed by AF-05).

column5: Test and review obligations for the HARDEN-8 acceptance (40-step run across two resumes, history bound 17,212 units, sentinel retrieval beyond 4,000, fifth-read limit, overflow cases, duration interruption, budget-crossing cases).
column12: Acceptance-test specification for a completed packet; the properties it verified are carried by C04:evidence-read, C03:budgets and C01:overflow-recovery.

column5: Accepted.
column12: Metadata.

column5: V0.1/V0.2 hardcoded refusal above Read and an unchained audit sink; V0.3 replaces them (D-008 hash-chaining, D-011 analyzer escalation).
column12: Rationale only.

column5: PolicyEngine (bOps.Policy) evaluates a PolicyContext against a PolicyConfig (defaults per RiskLevel, per-tool overrides, per-package risk ceilings), never names a tool or package in code (A1; identifiers come from PolicyConfig data), and checks RiskLevel.Critical first and unconditionally before any config lookup so no override, default or ceiling can yield anything but Forbidden for it.

PolicyConfigLoader parses policy.yaml (YamlDotNet is a bOps.Policy dependency, never Abstractions) and REJECTS with PolicyConfigurationException a document assigning defaults.critical anything but forbidden; built-ins distinguish two failure modes: SafeDefault (Read/Low automatic, Medium/High approval, Critical forbidden) only when no policy.yaml exists, and AllForbidden (everything forbidden) when a file exists but failed to load, so a broken policy never falls back to something more permissive.
AgentRunner.ExecuteStepAsync calls policyEngine.Evaluate; PackageTrustLevel was hardcoded Official because all packages were first-party (known simplification until dynamic loading).
column12: Superseded: PackageTrustLevel is host-assigned and inherited from the verified publisher key for dynamic packages (B7, ADR-0020); carried by C02:trust-level.

column5: ConsoleApprovalProvider (CLI) prints tool, risk, reason, arguments and what will be verified, then blocks on a y/N prompt plus optional note; IApprovalProvider is an interface so API/UI hosts implement a queue without AgentRunner or PolicyEngine changing; ApprovalAuditEvent (Package, Tool, Approved, Approver, Note) is distinct from PolicyDecisionAuditEvent and records who decided; a rejected approval ends the step like a denial with Authorization=UserRejected and counts as a deviation that triggers a replan.

JsonLinesAuditSink writes each event in an AuditChainEnvelope {Seq, PrevHash, Hash, EventJson} with Hash = SHA256(PrevHash + EventJson) and EventJson stored as an exact JSON STRING (re-serialized nodes are not byte-stable); the sink reads the last line at construction to continue the chain and throws if it is not a well-formed envelope (a pre-chain or truncated file is refused, never silently adopted); AuditChainVerifier re-derives every hash and prevHash continuity and reports the broken Seq; the guarantee is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof, and must be described that way.
Directory.Build.props moves AnalysisLevel to latest-all; findings were fixed not suppressed; one documented solution-wide suppression CA2007 (ConfigureAwait).
column12: Engineering/build rule owned by 02-coding-standards (level B), not an architecture contract.

column5: Rejected: a per-package trust table populated now; a nested JSON object in the envelope (non-lossless round trip causes verifier false positives); silently adopting the last line of an unverified audit file; replan on plain Failure; a CLI audit-verify subcommand deferred.

Every non-Read call goes through policy; pre-chain audit.jsonl cannot be continued and must be moved aside; bOps.Policy depends only on bOps.Abstractions (A7) and bOps.Runtime depends only on IPolicyEngine/IApprovalProvider, never referencing bOps.Policy, keeping the engine swappable at the composition root.
Flagged gaps at V0.3 (model-call kind in audit, no CLI audit verifier, six backfill ADRs unwritten).
column12: Point-in-time gap list; ADRs 0001/0002/0005/0006/0011/0012 now exist.

column5: Accepted.
column12: Metadata.

column5: B3/D-006 enforce a VerificationSpec at registration, but V0.1-V0.3 never ran it; principle 3 was structural but not yet real.
column12: Rationale only.

column5: After every EXECUTED non-Read tool call (outcome Success, Failure or Timeout) the runtime calls the declared VerificationSpec; it does not run for a call never executed (policy denial, operator rejection, argument-validation failure), where Verification stays null; it runs on Failure and Timeout because a timed-out or partially failed side effect may have partially happened (S7) and the evaluator compares observed state with the original arguments, never the original result.

The runtime resolves VerifyToolName in the same IToolRegistry, carries over only the ArgumentsFrom names, validates against the verification tool manifest (S2), executes through the same per-tool-timeout path (a throw becomes Failure) and hands whatever ToolCallResult results - including one the runtime manufactured because the verifier did not resolve or failed validation - to IVerifiableTool.EvaluateVerificationAsync; this is the only place "could not verify" becomes Inconclusive, the runtime never invents a fallback and never assigns NotApplicable itself; an exception in EvaluateVerificationAsync yields Inconclusive with the message, never Confirmed; the verification call is runtime-mandated infrastructure that is NOT routed through IPolicyEngine/IApprovalProvider and is never seen or requested by the model.
column12: Narrowed by ADR-0031 (verification stays inside the delegated envelope) and ADR-0036 (entitlement applies; Inconclusive without invoking the evaluator when authorization prevents invoking verification).

column5: ToolCallAuditEvent.Verification carries the status for every executed non-Read call; the observation fed to the model gets an explicit "Verification: {status}" line (with Detail) after the tool output; Refuted joins the replan deviation set and triggers a replan; Inconclusive and NotApplicable do not trigger a replan and are never treated as success (information for the model).
A bops.verification child activity tagged with original tool, verification tool, its outcome and final status; no new metric instrument.

Rejected: verifying only on Success; the runtime deciding NotApplicable for an unresolvable verifier (that is Inconclusive); replanning on Inconclusive; a separate VerificationOutcomeAuditEvent (Verification is a field of the call event); recording the verification call as its own ToolCallAuditEvent (it was never proposed by the model or subject to policy and would be indistinguishable from an agent action).
Package IVerifiableTool.EvaluateVerificationAsync must tolerate a verification result it did not expect (Failure from an unresolvable verifier or unresolved ArgumentsFrom); no Abstractions change.
Flagged gaps at V0.4 (model-call kind in audit, no audit-verify command, six backfill ADRs unwritten).
column12: Point-in-time gap list.

column5: Accepted 2026-09-15; amended by ADR-0040 (execution attempts, ordered resumability table, atomic transition before resume, fencing, per-attempt vs lifetime budgets, cumulative tokens, zero-plan replanning, lifecycle audit); extended by ADR-0051 (second table in tasks.db, ITaskStore and the TaskState row unchanged).
Task state lived only in locals, so a killed process lost it; EF Core was rejected for a single-aggregate store; the ADR is required because it adds a contract and a core dependency.
column12: Rationale only.

column5: ITaskStore (SaveAsync, LoadAsync, ListByStatusAsync) is declared in dependency-free bOps.Abstractions; bOps.Memory provides SqliteTaskStore over Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, one table with TaskState serialized whole as a JSON column via System.Text.Json source generation; no EF Core.

AgentRunner takes ITaskStore as a required dependency; it saves the task Running after the initial plan and after every step so a crash leaves the last COMPLETED step durable, never a half-written one, and saves the final TaskState at a terminal status.

ResumeAsync rebuilds the conversation history from task.Steps (each step re-wrapped exactly as RunAsync would) and the current plan from Plans[^1], then continues the same loop from the next step index - not a separate loop implementation.
column12: Resumability conditions superseded by the ADR-0040 state machine; history rebuild now deterministic from persisted state (C01:context).

column5: bops resume <task-id> is the first CLI subcommand; bops "<goal>" is unchanged.
column12: CLI usage is operator documentation, not a structural rule.

column5: Rejected: EF Core; a JSON-lines task file (audit is append-only, a task row is mutated each step); ITaskStore inside bOps.Memory (Runtime must not depend on Memory, same reasoning as IAuditSink); an optional no-op ITaskStore (a null-checked shim is forbidden).

bOps.Memory is a core project with Microsoft.Data.Sqlite outside Abstractions; every host wires a real store; a resumed history is an approximation (literal model-call objects were not persisted; later superseded by ModelCallRecord, ADR-0039); bOps.Memory is a fourth core assembly scanned by the A1 architecture test and must contain no package/tool/provider literals.

Accepted 2026-09-15; amended by ADR-0040 (resume 202 only after the atomic transition and launcher admission, 409/501/503 bodies, task view fields executionAttempt/accounting/origin/terminalReason/executing/resumable/resumeBlockedReason, /events on status or attempt change), ADR-0043 (authentication only: browser session, cookie, Bearer precedence, CSRF gate) and ADR-0044 (delegation readiness, skills endpoint, duplicate-key rejection, typed 400 codes, typed limitation fields).

V0.9 is a SECOND CLIENT of the same local single-node runtime (principle 6), not multi-agent supervision or remote transport; the API must serve concurrent clients, return before a task finishes and accept approval decisions from a different request.

bOps.Api is a thin ASP.NET Core Minimal API host wiring the same core components as bOps.Cli (AgentRunner, IToolRegistry, IPolicyEngine, IAuditSink, ITaskStore, providers) and adding only what an HTTP channel needs; hosts contain no logic.

MVP endpoints: POST /api/agents/tasks (202 with task id, never blocks), POST .../{id}/resume, GET .../{id}, GET .../{id}/events (SSE), GET tasks?status=, GET /api/approvals/pending, POST /api/approvals/{id}/respond, GET /api/tools.
column12: V0.9 MVP surface; the current surface is defined by the bOps.Api endpoints and their tests and has grown through later ADRs; the structural properties (202 Accepted, never block on task completion) are carried by C05:api-background-tasks.

column5: A task runs as a detached background operation, not inside the starting request; AgentRunner has no mutable instance state (a singleton serves concurrent requests); progress is observed through ITaskStore, which is updated after every step - the events endpoint polls the store rather than requiring a new event-bus abstraction.
column12: The launcher's containment backstop is added by ADR-0039 (C01:call-containment) and admission by ADR-0040 (C03:resume).

column5: Approvals cross the request boundary through a host-local ApiApprovalProvider : IApprovalProvider (in bOps.Api, like ConsoleApprovalProvider in the CLI): it stores (manifest, reason, TaskCompletionSource<ApprovalDecision>) in memory, awaits it with the call's cancellation, and a different request completes it; pending approvals are NOT persisted - a restart loses them while the Running task stays resumable.
This version has no authentication or authorization, assumed behind a trusted network or operator reverse proxy; real auth deferred to the V1.0 hardening line.
column12: Superseded: authentication exists (API credentials and browser session, ADR-0043; C05:api-auth). The "anyone who can reach the port can approve" statement is expired.

A plugin ships bops-plugin.json deserialized into PluginManifest (SchemaVersion, Id, Publisher, Version, MinHostAbstractionsVersion, EntryAssembly, EntryType, DeclaredCapabilities, Dependencies, MaxDeclaredRisk); a shape in Abstractions, never an instance; SchemaVersion is checked against a supported set so a future breaking manifest fails loudly; DeclaredCapabilities, Dependencies and MaxDeclaredRisk are informational only, to let an operator read what a plugin claims, never to configure policy.

One collectible PluginLoadContext per plugin resolves the plugin's own dependencies from its folder, and deliberately returns null for bOps.Abstractions so the CLR falls through to the single copy already in the default context: a plugin can never have its own second incompatible copy of the contract types.

Install copies into staging, validates there, then moves into place only after validation (an interrupted or rejected install leaves nothing), rejects an Id collision (the host arbitrates identity) and records the plugin DISABLED; Enable loads EntryType into a fresh load context, constructs it with ActivatorUtilities against a RestrictedPackageServiceProvider exposing exactly the A10 list (not the host IServiceProvider) and registers its tools or model-provider factory in the SAME registries the host uses (no parallel registry), rejecting an entry type implementing neither or both interfaces before anything is registered; Disable calls SetEnabled(package,false) and unloads the collectible context; Remove disables first, then deletes folder and record, so a partial failure leaves disabled-but-present never deleted-but-registered.

column5: Linux shells out to systemctl via ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList, never UseShellExecute or a composed command string (the OS exec receives argv, no shell interprets metacharacters); exactly two fixed invocation shapes exist (list-units --type=service --all --no-legend --no-pager --plain, and show <name> --property=LoadState,ActiveState,SubState,Description --no-pager), the model supplies at most the one validated name argument and can never reach another subcommand, flag or binary; output is parsed from --property Key=Value lines, never human-formatted status text; an implausible unit name never reaches systemctl and is reported as not found.

In-flight approvals are deliberately not restored after a crash: a resumed task requests a NEW approval from a currently authenticated approver, because persisting a decision would turn a point-in-time human decision into a reusable bearer capability.

column5: ToolParameter gains additive init-only constraints (numeric Minimum/Maximum, string/path MinLength/MaxLength, PathList MinItems/MaxItems) without changing its positional constructor; registry validation rejects inconsistent or inapplicable constraints; the runtime enforces every declared constraint BEFORE policy, approval or execution, reports the specific violation and never clamps; every provider schema projects the same constraints, enum values and additionalProperties:false from the manifest, the manifest being the sole constraint source (package-local validation is defence in depth).

ToolCallResult gains additive init-only FailureKind and Completeness (Unspecified defaults): runtime-owned failures are classified structurally, packages may report environmental failure and complete/partial/unavailable evidence, and the runtime propagates the typed values to the step and audit without parsing package JSON; additions are binary/source compatible and round-trip.

Rejected: constraints as constructor parameters (breaks compiled plugins); inferring bounds or completeness by parsing descriptions or package JSON in the runtime (core stays package-agnostic); clamping invalid arguments (hides the requested operation from policy and the model). Validation, authorization, timeout, internal and environmental failures stay distinguishable from successful-but-partial evidence; existing manifests and plugin binaries load unchanged.

column5: A layer above the single ITool call is needed: Capabilities (preconditions, input shape, rollback) before any call; an observation vs inference distinction that survives; authorization of a whole sequence as one unit with a guarantee that what was approved is exactly what runs; this ADR settles vocabulary and immutable data contracts, not Skill execution.

column5: Five terms: Package (deployment unit, host-assigned PackageId, A11), Tool (the runtime's only unit of execution, ITool/ToolManifest), Capability (named versioned operator-facing operation realized by an ExecutionPlan of typed Tool calls, never free commands), Skill (a package that contributes Capabilities plus deterministic domain logic) and Agent (orchestration role with reduced privilege, V1.2); a Capability is not a bigger Tool and the single-tool call path through policy/approval/verification/audit is unchanged.

A Skill's capability selection and evidence gathering is ordinary package code, deterministic, NOT a second LLM call, with the same trust model as a Tool implementation; the model still never touches the machine.

EvidenceKind {Fact, Inference, Recommendation, ExecutedAction, Verification} and Evidence(Id, Kind, Description, Data, SourceTool, ObservedAtUtc): an Inference or Recommendation is explicitly not a Fact; Finding.EvidenceIds cannot be empty, enforced by the constructor throwing (the invariant belongs on the type; citing evidence never recorded is checked later at report validation); Evidence.Data reuses the Sensitive-parameter redaction path, redacted by whoever assembles it before construction (S6).

ExecutionPlan(CapabilityName, CapabilityVersion, Rationale, Steps) is the authorizable artifact distinct from AgentPlan/PlannedStep (the model's revisable intention): non-empty steps with contiguous indexes 0..N-1, immutable; ExecutionPlanHasher computes SHA-256 over canonical JSON.

The hash is over a canonical form (every JSON object's properties recursively sorted by ordinal key), never default serializer order; it is computed on demand and never cached on the record (record 'with' would invalidate a stored hash); ExecutionPlanApproval binds a PlanHash to an ApprovalDecision and before execution the runtime recomputes the hash and compares: a mismatch means the plan changed and a fresh approval is required (hash equality, not a heuristic diff).
SkillReport(Evidence, Findings, Plan?) is data assembled from what was actually recorded, never free model narrative; there is no unstructured-narrative field.

PolicyContext gains optional init-only SkillId, CapabilityName, Target, Environment and BlastRadius {Single, Multiple, Fleet} (a magnitude, never a count or a named resource, keeping A1); defaults absent for plain tool calls; Critical stays unconditionally Forbidden regardless of these fields; rule evaluation over them was deferred (ADR-0025).
ICapability/ISkillProvider execution interfaces, runtime orchestration, policy rule evaluation over the new fields and a sample Skill were deferred (CapabilityManifest declared only).

column5: Executable package boundary preserving four invariants: a package cannot impersonate another; evidence collection calls only Read-risk tools owned by the same package; every such call crosses validation, policy, timeout and audit; approval applies to the exact immutable plan.

Additive Abstractions: CapabilityRequest (typed input, target, environment, blast radius, dry-run), ICapability (one CapabilityManifest; prepares a SkillReport), ISkillProvider : IToolProvider (stable Skill id, deterministic Capabilities, package tools; may not also be a model provider) and IToolInvoker (tool name + ToolArguments -> ToolCallResult); an ICapability receives IToolInvoker as an invocation-scoped argument and never IToolRegistry, IServiceProvider, policy, audit, approval or another package's services; package identity is bound by the host when it creates the invoker, so package code has no value to forge.

Node-scoped ISkillRegistry stamps the host-assigned PackageId on every Capability manifest, rejects blank or duplicate Skill/Capability identities and duplicate object identities, keeps ordinal order; dynamic activation accepts an ISkillProvider only after signature and publisher trust checks, declared Capability names must exactly match the plugin manifest; disable/unload unregisters both tools and Skills before releasing the load context.

AgentRunner.PrepareSkillAsync resolves provider and Capability, creates the bound IToolInvoker and runs package code under the Capability timeout; every invoker call resolves through the node's real registry, rejects a missing, disabled, platform-incompatible, cross-package or non-Read tool, runs through argument validation, contextual policy, timeout and audit and returns a bounded ToolCallResult; the prepared report is validated before leaving the runtime (unique evidence/finding ids, every Finding cites recorded Evidence, plan matches Capability name/version, a plan step whose risk exceeds the Capability manifest is rejected). ExecutePreparedSkillAsync re-resolves the Skill, revalidates, requires an approved ExecutionPlanApproval with the exact hash for every non-Read Capability and executes through the ADR-0024 pipeline; Capability approval never waives per-step policy, approval or verification.

policy.yaml gains an optional skills sequence whose rules name an exact Skill, Capability, target, environment, blast radius and mode; a Skill-originated call with missing context, no exact matching rule or multiple exact matches is Forbidden; Critical stays unconditionally Forbidden and package ceilings apply before contextual rules; exact matching is deliberate (wildcards would add a second pattern language at an authorization boundary).

Skill preparation and execution emit SkillRunAuditEvent correlated by task id and run id; contextual tool and policy events carry Skill id, Capability name, target, environment, blast radius and plan hash when present; no evidence data or tool output in telemetry.

Capability exceptions become a failed audited Skill report, expected tool failures stay ToolCallResult values, caller cancellation propagates and the Capability timeout is a hard bound over preparation; V1.1 Skill runs are terminal and non-resumable (not written to ITaskStore, no Skill resume API) - interruption means a new run, plan and approval; durable Skill-run state needs a future ADR.

Rejected: giving Skills IToolRegistry; a process-wide IToolInvoker in constructors (context would be lost or forgeable); prepare-and-run in one call (no immutable plan to approve); persisting only a plan index (does not prove which effects happened).

SDK additive and dependency-free; node-scoped Skill registry; SafeDefault contains no contextual Skill grants so Skill calls fail closed until an exact Skill policy rule exists; V1.1 proves the boundary with one signed dynamically loaded sample Skill and claims no crash resumability.

column5: A directory tree can be huge, mutate during traversal and contain inaccessible paths/symlinks; the complete list must not travel in tool output (bounded-output and telemetry rules) nor live in process memory; the exact inventory is durable runtime state scoped by node, actor and task; model-supplied arguments must not nominate that scope and ITool.ExecuteAsync must not break.

ToolExecutionContext(Node, TaskId, Actor) and optional IContextualTool : ITool; the runtime invokes the contextual overload when a tool implements it; the legacy ExecuteAsync stays mandatory and a contextual tool fails closed there when its operation requires host-owned context; AgentRunner builds the context from the same host-owned values written to audit events - neither a model nor a package may supply or replace them; verification and restricted Skill evidence calls preserve the original task and actor context.

fs.size stays Read (derived inventory bookkeeping is not mutation of the target); inputs are one path, max depth, max entries, top-N, max collection duration and an exact-inventory flag with host defaults and hard ceilings (out-of-range requests fail, never coerced); traversal is iterative, never follows symlinks/reparse points, resolves and checks the read policy immediately before reading metadata or children; counts include the root; a top-N accumulator retains only N largest files; warnings and response bytes are bounded; limit exhaustion, policy denial, inaccessible entries, overflow, cancellation or detected mutation make the result partial, never complete or approval-ready, and never return an exact manifest reference.

Exact entries are inserted incrementally into a package-owned SQLite store (WAL, busy timeout, restrictive Unix permissions, parameterized SQL); a manifest is building, becomes ready only after complete enumeration and final validation, otherwise incomplete; expired and abandoned building rows are cleaned up; manifest ids carry 128 bits from a cryptographically secure GUID and are opaque; every row is scoped to host-supplied node, actor kind/id and task id, and paging or deletion APIs must match the complete scope (an id alone is not authorization); entries use normalized root-relative paths with type, length, timestamps, attributes and link target, detecting ordinary staleness without hashing contents; an inventory is evidence, not a filesystem lock, and the deleter must re-resolve under S11 and compare metadata immediately before deletion.

Entries are read in ordinal relative-path order and hashed through a length-prefixed canonical binary encoding covering canonical root, traversal semantics and every entry but excluding random id, creation/expiry and scope (an unchanged tree repeats the content hash); the approval hash will wrap it; the tool result carries only bounded counts, totals, top entries, warnings, completion state, elapsed time and (ready exact inventory only) id, content hash and expiry - exact entries never enter normal tool output, model context, telemetry or a single audit event.

Rejected: node/actor/task parameters on fs.size (forgeable); breaking ITool.ExecuteAsync (frozen SDK); ambient static/AsyncLocal context; a JSON-lines manifest file; in-memory entries written once (memory scales with target, a crash loses the preflight); hashing every file's contents.

Filesystem package takes a direct Microsoft.Data.Sqlite dependency (not on bOps.Memory); hosts configure store path, retention, defaults and ceilings and keep the DB outside read/write target patterns; runtime tests cover contextual dispatch and filesystem tests use real directories on Windows and Linux; paging/authorization endpoints and destructive reconciliation belong to the deletion ADR.

column5: Path-based approval is insufficient (trees change after preview, overlapping batches duplicate entries, multi-entry delete is not atomic); RiskLevel.High alone cannot express "approval for every execution" because policy may make another High tool automatic, and the invariant must hold without naming a filesystem tool in the runtime.

ToolManifest.RequiresExplicitApproval (default false): after ordinary policy evaluation an Automatic decision for such a manifest becomes an approval decision; Forbidden stays forbidden; a manifest may tighten but never loosen policy; the effective decision and its reason are audited.

Optional IApprovalBoundTool: after a human answers and before target execution the runtime gives the tool the host-owned ToolExecutionContext and the exact ApprovalDecision; the callback may update only approval/preflight bookkeeping and validate that the approved arguments still identify a consumable object; a failed approved binding prevents execution; a rejected decision is audited and never calls ExecuteAsync.

ToolParameterType.PathList is a JSON array of path strings exposed to providers as array of strings; runtime validation rejects non-arrays, non-string members, unknown arguments and other type mismatches before approval or execution (no delimiter grammar or embedded JSON in a string).

Read-only fs.delete_tree.prepare builds a DeletionManifest through the inventory service from a bounded path list (the API exposes the same service); fs.delete_tree accepts ONLY manifestId and approvalHash - never a root path, glob or recursive flag; roots with glob metacharacters are rejected, fully resolved under S11, required to satisfy both read and write policy, deduplicated by platform comparison, sorted and reduced so descendants of a selected root are not enumerated or deleted twice, with the reduced canonical root list shown as a warning-bearing preview; the manifest has a cryptographically random opaque id scoped to node, task and preparing actor; the SHA-256 approval hash (length-prefixed binary) covers schema and permanent-delete semantics (no-follow-links, children-first), id, node, task, owner, creation/expiry, every canonical root, counts and bytes, and every canonical absolute entry path with type, size, timestamps, attributes and link target.

column2: Decision: bounded summaries and audit summary
column5: The approval hash is instance-specific (random id and scope), unlike the repeatable content hash; the full list stays in SQLite; tool output and pending-approval DTOs carry only bounded summaries, id, approval hash, counts and bytes; an optional host-bounded IToolAuditSummaryProvider adds those aggregates to ToolCallAuditEvent without copying arbitrary output or paths, and the runtime drops summaries over 8 KiB.

Defaults 10,000 entries, 32 roots, depth 32, 30 s build, 10-minute approval window; hard ceilings 100,000 entries, 64 roots, depth 128, two minutes; operators may only lower them; exceeding a ceiling, incomplete enumeration, inaccessible metadata, overflow, cancellation or detected mutation yields rejected or incomplete state and no approval-ready manifest; expiry is checked when approval is bound and again when execution begins but never interrupts an execution that already entered executing; terminal summaries retained seven days (configurable); unconsumed manifests expire at the approval deadline.
column12: The fail-closed rule is carried by C02:deletion-manifest; default and ceiling values are operator-facing configuration documented in the guide.

column5: Durable states building, ready, approved, executing, partially_completed, verified, refuted, inconclusive, expired, rejected; building->ready only after complete inventory and canonical hashing; ready->approved is an atomic compare-and-set in the approval-binding callback after an affirmative decision whose manifestId and approvalHash match; a rejection records ready->rejected; approved->executing is another atomic CAS making the manifest one-shot and rejecting duplicate approval or execution; execution ends executing (all deletes succeeded, awaiting verification) or partially_completed (interruption, drift or OS failure after any completed delete); verification moves either to verified/refuted/inconclusive; an approved binding stale before target execution is rejected with zero deletions; approvals are never persisted as reusable bearer capabilities across restart.

Before the first delete the executor reconciles completely against the stored set, including unapproved children; any missing, added, replaced, renamed, retyped or metadata-changed entry fails closed with ZERO deletions; immediately before each destructive call it resolves and rechecks policy plus identity metadata; symlinks/reparse points are entries, never traversal edges; entries are processed deepest-first with ordinal tie-break, files/links without following links, directories non-recursively after approved children (directory last-write and Linux creation/inode-change time are checked only in the initial reconciliation, since approved child removal legitimately changes them; resolution, type, attributes and link state are rechecked before the directory operation); every attempted entry gets one bounded durable result; cancellation propagates after recording reconciliation and is never described as rollback; the contextual read-only fs.delete_tree.verify classifies each entry (absence confirms, present matching = remaining, present non-matching = recreated-or-changed, inaccessible = permission-denied/inconclusive): only universal absence is Verified, any known presence Refuted, an unobservable path makes the result Inconclusive unless a refutation exists.

Operator endpoints create/browse manifests only with the exact node/task/owner scope; approval preview endpoints are addressed through a live pending approval id, require the Approver role and derive scope from that request (a manifest or task id alone is insufficient); cursors are opaque ordinals bounded by server page-size limits and re-authorized on every request; search is server-side; download streams JSON Lines without buffering; an affirmative API response for fs.delete_tree requires a separate acknowledgePermanentDeletion boolean; the Angular client shows roots, counts, bytes, hash, expiry and warnings, pages and filters entries, never renders the whole list as one DOM collection and disables approval on expiry, hash mismatch or non-ready state.

Rejected: a recursive flag on fs.delete; relying on High-risk policy defaults (mandatory approval is an invariant, not configuration); approving roots and enumerating at execution; all paths in approval/model/audit payloads; delimited or JSON-in-string roots; recursive OS deletion (could consume unapproved entries); promising rollback or atomicity.

Additive SDK surface; tools that opt into the flag become strictly safer while core code still names no concrete tool; the Filesystem package owns manifest/result tables in its own SQLite database independent of bOps.Memory; destructive decisions remain server-side; attack tests (symlink/parent replacement, rename, added/removed entries, altered hash, expiry, scope reuse, duplicate consumption) run on real temporary trees.

column5: web.search/web.fetch are the first tools reaching destinations the operator did not enumerate in advance; the URL is adversarial input like a container log line (S5); Read classification exempts a tool only from approval and IVerifiableTool, not from S5/S6/S10; the managed risks are SSRF, DNS rebinding, decompression bombs and unbounded memory; no SDK change needed (RiskLevel.Read, ToolManifest.Requires).

column2: Decision: two tools two trust boundaries
column5: web.search calls exactly one address, Web:Search:BaseUrl, operator configuration read at startup and never model-influenced (same trust as ModelProvider:BaseUrl or Docker:Endpoint), therefore not routed through the SSRF path but still size/timeout bounded; it requests format=json and never scrapes HTML (a non-JSON reply is an actionable structured failure); web.fetch accepts a model-chosen, adversarial URL and is governed by the SSRF/redirect/decoding rules.

web.fetch uses one SocketsHttpHandler per package instance with AllowAutoRedirect=false, UseCookies=false, Credentials=null, AutomaticDecompression=None and a custom ConnectCallback that on every new connection resolves the host through IDnsResolver, validates EVERY returned address against IpAddressPolicy (by default denying loopback, link-local incl. the 169.254.169.254 metadata address, RFC 1918, IPv6 unique-local fc00::/7, multicast, unspecified and IPv4-mapped IPv6 wrapping any denied address), connects a raw Socket to the first surviving address or fails with an actionable "destination denied by network policy", and returns a NetworkStream (TLS is layered by the handler using the original hostname for SNI/validation, so certificate checking is unaffected); the only override is an explicit narrow operator allowlist (Web:Fetch:AllowedHosts/AllowedNetworks) checked before the deny rules; because the callback re-validates on every new connection and a redirect to another scheme/host/port is a new connection, the validated address is the connected address atomically (no check-then-connect window).

Redirects are an explicit loop in WebFetchService capped by Web:Fetch:MaxRedirects (default 5, ceiling 10); an https->http downgrade is rejected by default; exceeding the cap or a rejected downgrade ends the fetch with a bounded diagnostic, never a partial silent success.

Automatic decompression is off so a byte budget applies to the DECOMPRESSED stream: supported Content-Encoding (gzip, deflate, br) is wrapped in a counting stream that aborts past Web:Fetch:MaxDecompressedBytes, the raw stream is independently capped at Web:Fetch:MaxResponseBytes, and abort yields a truncated result, never unbounded allocation or an unhandled exception.

Only a fixed textual allowlist is decoded (text/plain, text/html, text/markdown, application/json, application/xml, text/xml, text/csv; operator-narrowable, never wider without explicit configuration); anything else returns content-type, byte length and a bounded diagnostic, never raw bytes; charset is limited to utf-8, us-ascii, iso-8859-1 from the Content-Type header, anything else decodes as UTF-8 (an attacker-controlled charset declaration is not trusted beyond selecting among those).

Both tools return requested URL, final URL, HTTP status, content type/encoding, retrieval timestamp, a truncated flag and the bounded text body - never raw headers or cookies; the text is untrusted external data returned as ordinary tool output under the existing S5 delimiter/neutralization boundary, with no additional prompt-injection transformation.

web.search declares Requires ["web.searxng"], satisfied by a local synchronous check that Web:Search:BaseUrl is a well-formed absolute http/https URI (not a live probe), so an unconfigured instance means the tool is absent from the model's view; web.fetch has Requires [] and is always available where the package loads.

IDnsResolver is injected into the package HttpClient so tests can map hostnames to attacker-chosen addresses; a local HttpListener supplies redirect chains and oversized/compressed bodies; default-deny and allowlist paths are separate assertions.
