column5: Rejected: validating the resolved address once before SendAsync (the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU window); inspecting the final URI after automatic redirects (detection is not prevention); hostname blocklists (bypassed by any name resolving into a denied range); automatic decompression with only a final text cap (decompression bomb); returning raw bytes for any content type; a request-body/header/credential passthrough (one step from an SSRF credential relay).

Web is a first-party package following A8 with no Web identity in Runtime, Policy, Memory or Audit; web.fetch cannot complete a connection to loopback, link-local, private, unique-local, multicast or unspecified addresses unless explicitly allowlisted, including via redirect or changing DNS answers; a hostile instance, bomb or slow response degrades to a bounded failure inside the S7 timeout; output remains S5 data; attack tests (redirect-to-loopback/private/metadata, DNS rebinding via swapped resolver answer, oversized body, decompression bomb, invalid charset, slow stream, excess redirects, scheme downgrade) run against a real local HttpListener, not only recorded fixtures.
Accepted 2026-09-17.
column12: Metadata.

column5: ADR-0045 supersedes only this ADR's restart-to-apply consequence (execution-pinned live Settings and approved-in-principle fallback chain); every model attempt resolves the current credential for its pinned provider through this ADR's secret authority; no historical credentials are preserved; ModelProvider:ApiKeySecret is bound only to the merged ModelProvider:Provider value (before Settings selection) and never applied to another provider (Settings-selected, fallback or resumed); the vault, masking, master-key, provider-profile and environment-precedence decisions otherwise remain in force.

UI-written provider keys need durable storage beyond environment variables; D-017 settles the shape; "provider selection" cannot be just an id because every provider package needs an operator-supplied BaseUrl (otherwise a new provider's key points at the wrong endpoint) so provider configuration is fully UI-managed; no AEAD/KDF existed before so the vault lives in bOps.Runtime beside EnvironmentSecretProvider (Abstractions stays dependency-free); there was no Administrator role (viewer/operator/approver only) and writing credentials needs one.

One versioned JSON vault file (Vault:FilePath, default vault.dat) {SchemaVersion, Version, Entries[providerId]: nonce, ciphertext, tag, Created/Updated, MaskPrefix/MaskSuffix/MaskedLength, PlaintextLength}; each entry is encrypted independently with AES-256-GCM (BCL AesGcm, no custom cipher), a fresh random 96-bit nonce on EVERY write of that entry, and additional authenticated data UTF8("{SchemaVersion}:{providerId}") so ciphertexts cannot be relabeled or swapped between provider ids without tag failure.

The master key is supplied externally through SecretReference/ISecretProvider (Vault:MasterKeySecret, default environment variable BOPS_VAULT_MASTER_KEY) and is fed to HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869, BCL; fixed non-secret salt/info) to derive the 32-byte AES key; startup is fail-closed: a resolved value shorter than 20 characters is rejected, and a configured-but-unresolvable key (e.g. unset variable) makes the host REFUSE to start (a silently disabled vault would make UI-written secrets appear protected); when Vault:MasterKeySecret is absent the vault is simply inactive (no VaultSecretProvider, Settings secret writes unavailable) and CLI-only deployments are unaffected.

Rotation is a CLI-only command (bops vault rotate-key, never on the API): decrypt all entries with the current key, read a new key from a second SecretReference, re-encrypt every entry with fresh nonces and atomically replace the file - the highest-privilege maintenance operation stays on the machine-access surface; corruption or tamper (invalid JSON, failing GCM tag, truncated nonce/tag, unknown SchemaVersion) is fail-closed with VaultCorruptedException/VaultDecryptionException, never dropping the entry or treating it as absent; backup is file-level and a copied vault file alone is inert because the master key is never stored beside it; a lost file means a fresh empty vault and re-entry of keys.

VaultStore writes to .tmp-{guid} then File.Move(overwrite) (atomic same-volume), on Linux restricts the file to UserRead|UserWrite; Windows gets no extra ACL hardening in this batch (documented known limitation); a SemaphoreSlim(1,1) serializes in-process writers and the root Version integer is the optimistic-concurrency token - every write requires expectedVersion to match disk or throws VaultConcurrencyException, mapped to HTTP 409 with current state.

API key: the existing ISecretProvider resolution of ModelProvider:ApiKeySecret is tried first and a non-empty result is an explicit operator override that wins outright; only when null/empty does the host fall back to VaultSecretProvider for the effective provider; active provider: the real environment variable ModelProvider__Provider (checked directly, since appsettings always has a value) wins outright over Settings, otherwise the Settings-stored provider beats the appsettings default; no previously-working environment-backed setup behaves differently. Changes applied on next restart.
column12: Restart-to-apply is superseded by ADR-0045 (live Settings for new executions, credential change at next model attempt); ApiKeySecret binding narrowed by ADR-0045.

column5: Each provider's non-secret configuration (BaseUrl, Model, SupportsNativeToolCalling, open ExtraParameters string map) is a ProviderProfile in the plain settings.json SettingsStore keyed by provider id, while the API key stays in the encrypted vault under the same id (the vault threat model never needs to cover non-secrets); if ModelProvider__Provider is a real environment variable the whole appsettings ModelProvider block is used and Settings is not consulted, otherwise each of BaseUrl/Model/SupportsNativeToolCalling comes from the stored profile with field-by-field fallback to appsettings so a partial profile never leaves the host without a default; ExtraParameters is stored and returned but deliberately not wired into ChatModelOptions/Create (no provider needs it, Abstractions is not extended speculatively).

Display mask is first six characters...last four for secrets of length >= 10; for length 1-9: revealed=min(length-1, floor(length*0.4)), prefix=ceil(revealed/2), suffix=revealed-prefix so prefix+suffix < length always; the mask is computed once from plaintext at write time and stored as non-secret metadata, never recomputed from a later decryption - rendering a mask never reads plaintext back out of the vault.

SettingsChangedAuditEvent (SettingName, Operation Set/Replace/Clear/SelectProvider, ProviderId, Outcome Success/Denied/Failure) records every Settings mutation and NEVER a value or a reversible fingerprint; because the event is outside any task it uses documented sentinels TaskId=Guid.Empty and StepIndex=-1 rather than relaxing the shared base type.

Rejected: OS-native credential store as only backend; storing the raw AES key; a per-entry master key; exposing rotation through the API (a compromised session must not gain the highest-privilege operation); an advisory file lock instead of an optimistic version token; re-reading plaintext to render the mask.

No new Abstractions type or dependency (vault is a new provider id alongside environment); the cryptographic surface (VaultCipher, VaultStore, VaultSecretProvider) must carry known-answer, round-trip, tamper, wrong-key and concurrency tests before endpoints depend on it; bOps.Api gains a fourth role administrator and SettingsEndpoints, every mutation audited and no endpoint or log can expose plaintext; a host without Vault:MasterKeySecret behaves exactly as before; Windows ACL hardening is a known gap relative to Linux; ProviderProfile and key are split across two stores joined by provider id; ExtraParameters affects no behavior yet.
column12: Restart-required consequence is superseded by ADR-0045.

column5: Accepted 2026-09-18; amended by ADR-0031 (§3 per-role requirements; where profiles live) and ADR-0044 (roles required depend on the request; root envelope derived from required roles only); extended by ADR-0051 (journal semantics and ReconciliationAction/StepReconciliation reused for ordinary tasks); governs V1.2 and resolves what ADR-0025 deferred.

Delegation must not weaken: one place authorizes and audits a tool call (A5, S9); Critical unbypassable and approval never waives per-step policy; tool output is data including BETWEEN agents (S5); verification fails closed; approvals are not persisted across restarts; four operator choices (D-026): fixed pipeline, human-only approval, side-effect-only journal, all surfaces.

An agent is a runtime-created single-run execution context with identity, role, authority envelope, budgets and parent - not a process, service, thread or plugin; the runtime assigns AgentId (no package or model can supply one); AgentIdentity is additional to ActorIdentity and every audit event of a delegated run carries both; an AgentIdentity can never be an approver; roles are generic AgentRoleKind {Discovery, Diagnostic, Remediation, Verification}; role profiles are host configuration (optional delegation section of policy.yaml), never code and never plugin-contributed; a missing/malformed section or a role without a profile denies delegation (S3); SafeDefault ships no profiles so delegation is off until an operator grants it.

The orchestrator is deterministic runtime code: Discovery (read-only, Read tools) -> Diagnostic (read-only; Findings; may prepare an immutable ExecutionPlan through an ICapability but not execute) -> operator approval of the plan hash (no plan = completed diagnosis, no approval = rejected, neither an error) -> Remediation (executes exactly the approved plan through the step pipeline; NO model call, so a model cannot alter an approved plan) -> Verification (distinct identity, gathers its own Read evidence, evaluates the declared VerificationSpec deterministically, NO model call; Inconclusive and Refuted are not success); the model reasons only inside Discovery and Diagnostic over an envelope-restricted tool view; the set and order of roles cannot be changed by a model, tool output or configuration; roles cannot request further delegation (depth structurally 1, no cycles, runtime rejects any other depth though ParentAgentId and Depth are recorded); parallel execution is excluded.

AuthorityEnvelope is immutable with exact non-wildcard members: allowed Skill/Capability names and Read-evidence tool names, max RiskLevel and blast radius, allowed targets and environments, optional UTC maintenance window, budgets (steps, tokens, absolute deadline), depth and originating ActorIdentity; child = parent ∩ role profile ∩ request per dimension (set intersection, minimum risk and blast radius, interval intersection, minimum budgets against the parent's REMAINING amount, earlier deadline); an empty intersection is a denial (DelegationDenied, audited with dimension and reason), never a fallback to a default or the parent value; the check runs in ExecuteStepAsync BEFORE IPolicyEngine.Evaluate and can only deny, the effective decision being the more restrictive of envelope and policy; the same fields are placed in PolicyContext; a delegated step without an envelope is rejected, never run unrestricted.
column12: Empty intersection in any dimension is a denial is refined per role by ADR-0031 (see DOC-02-effective-rules E-DELEG).

column5: Only Evidence, Finding, ExecutionPlan and VerificationReport values cross between roles: no free-text channel, no role can address another; their text reaches a later role only as delimited tool-result data (S5); every Finding keeps citing recorded Evidence; Evidence gains optional provenance (AgentId, role, delegation id).

Approvals are human only: IApprovalProvider is never invoked on behalf of an agent, an ApprovalDecision whose actor is an agent identity is rejected, the API approval route authenticates a human principal; Diagnostic, Remediation and Verification receive three different AgentIds (a run whose Verification identity equals another role's is invalid); Verification does not trust Remediation's ToolCallResult - it receives the approved plan hash and expected end state and reads the system itself.

A child's deadline and budgets are reserved from the parent's remaining amount before the role starts and reconciled at the end, consumption persisted; restarting a role never resets its budget and a maximum number of resumes bounds crash loops; one cancellation token tree covers run, role and step; cancelling a side-effecting step whose outcome is unknown is journaled as unknown, not failed; budget exhaustion, deadline expiry and cancellation are distinct audited terminal states.

IDelegationStore (Abstractions) persists a DelegationRun aggregate (objective, actor, status, per-role identity/envelope hash/status/budget consumed, approved plan hash, step journal), implemented by bOps.Memory over SQLite (whole aggregate JSON, one row per run, transactional replace); TaskState/ITaskStore unchanged; only steps with side effects are journaled in two durable writes - an INTENT (step index, tool, argument hash) committed before execution and an OUTCOME after; read-only roles store results at completion and restart from the beginning against remaining budget; resume is fail-closed: completed role -> next role; interrupted read-only role -> restart; plan prepared without approval -> fresh human approval of the same hash (approvals are never persisted); outcome Succeeded -> never re-executed; intent without outcome or outcome Cancelled/Timeout -> AMBIGUOUS: run the declared VerificationSpec - Confirmed records done-by-reconciliation, Refuted/Inconclusive stops the run RequiresReconciliation; RequiresReconciliation waits for an operator (accept the step as done - audited, administrator-only - or abandon), with no automatic retry (a retry is a new objective, plan and approval); the store is node-local (A6) and delegation start is idempotent on a caller-supplied key.

New events (delegation requested, envelope reduced, delegation denied, role started/completed, budget consumed, journal intent/outcome, reconciliation, run terminal outcome); existing ToolCall/PolicyDecision/Approval/SkillRun audit events gain an optional Delegation correlation block (delegation id, agent id, role, parent, envelope hash), null for non-delegated runs; envelope contents are audited as a hash plus reduced dimensions; arguments and output keep their redaction (S6) and never reach telemetry.

Runtime DelegationRunner (start, resume, cancel, reconcile); CLI bops delegate [resume|cancel|reconcile|status]; authenticated API endpoints to start/list/read/cancel/resume/reconcile with the operator role for start/cancel/resume and administrator for reconcile; approval reuses the existing human path; a Delegations UI view with existing untrusted-output rendering rules.

All new contracts are additive, product-neutral and dependency-free in Abstractions (moved to 1.2.0-preview.1), no frozen 1.0 member removed or changed, round-trip tests for every new type (A2), the core names no package/tool/provider (A1) and role profiles are data.

Out of scope: parallel agents; agent-to-agent conversation; approval by any agent including low-risk auto-approval; wildcards in envelopes; model-driven selection/ordering of roles; a model in Remediation or Verification; per-role model/provider choice; plugin-contributed roles; multi-node delegation, Control Plane or remote agents; commercial Skills; guarantees against a malicious in-process package (S8).

Rejected: a model-driven delegation graph (poisoned output could steer roles); roles without any model; agent approval of low-risk actions (a second approval channel); enforcing the envelope only inside IPolicyEngine (reduce-only would depend on every engine; enforcing before policy in the single path keeps A5); journaling every step of every role; resume only at role boundaries; automatic retry of an ambiguous step (an unverified retry of a non-idempotent action is the failure this design prevents); separate processes per agent.

The tool authorization path stays single; delegation is denied by default and needs explicit operator configuration; operators must re-approve after a restart (deliberate, ADR-0022); a crash test is required for every durable state transition; known limits: the delegation store is protected by file permissions only, not tamper-evident like the audit chain, and envelopes restrict calls that go through the runtime and nothing against code that does not (S8).

Accepted 2026-09-19 (D-027); amends ADR-0030 §3 and where §1 profiles live; amended by ADR-0044: the table applies to the roles the request requires, a REQUIRED role with no usable profile denies delegation, a role the request does not require needs none; an accepted ADR is never edited to change its meaning.

The literal "empty intersection in any dimension is a denial" forces grants no role uses (read-only roles need no Skills/tokens; Remediation and Verification make no model call) and can block an operator-approved plan once Discovery/Diagnostic spend the token budget; tool manifests declare no target/environment and BlastRadius is Single<Multiple<Fleet so a ceiling is never empty.
column12: Rationale; the rules are in Decision.

column5: Per role each dimension is Required (non-empty after reduction else DelegationDenied audited with role and dimension), Optional (empty = nothing permitted, not a denial) or Not applicable (forced empty/zero): Skills and Capabilities not applicable for Discovery and Verification, optional for Diagnostic, required for Remediation; Tools, Targets, Environments, Steps required for all; risk ceiling fixed to Read for Discovery/Diagnostic/Verification and required above Read for Remediation (a Read ceiling would execute nothing so it is denied; Critical stays Forbidden, S3); blast radius = minimum of the three ceilings; maintenance window: profile, request and parent windows present and not overlapping is denied, absent means unrestricted; Tokens required (>=1) for Discovery/Diagnostic and not applicable (0) for Remediation/Verification; deadline = earliest of the three and already past at root derivation is denied; Diagnostic with no Skill/Capability yields Findings only (a completed diagnosis, not an error); Tools covers any tool a step calls so a plan step whose tool is not in Remediation's set is denied even if its Capability is allowed; Verification needs neither Skills nor Capabilities.

Forcing a dimension to empty only removes authority so child ⊆ parent ∩ profile ∩ request holds and reduction stays monotone; a profile granting a non-empty value in a not-applicable dimension (Skills to Verification, a positive token budget to Remediation) is MALFORMED and denies delegation as a whole when loaded, never silently ignored; the operator request is one narrowing for the objective, not per role (a request naming Skills is not rejected because Verification ignores them); a model call or Capability invocation in a role where the dimension is not applicable is denied at enforcement.

A required budget granted as zero, a non-intersecting window or an already-past deadline at root derivation is DelegationDenied; once running, exhausting a granted budget or reaching the deadline ends the run as BudgetExceeded or DeadlineExceeded (not an authority denial); because tokens are not applicable to Remediation and Verification, exhausting them cannot block an approved plan or its verification.

The envelope is checked in ExecuteStepAsync before IPolicyEngine.Evaluate and can only deny: per step it checks the tool against Tools, risk against the ceiling and time against the window at execution (not only derivation), and for a step with a skill scope also Skill, Capability, target, environment and blast radius; a model-proposed Read call is bound by Tools, the Read ceiling, window and budgets - Targets/Environments are audited and placed in PolicyContext but NOT matched per Read call (what a Read tool touches stays bound by its own argument validation and path policy, S2/S11); a step above Read carrying NO skill scope is denied in a delegated run - only Remediation acts, only by executing the approved plan whose steps carry scope.

Because bOps.Runtime must not reference bOps.Policy, role profiles (per AgentRoleKind, time as a maximum duration with the absolute deadline derived at start as earliest of parent deadline, request deadline and start+duration), the operator's authority request (narrowing only, every dimension optional, can never grant) and a read-only source interface go into Abstractions, additive and dependency-free with round-trip tests (A2); bOps.Policy implements the source from policy.yaml's delegation section and Runtime depends on the interface only; a role without a profile or a malformed section denies delegation (S3), SafeDefault ships none; objective and idempotency key belong to the delegation start request.

Rejected: the literal reading; requirements declared per dimension in the profile (puts an architectural fact in operator configuration); per-Read-call target matching via manifest metadata (deferred, an SDK change across all packages); runtime-owned profile types with host adapters; a clarification section inside ADR-0030 (would change an accepted ADR's meaning).

Operators write smaller profiles; granting something a role cannot use is rejected at load time; exhausting tokens cannot stop Remediation or Verification; the table is both documentation and code and changing it needs an ADR (here: an approved contract change); tested table-driven and with a monotonicity property test; Targets/Environments are not matched for plain Read calls (known limit, repeated in the delegation threat model).

Accepted 2026-09-21; amended by the HARDEN-7 amendment (2026-10-02: aggregate/raw modes, aggregate-only long horizons, temporal coverage, schema 2 for both tools; system.stability is ADR-0041) and the HARDEN-9 amendment (2026-10-03: excludeSources, schemaVersion stays 2; runtime part is ADR-0042).
column12: Amendment index; the amended rules are carried below.

column5: Diagnosis needs the OS log; both stores are large, shared with other identities and full of attacker-writable text, so the tool must be bounded in time, count and bytes, must say when it could not see something, must treat every message as untrusted data, and must not become a shell or widen what bOps can read.

system.events is ONE Read tool contributed by System.Windows and System.Linux (A8), identical manifest apart from Platforms, with manifest, argument parsing, filter semantics, ordering, bounds and JSON output in System.Core and only collection per OS; no service.logs, journalctl.* or eventlog.* tools - a service is diagnosed by filtering system.events on source.

Every argument optional, out-of-range values rejected never clamped: windowMinutes 1-10080 (60), minSeverity enum, source <=128, eventId <=64, channel <=256, text <=256 (first 2000 characters of the message), limit 1-500 (50), maxOutputBytes 4096-65536 (32768); source/channel/eventId/text accept only a small fixed character set (letters, digits, space _ . @ : / ( ) -; no control characters in text) so a value can never carry query syntax.
column12: Exact argument table is tool specification, in docs/system-events.md; the reject-never-clamp and fixed-character-set properties are the rules.

column5: Per-argument meanings of windowMinutes, minSeverity, source, eventId, channel, text, limit, maxOutputBytes on Windows vs Linux.

Deterministic JSON newest-first; sources reuse the inventory vocabulary (available, partial, unavailable, unsupported, notApplicable) and a source unreadable for permissions, missing log service or I/O failure is unavailable - NEVER an empty healthy result; status is unavailable when no applicable source could be read and partial when some could not; truncated is true when limit, byte budget or scan ceiling cut the result; complete is true only when status is complete and truncated is false, so an empty events list is trustworthy only when complete is true; unknown levels/providers stay explicit rather than guessed; raw XML, journald field bags and native metadata are not returned; messages bounded to 2000 characters.
Schema-1 field list (window, observedEvents, returnedEvents, sources[], events[] with timestampUtc, severity, source, unit, eventId, channel, message, messageTruncated, processId, processName).

EventLogQuery/EventLogReader (System.Diagnostics.EventLog, reverse) with an XPath built only from validated values; time/level/provider/id filtered natively, text after FormatDescription; only channels the current identity can read are queried (denied/missing = unavailable, notApplicable for a default channel that does not exist); NO elevation, NO identity switch, NO PowerShell, NO wevtutil; an unreadable record is skipped and makes its source partial; a provider with no message text gives data values (never an invented message); native provider filtering is case-sensitive so source is first matched to the registered spelling and otherwise post-filtered case-insensitively; cancellation calls CancelReading and a 20-second bound (shorter than the 30 s default tool timeout) stops a read and marks it partial.
column12: Process-less Windows API use; the no-shell rules are the contract, collection mechanics are in docs/system-events.md.

column5: journalctl is started directly with UseShellExecute=false, every switch fixed in code (--no-pager --output=json --reverse --utc --since --until --lines --priority --output-fields), every value as its own ArgumentList item, fixed environment LC_ALL=C and no argument reaching the command line except through a validated single-purpose value; source and text are matched by the shared filter after parsing; a scan ceiling of 10,000 records per source bounds work (hitting it with an unsatisfied filter makes the result truncated); stdout read line by line stopping at the ceiling, the child killed on cancellation or timeout, stderr capped; missing executable, non-zero exit or unreadable journal = unavailable; an identity that does not see other users' messages (adm/systemd-journal groups) makes the source partial with that reason; non-JSON/unparsable records are skipped and make the source partial.

Event messages are attacker-influenceable text and cross the tool boundary only as data inside the delimited tool-result turn, never altering runtime state; audit records redacted arguments plus an IToolAuditSummaryProvider aggregate (status, completeness, observed/returned counts, counts by severity, per-source status) and NEVER a message; telemetry never carries a message.

bOps asks for no extra privilege to read more; what the host identity cannot read is reported as a gap; the documentation says which groups/rights widen visibility and leaves that choice to the operator.

Rejected: a libsystemd binding (native dependency; revisit if process cost matters), PowerShell Get-WinEvent/wevtutil (a command surface), separate service.logs/journalctl.*/eventlog.* tools, a minSeverity default of warning, clamping out-of-range arguments, returning raw native records.

One Read tool answers recent events on both systems with one shape; an empty result is trusted only when complete is true; the Linux collector needs journalctl and a readable journal, Windows sees only readable channels (not Security without the right); Linux source/text filtering after the scan ceiling can report a rare source as truncated rather than miss it silently; no Abstractions/policy/runtime/persistence change.

Accepted 2026-10-02 as an operator decision through the HARDEN-7 gate with independent-review corrections; system.stability, evidence-time rules and crash correlation are ADR-0041; everything not named stays; completeness semantics follow ADR-0022 HARDEN-6 (ToolResultCompleteness).
column12: Provenance of the amendment.

column5: The incident showed flooding (100 rows = 7 signatures), a 7-day horizon, and invisible log retention (complete:true meant only "every source read, nothing cut"); a "7 days raw / 180 days aggregate" rule is a cross-field condition manifest constraints cannot express.
column12: Incident rationale; resulting rules below.

column5: system.events and system.crashes each gain ONE optional mode argument (raw|aggregate), the single canonical aggregation switch (no boolean aggregate argument or any second switch): system.events defaults to raw (existing behaviour preserved; aggregation and long horizons are explicit opt-in), system.crashes defaults to aggregate (intentional default change versioned by schema 2); aggregate returns one group per aggregation key with count, firstSeenUtc, lastSeenUtc, raw returns rows; every filter applies before aggregation in both modes; limit bounds groups in aggregate and rows in raw; the result states its mode.

Minute arguments keep their manifest bounds (1-10080); long horizons are a separate day argument (windowDays for events, sinceDays for crashes, Integer 1-180) valid ONLY in aggregate mode; mode resolves first (explicit, else tool default) so windowDays without mode is a raw request and is rejected while sinceDays without mode is valid; two cross-field rules enforced once, in the shared System.Core reader before collection, as ToolFailureKind.Validation naming the rule, in fixed order: (1) minute and day argument together rejected, (2) day argument in raw mode rejected, (3) the remaining checks; nothing clamped and the tool never switches mode itself; every numeric bound stays a manifest constraint and no conditional-schema machinery is added to Abstractions; aggregate over a long horizon runs under the SAME scan ceilings and time bounds and a hit ceiling is reported truncated with the instant actually reached, never raised silently.

Aggregate key = (channel, source, unit, eventId, severity) compared ordinally on normalized values; count, firstSeenUtc/lastSeenUtc, sampleMessage of the newest record cut to 512 characters; ordering count desc, lastSeenUtc desc, then key fields; observedEvents counts matched records before grouping in both modes; record times (timestampUtc, firstSeenUtc, lastSeenUtc) are record times that system.events does not interpret (Kernel-Power 41, bugcheck 1001 and WER 1001 are recorded later than the incident, see timestampKind); the byte budget removes groups/rows from the end and sets truncated, nothing else removed.
column12: Result schema and ordering are tool specification (guide); the interpretation limit on record times is carried by C04:time-semantics.

column5: Crash records merge only on a shared WER report GUID (records without one are never merged); raw rows keep schema-1 fields and add timestampKind, reportedUtc, reportId, eventName, code, bugcheckCode, liveDumpCode, exceptionCode, faultModule, bucket, evidenceSources; dumpPath carries a path string only and the dump file is never opened; code canonical lower-case 0x hex, Linux signal decimal; aggregate key (kind, eventName only when kind is wer, code, application, module, timestampKind) so a group never mixes occurred and reported times; uncorrelatedCount = members without a reportId that bOps does not guess to be duplicates; a crash belongs to the window by its primary timestamp; bounds: 512 records per provider, 512 report directories per WER dir, 2,048 normalized records, shared 20 s budget, Event Log read capped at 10 s, Report.wer streaming key scan up to 256 KiB per file and 32 MiB per call (skipped file = partial source; reaching the per-call cap = partial and truncated), result fixed at 65,536 bytes.
column12: Field list, ordering and bounds numbers are specification in docs/system-maintenance.md; the no-guess correlation and no-mixed-time rules are binding.

column5: Crash raw row fields, code canonicalization, aggregate-key and ordering, window rule, WER source names, ceilings and Report.wer scan limits.

system.events, system.crashes and system.stability each return a coverage object answering only "how far back does each store actually reach compared with what was asked" (never whether the read succeeded): stores with basis eventLog/journal/directory, oldestAvailableUtc, logMaximumBytes (integer or null; always null for journald), state complete|partial|unknown; eventLog/journal store state is complete when oldestAvailableUtc <= requestedFromUtc, partial when later, unknown when undeterminable (null, never an estimate); directory stores (WER dirs, minidump dir) are ALWAYS unknown because absence of older files proves nothing and never change the global state; global state is partial if any retention-bearing store is partial, else unknown if any unknown or none, else complete; each source carries examinedFromUtc, the oldest instant this call's scan actually reached (null if not read); coverage probes share the call's 20 s bound and a probe that does not finish leaves oldestAvailableUtc null and state unknown.

complete = (status == complete) AND (truncated == false) AND (coverage.state == complete); ToolCallResult.Completeness stays derived from the emitted JSON: a scan cut by ceiling/time/limit/byte budget or an unreadable source is Partial, no readable source is Unavailable, a store whose history starts after the requested start or whose oldest record is undeterminable is Partial; Complete never hides a retention gap (an empty or short result for a request longer than retained history is Partial) and coverage complete never makes a truncated result Complete; status keeps meaning source state so the two dimensions stay distinguishable.

Bounds unchanged (scan ceiling 10,000 per source, 20 s per call now covering coverage probes, 2000-char messages, limit/maxOutputBytes ranges); no new privilege, no PowerShell, no wevtutil, no shell; the XPath is built only from validated values and package constants and journalctl/coredumpctl are started directly with fixed switches; audit summaries add mode, observed/returned groups, coverage.state and per-store name/state/oldestAvailableUtc and system.crashes gains an IToolAuditSummaryProvider (mode, status, complete, truncated, observedItems, counts by kind, per-source status, coverage), and neither summary ever carries a message, application/module name, report id, bucket or path.

system.events 1->2 (default behaviour preserved: mode raw, additive fields, stricter complete), system.crashes 1->2 (intentional default change to aggregate, additive row fields, kind vocabulary extension, summary/dumpPath corrected, fixed 65,536-byte budget, stricter complete), system.stability new at 1; no Abstractions change; contract types are package-local in System.Core; every schema-1 argument stays valid; readers must check schemaVersion; no consumer outside the System packages parses output.
column12: Schema version history is tool specification; the compatibility discipline (additive, readers check schemaVersion) is captured by C04:aggregate-modes.

column5: Rejected: raising the minute bound to 259,200 with package-only raw rejection (schema would advertise values the tool refuses), conditional schemas in Abstractions, separate summary tools, raw default for crashes, aggregate default for events (independent review), a boolean aggregate argument, retention reported only via Completeness or only via coverage, inferring directory coverage from the oldest file, time buckets in events/crashes aggregates, groups mixing occurred and reported times.

More results are Partial by design; complete:true now means every source read, nothing cut and history reaches the request start; schema 2 changes only the crashes default shape; coverage costs one bounded read per store; independent review (CHANGES REQUIRED on 017477e) moved events back to raw default, fixed the cross-field rule order and recorded acceptance as an operator decision.

column5: system.events gains optional String excludeSources (MinLength 1, MaxLength 1024) valid in both modes and every horizon: absent/null = no exclusion, comma-separated, trimmed entries each non-empty, <=128 UTF-16 units, source character set, at most 8 entries; rejected as Validation (nothing clamped or corrected): empty entry, >8 entries, entry >128, forbidden character, two entries equal under OrdinalIgnoreCase, entry equal to source; a syntactically valid name matching nothing is ACCEPTED and echoed (existence is not knowable before the read); the description states the limits the constraints cannot (and that excluded sources are not evidence of absence); a String is used because Abstractions has no list type except path-policy-bound PathList.

A record is excluded when its CANONICAL source (the value shown in the result's source field) equals an entry under OrdinalIgnoreCase - no second matching rule; Windows: exclusion is native BEFORE the scan ceiling via a Provider[@Name!='p1' and @Name!='p2'...] XPath predicate built only from registered-spelling or validated names (never caller XPath; not() is not used) AND the shared post-filter is applied as well; if the construct is not honoured on real Windows implementation stops and returns to architecture rather than silently switching to post-filtering (it would change ceiling, truncated and completeness semantics); Linux: canonical source is SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER, else _SYSTEMD_UNIT, else _COMM, else unknown, exclusion is the shared post-filter after parsing only (journald matches cannot be negated) and never compares the unit separately.

Exclusion is applied before grouping, before limit and before the byte budget; observedEvents counts matched records after exclusion; Windows natively excluded records do not count toward the 10,000 scan ceiling while Linux excluded records do; no excluded-record count is reported; every successful result carries an always-present top-level excludeSources array right after window ([] when absent, else trimmed caller-spelling entries sorted OrdinalIgnoreCase then Ordinal, byte-identical for permuted input), part of the envelope and never removed by the byte budget, proven by test to fit the minimum maxOutputBytes of 4,096 (else return to architecture rather than shorten); completeness and coverage unchanged: complete:true with an exclusion means complete for the FILTERED question and ADR-0042 §7 forbids reading an excluded source as absent.

schemaVersion stays 2 (additive optional argument and always-present echo); manifest gains the parameter and description while Windows/Linux manifests stay identical apart from Platforms and both provider adapters project minLength/maxLength; audit carries the redacted argument (not Sensitive) and the summary is unchanged and never carries a message; system.crashes and system.stability gain nothing (self-noise is a system.events problem).

column5: Image, build and volume management are reads or mutations with large blast radius (a build runs Dockerfile instructions and sends a directory to the daemon; a volume removal destroys data permanently); the tools must be typed, narrow, bounded in output and duration, verified, and never a route to the Engine API in general, a shell in a container or a prune.

Nine docker.* tools are added and the existing eight are unchanged (all requiring the existing docker capability, windows+linux, via Docker.DotNet): image.inspect/volumes/volume.inspect Read; image.pull Medium; image.tag Low; image.remove, build, volume.remove High with explicit approval; volume.create Low; each non-Read verified (VerificationSpec + IVerifiableTool); risk follows the effect; deliberately NOT added: container create/remove/exec, image or volume prune, push, registry credentials, Compose - a future prune needs a prepare/manifest/approve/execute design like governed recursive deletion; no generic Engine API, no shell, no argument carrying a daemon path or JSON.
Per-tool risk, explicit approval and verifier mapping.

The runtime carries an argument into the verification call by name (VerificationSpec.ArgumentsFrom), so the argument naming the thing to verify must carry the verifier's name (image for images, volume for volumes; image.tag takes source and image).

Deterministic JSON schemaVersion 1; a missing image/volume is exists:false and a SUCCESSFUL read (so verification distinguishes absence from a failed reader) while daemon errors/permission/unreadable answers are failed reads; lists sorted, bounded by limit 1-500 (100) and maxOutputBytes 4096-65536 (32768) with truncated; image.inspect returns no labels/environment/entry point/command; volumes return at most 20 bounded labels and NEVER the mount point or driver options (host paths that tell an attacker where data lives); mutations return what happened (bounded).

Image references use a strict grammar (components, optional registry host:port, tag, sha256 digest, <=255 chars; uppercase repositories and query-like text rejected before the daemon); inspect/remove also accept an image id (12-64 hex, optional sha256:) while pull, tag target and build tag accept a name only so a hex name cannot be mistaken for an id; familiar names are normalized as Docker does so verification compares like with like; volume names 2-128 chars [A-Za-z0-9_.-] starting alphanumeric.

Pull: typed reference plus optional platform, anonymous registry access only (credentials never appear in arguments, output, audit or telemetry), the progress stream reduced to the last error; Tag: one target from one local source, REFUSED if the target names a different image (moving a tag silently is a consequential mutation), success-no-change if it names the same image; Remove: exactly the named reference/id without force and without pruning untagged parents, in-use or multi-tagged refused with the daemon's reason, a missing image is a failure.

docker.build(context, dockerfile?, image) builds one local directory into one tagged image: Docker:Build:Contexts (empty by default, the tool is hidden from the planner via capability docker.build-contexts until set) is the allowlist - the fully resolved context path must be inside one; the Dockerfile is a relative regular file inside the context (no .., rooted path or control chars; no remote Git contexts, inline or model-supplied Dockerfile text); ANY symbolic link or reparse point in the context refuses the build (checked per archive entry while writing); a .dockerignore is refused (bOps does not implement its matching and will not silently send files meant to be excluded); bounds MaximumContextFiles (10,000) and MaximumContextBytes (64 MiB) enforced while writing a temporary archive deleted at call end; fixed options (intermediate containers removed, cache used, no force-pull, default network) with no build arguments, BuildKit secrets or SSH forwarding, network/isolation overrides, target, platform, squash or extra hosts; output is the image id, context counts and a bounded tail (<=20 lines of 200 chars), never the context or full build log in result, audit or telemetry; runs under the per-tool timeout (30 s default; operators raise it) and a cancelled/timed-out build is verified like any mutation.

docker.volume.create makes one named volume, driver local unless Docker:Volumes:Drivers lists others (the driver argument must be on that list), with no options bag, labels or driver option; an existing volume with the same driver succeeds with created:false, a different driver is refused; docker.volume.remove removes one named volume, never forces, never prunes, an in-use volume is refused and reported.

A daemon not-found/conflict/in-use/unauthorized answer is a failed ToolCallResult with a bounded reason, never an uncaught exception; an unreachable daemon hides the docker.* tools through the capability; arguments are audited redacted (none is secret), results carry identifiers, counts and bounded daemon text; labels and build output are text someone else wrote, bounded, and reach the model only as data inside the delimited tool-result turn.

Rejected: the docker CLI through a process (a command line is what the safety model forbids); one tool with an operation argument (risk, approval and verification belong to a tool; a combined tool carries the highest risk); honouring .dockerignore (deferred, a partial implementation would send excluded files); following links in the context; returning the volume mount point; forcing removal or pruning; build arguments and secrets until a threat-modelled contract exists.

Each operation is verified without a shell or the Engine API; builds are impossible until a context directory is configured and the planner does not see the tool; contexts with links or .dockerignore are refused; a FIFO/socket in a context can make archive reading wait (cancellation stops the call; recorded residual risk); the 30 s default timeout is short for pull/build; no Abstractions/policy/runtime/persistence change, Docker.DotNet the only dependency.

column5: Four diagnostic questions (who started it and as whom, is it getting worse, what is it part of, what did it load) must not be answered with one generic tool: process.start and an environment dump are permanently out of scope (an environment block routinely carries connection strings, tokens and passwords).

process.inspect keeps its name, pid parameter and every existing field and gains ten nullable fields; process.metrics, process.tree and process.modules are added; all four are Read, contributed by System.Windows/System.Linux (A8) with manifests, validation, tree walk, rate arithmetic and JSON in System.Core and only collection per OS; nothing is added to Abstractions.

Read tools declare NO VerificationSpec (B3 applies to non-Read only): verification confirms an intended effect, an observation has none, and a read tool verifying that reading twice returns the same answer would turn a normal race on a live machine into a Refuted step.

Added nullable parentPid, executablePath, commandLine, user, privateMemoryMb, virtualMemoryMb, handleOrFdCount, cpuTotalMs, ioReadBytes, ioWriteBytes; every field is read independently - a field the identity may not read is null and the rest stands; keys always present so "not reported" differs from "not in this version"; commandLine is attacker-influenceable text (S5) bounded to 2048 characters; the environment of a process is NOT in this shape and never will be.

Two samples one difference: pid (>=1), sampleMilliseconds 200-5000 (500); cpuPercent is host-normalized (Δ processor time ÷ wall interval ÷ ProcessorCount × 100, clamped 0-100); a process exiting between samples is exists:false partial:true with no rates; a rate is never negative.

rootPid optional, maxDepth 0-16 (4), limit 1-2000 (200); deterministic depth-first order with children by PID; a rootPid not among observed processes is rootFound:false with no rows (never an empty tree that reads like a quiet machine); skipped counts unreadable processes and complete is true only if the root was found, nothing cut and nothing skipped; owner identity resolved only for returned rows; a visited set bounds parent chains closing on themselves after PID reuse.

pid, limit 1-1000 (200), maxOutputBytes 4096-131072 (32768); rows name, path, baseAddress (lower-case 0x hex), sizeBytes, version unique by normalized path; a process whose module list is unreadable is status unavailable with an empty list and complete:false - the gap is the answer.
Out-of-range arguments are refused with an actionable message (D-028), a silently widened or narrowed request being a wrong answer that looks right; pid and rootPid below 1 are rejected.

System.Diagnostics.Process for memory/threads/CPU/modules, System.Management (Windows package only) for Win32_Process ParentProcessId/ExecutablePath/CommandLine and GetOwner - the managed CIM client with NO PowerShell, NO wmic.exe, NO SeDebugPrivilege and no arbitrary Process.Start; the only value interpolated into a WQL query is a PID already validated as an integer so no model text reaches the query language; kernel32 via LibraryImport for I/O counters, handle count and page faults; names follow Process.ProcessName spelling.

/proc/<pid>/{stat (fields after the LAST ')'), status, cmdline, exe, io, fd, maps (coalesced per path, no anonymous or pseudo regions)}; UIDs resolved from local /etc/passwd only; ENOENT (exit race) and EACCES (partial visibility) answer null for that field; clock ticks fixed at 100; rchar/wchar so both platforms report the same meaning for a field name; Linux records no version metadata for a mapped image so version is null rather than guessed; bOps asks for NO extra privilege and reports unreadable data as a gap (S10).
column12: Collection mechanics are tool specification (guide); the no-privilege/no-guess rules are carried by C02:least-privilege and C02:process-diagnostics.

column5: Rejected permanently: process.start or a shell running ps/tasklist/lsof (S1); a redacted environment (a redaction list is a blacklist and the one missed variable matters); toolhelp snapshot (gives neither command line nor owner, revisit if WMI cost dominates); NtQueryInformationProcess/PEB walk (undocumented, one field from the environment); separate parent/children tools; a sampling argument on process.inspect (it verifies process.stop/kill and must stay instantaneous); clamping; maxOutputBytes on process.tree.

column5: The existing Network package cannot map ports to PIDs, show the full routing/neighbor tables, give interface rates, run a deliberate DNS query, trace a path or probe clock offset; these need native OS APIs, so the native surface is a sibling package family rather than a rework of six tools in production.

bOps.Packages.Network.Native.Core/.Windows/.Linux follow A8 (manifests, validation and JSON in .Core, OS packages only collect) and leave bOps.Packages.Network unchanged, with exactly one native package chosen by OS; network.dns_query, network.traceroute and network.ntp_probe need no OS-specific collection and are concrete classes in .Core taking a platform string (a deliberate, called-out deviation from the abstract-base pattern).
All seven tools are Read and declare no VerificationSpec (same reasoning as ADR-0034: a read has no effect to confirm).

Arguments protocol (all/tcp/udp), state, pid, localPort 1-65535, limit 1-5000 (500); UDP rows report remoteAddress/remotePort/state as null; pidMappingComplete is a top-level envelope fact; Windows owner-PID tables need no elevation; Linux maps /proc/net inodes to PIDs by a bounded scan of visible /proc/<pid>/fd and a process directory it cannot list leaves its sockets unmapped with pidMappingComplete:false - an honest gap, never a silent wrong answer.

network.routes returns the full table (Windows GetIpForwardTable2 parsed by fixed byte offset; Linux exactly the fixed ip -j route show / ip -j -6 route show via ArgumentList, no shell, no model switches) while network.route stays untouched; network.neighbors (GetIpNetTable2; ip -j neighbor show / -6, the second and last fixed ip invocation); network.interface_stats samples twice and reports rates (a counter the platform does not report is null, never zero) using BCL counters on Windows and /proc/net/dev + /sys/class/net on Linux.

name, recordType (A/AAAA/PTR only), server optional, timeout 100-10000 ms (3000); without server System.Net.Dns answers; with server DnsUdpClient sends exactly one UDP/53 query for exactly one of A/AAAA/PTR, IN class, parses exactly one reply (including RFC 1035 compression pointers); no raw query type, class, opcode or option field is exposed - the three types are the entire surface by construction, not by a loosenable validation.

host, maxHops 1-64 (30), timeout 100-5000 ms (1000), addressFamily auto/ipv4/ipv6; one ICMP echo per hop via Ping with increasing TTL (DontFragment) stopping at success/maxHops/unresolvable host; every hop recorded (reached, ttlExpired, timeout, error); NO tracert.exe/traceroute process anywhere.

host, timeout 100-5000 ms (2000); SntpClient implements RFC 4330 client mode over UDP/123, one request, four timestamps, offset=((T2-T1)+(T3-T4))/2, delay=(T4-T1)-(T3-T2); a reply is valid:false with a detail (never a trustworthy-looking offset) when mode is not 4, the leap indicator is 3 (unsynchronized), or stratum is 0 (kiss-of-death, code surfaced); it is a diagnostic client, never adjusts the host clock.
Out-of-range values are refused with an actionable message (D-028), same as process.*.

MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2/MIB_IPNET_ROW2 embed a SOCKADDR_INET union and are read by fixed documented byte offsets (including x64 padding); owner-PID table rows are read the same way; every iphlpapi.dll entry point uses LibraryImport (never DllImport) with DefaultDllImportSearchPaths(System32).
column12: Implementation detail verifiable in the code (Network.Native.Windows); the safety-relevant part (System32-only DLL search) is carried by C02:native-interop.

column5: /proc/net/{tcp,tcp6,udp,udp6}, /proc/<pid>/fd, /proc/net/dev and /sys/class/net, plus EXACTLY two fixed ip -j invocations (route, neighbor; each with -6 variant) run via ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList with UseShellExecute=false, parsed as JSON, no other argument ever appended, no model input ever reaching the argument list, no other command ever run - not a generic process-execution surface (S1).

bOps asks for no extra privilege to see more; unreadable data is reported as a gap (pidMappingComplete:false, a null field, an empty routing table read as genuinely empty only when the read itself succeeded), never silently widened or narrowed.

Rejected permanently: a generic network.exec or shelling to netstat/ss/route/arp/tracert (S1); reworking the existing package in place; GetIfEntry2 struct family; a full DNS/NTP library (exposes query types/classes the task excludes - S1's spirit extends to data formats); parallel or multiple probes per hop; treating NTP stratum 16 as valid with a warning; [StructLayout(Explicit)] for the union.

Typed bounded Read tools cover socket ownership, routes, neighbors, rates, DNS, trace and clock offset, correlatable with process.* and system.events; Native.Windows P/Invokes iphlpapi directly (no new NuGet); Native.Linux runs exactly the two named ip invocations; unprivileged Linux leaves some sockets unmapped (visible gap); traceroute/ntp_probe cost one round trip per hop/call kept inside the default timeout by their bounds; no Abstractions/policy/runtime/persistence/audit change.

column5: Accepted 2026-09-24 by the operator; amends ADR-0016 only for pre-invocation runtime authorization denial of required verification; extended by ADR-0051 (ordinary tasks gain the journal; entitlement stays evaluated before the intent and is never persisted).

Model proposal, policy, human approval, execution, verification and audit are independent; standalone Apache-licensed bOps must operate when no entitlement provider is installed, reachable or healthy, but once an operation is explicitly governed a missing, failed, stale or unsuitable decision must prevent it; applicability cannot be inferred from provider presence, naming, tier or identity - it is a structural runtime-visible attribute and the model never decides or grants it.

A dependency-free public EntitlementApplicability/requirement in the resolved execution context, stamped by the HOST at registration from trusted host configuration or a trusted host-registered capability boundary (like host-assigned package identity - a package declaration is not authoritative, never supplied by a model, provider response, product name or installation state); exactly two meanings: Not governed (recorded, normal path, no provider consulted) and Governed (a current matching Allowed decision is required immediately before the operation executes); no implicit third state - a missing assignment for an operation meant to be governed is a registration/invocation error that fails closed and is never converted to not-applicable.

Serializable dependency-free contracts: a request with an opaque per-evaluation RequestBinding, subject, installation, feature, Skill identity/version, capability, requested resource and amount, node, target, validity context; trusted code generates a FRESH RequestBinding for every evaluation attempt - opaque to the LLM, echoed unchanged by the provider, containing no license, token, credential or vendor payload, never entitlement proof and never reused across retry, resume, replan, delegation or verification; the decision is a closed Allowed|Denied with the same binding, reason code, source category, effective limits and validity metadata (ValidFrom, ValidUntil, authority/freshness id); NotApplicable is host-owned and a provider cannot return it for a governed request; the provider returns the FINAL interpreted decision (including resource and limit evaluation) while Runtime validates structure, binding match and usability only - missing/malformed/wrong bindings fail closed and Runtime does not compare or hash every dimension (one authority for interpretation).

One node-scoped dependency-free entitlement service interface (A3/A5), no product types, raw credential/token fields, mutable global state or package service locator; the host owns provider registration and lifetime; a provider cannot widen policy, approval, the delegation envelope, package trust or the applicability boundary.

ONE semantic boundary: immediately before every entitlement-governed tool invocation (not necessarily one call site; one shared internal routine): in ExecuteStepAsync after envelope enforcement, argument validation, policy evaluation, required approval and approval binding but BEFORE durable side-effect intent and ExecuteWithTimeoutAsync; and for an explicitly governed runtime-mandated verification invocation after the delegated envelope permits that read and immediately before it invokes the verification tool; any other Runtime path that can directly invoke a governed ITool gets the same boundary; prepared-plan, delegated, evidence, resume, retry and replan paths route through ExecuteStepAsync; only a newly obtained, binding-matched, currently usable Allowed decision permits execution so approval followed by revocation yields no execution; entitlement never replaces policy or approval (a policy denial is final) and an Allowed cannot override an envelope denial; for runtime-mandated verification policy and approval are intentionally absent; an entitlement denial of an ordinary invocation is AuthorizationKind.EntitlementDenied (distinct from PolicyDenied), the tool does not execute, and in a prepared or delegated plan the stop set (PolicyDenied, UnknownTool, UserRejected) gains EntitlementDenied (plan Stopped, StoppedBy=EntitlementDenied, no later step) while a model-driven denied call is a denied-action deviation for replanning; no new global task status.

Runtime's injected TimeProvider is the authoritative clock and providers state validity in UTC; NO positive skew tolerance or grace: an allow is usable only when ValidFrom <= now <= ValidUntil; a future, expired, missing-window, malformed, revoked or binding-mismatched decision is denied; a detected wall-clock rollback invalidates cached authority and requires a fresh provider decision; provider-side cache/offline behavior may derive a fresh decision but every attempt gets a new binding which the decision must echo, and a previously returned Allowed cannot be replayed; provider absence or failure fails closed only for governed requests (no grace period invented); resource requests are part of the bound request, exhaustion or an unrecognized resource/constraint is denied, consumption/reservation is atomic at the provider boundary and Runtime never decrements opaque allowances itself.

column2: Decision: resumption, retry, delegation, running work
column5: An entitlement decision is per evaluation attempt and never persisted as reusable authority: resume, retry, replan, delegated execution and verification reconstruct the request, generate a new binding and obtain a new decision at their own boundary; delegation envelopes only reduce authority and cannot carry an allow across roles or retries; revocation cannot undo a completed effect nor promise cancellation of an irreversible native operation already inside ExecuteWithTimeoutAsync (recorded and reconciled through the existing timeout/verification and journal semantics) but it prevents subsequent not-yet-executed governed effects; verification of an already executed effect stays meaningful and must be attempted.

ADR-0016 still requires verification after every executed non-Read call; a governed mutation denied before executing has no effect to verify; AMENDS ADR-0016 in one narrow case - when Runtime authorization prevents the required verification tool from being invoked at all (denied delegated envelope, governed entitlement denial, missing/failing governed provider, invalid binding or validity) neither the verification tool nor IVerifiableTool.EvaluateVerificationAsync is called and Runtime directly returns VerificationStatus.Inconclusive with bounded neutral detail naming the boundary - never Confirmed, never Refuted, no automatic rollback (passing a manufactured Failure to an arbitrary evaluator is unsafe because it can ignore it and return Confirmed); everywhere else the actual verification ToolCallResult goes to the package evaluator which stays the sole interpreter even for Failure, and Runtime accepts its Confirmed; an unresolvable verification tool or failed argument validation stays under ADR-0016; a verification Read is governed only if its own applicability says so (mutation entitlement neither propagates nor exempts all reads); for delegated post-action verification Runtime checks the envelope of the execution context including Tools, then evaluates entitlement freshly if governed and never reuses the mutation's decision; the ADR-0030 Verification role's independent evidence gathering is a separate ordinary step path.

A bounded neutral entitlement audit record correlated with the tool call (applicability, request binding as neutral correlation, decision, source category, reason code, non-sensitive constraints/limits, validity state), never raw license/token material, provider payloads, credentials, signatures or unnecessary fingerprints; a denial after a mutation distinguishes effect executed, verification tool not executed, the runtime boundary that prevented it and final status Inconclusive; runtime-mandated verification gets no peer ToolCallAuditEvent; AuthorizationKind.EntitlementDenied identifies the gate while the separate neutral record explains it; the public surface owns only neutral contracts and generic enforcement - product business rules, provider implementations, credential formats, activation rules and product Skills stay outside this repository and Runtime names none of them.

Mitigation table: missing provider cannot lock OSS (explicit not-governed bypasses lookup); provider failure cannot become not-applicable; verification cannot bypass entitlement; authorization denial of verification becomes Inconclusive not success; stale/replayed allows defeated by fresh per-attempt binding, bounded UTC validity and rollback invalidation; Runtime does not reinterpret entitlement; revocation after approval caught by the check after approval binding; resume/retry/replan re-evaluate; EntitlementDenied stops later plan steps; audit carries only neutral outcome metadata; ambiguous applicability fails closed for governed and does not deny OSS; clock rollback never extends authority.

Rejected: planning-only or approval-only checks (revocation TOCTOU, cannot authorize resume/retry); enforcing only in ExecuteStepAsync (the verification call site would bypass); a public generic entitlement invoker; Runtime echoing/hashing every dimension (a second divergent interpreter); reusing the mutation allow for verification or exempting all reads; absorbing entitlement into policy; Skill-only entitlement; provider presence governing every operation; Runtime interpreting raw grants; indefinite cached allow.

M2 adds the serializable host-stamped applicability, request, request-binding, decision, validity/constraint, source-category, reason-code and node-scoped service contracts and appends AuthorizationKind.EntitlementDenied = 5 with existing numeric values frozen (Automatic 0, UserApproved 1, UserRejected 2, PolicyDenied 3, UnknownTool 4) and public-surface/round-trip/compatibility snapshots; M3 registers the service through the host, adds a shared internal evaluation routine at both known paths and neutral audit records; required sequences: ordinary invocation (envelope, argument validation, policy, approval and binding, fresh entitlement if governed, durable intent, execution, post-action verification, audit/journal) and runtime-mandated verification (resolve, validate, envelope, entitlement if governed, execute, evaluator; runtime authorization denial skips tool and evaluator and returns Inconclusive, with NO Policy or Approval); the M3 acceptance matrix (envelope/policy/approval denials win over an entitlement allow; entitlement denial = EntitlementDenied and no execution; plan Stopped by EntitlementDenied; verification outcomes; wrong binding fails closed; retry/resume/delegation get fresh bindings; cached provider decisions are bound to the current binding) must prove denied governed mutations never invoke the tool.
