column5: Archive intake must not create another loader, manifest interpretation, signature scheme, trust store, registry or installer: ADR-0020's PluginManager/PluginStore/PluginManifestValidator/PluginPackageSignature/PluginPublisherTrustStore and the collectible load context remain the only boundary; an archive is untrusted data until complete validation and commit; no assembly may be loaded, reflected as executable code, constructed or registered from an upload body, temporary archive, staging, quarantine or rejected candidate (metadata-only PE inspection permitted, never into an AssemblyLoadContext).

All upload/install, replace, enable, disable and recovery-affecting actions are administrator-only with API/backend authorization authoritative (never the UI or archive); the PluginStore record is extended additively with manifest snapshot and verified provenance, an opaque monotonic lifecycle version (ETag), CurrentGeneration, ActivationLkgGeneration, lifecycle state and a bounded sanitized failure stage/reason, and an active transaction records TransactionRollbackGeneration and CandidateGeneration in its recovery marker; states InstalledDisabled (every install/replacement ends here), Enabled (registered through the existing boundary and persisted for startup activation), ActivationFailed (not registered, sanitized failure recorded), RecoveryRequired (no single safe current generation provable; nothing registered until an administrator recovers); persisted Enabled intent and actual loaded state stay distinct; Received/Validating/Rejected/Quarantined are transient result stages, not plugin states; a rejected archive never makes a plugin record.

One configured local archive type, ZIP; no URL, remote repository, nested installer or generic package format; API request-body limit and backend streaming limit both apply; configured limits have hard ceilings and a value above its ceiling FAILS CONFIGURATION: compressed 64 MiB (ceiling 256 MiB), entries 2,048 (10,000), total uncompressed 256 MiB (1 GiB), single entry 64 MiB (256 MiB), depth 16 (32), normalized path length 240 chars (stricter platform limit when lower), compression ratio 100:1 per entry and aggregate, manifest 1 MiB; missing/negative/overflowing/inconsistent size metadata rejects the archive; streaming extraction independently counts actual entries/bytes and stops before a limit is crossed.

A same-volume lifecycle work area under the plugin root (uploads, staging, quarantine, lkg) restrictive to the host owner; atomic rename must be provable on the same volume else fail safely - never copy-and-delete replacement; before creating any path every entry is enumerated and canonicalized and the archive is rejected for empty/rooted/drive-qualified/UNC/absolute paths, .. traversal with either separator, paths escaping staging, duplicate or case-insensitive/Unicode-normalization/separator-normalization collisions, file/directory type collisions, symbolic links/junctions/reparse points/hard-link-like/device/special entries, limit excess, and lifecycle control/marker/store names; only after the whole structural pass approved paths are materialized under a unique staging directory verifying parents are ordinary directories, opening without following links and rechecking containment/reparse attributes before and after writing (Path.GetFullPath is a containment check, not the extraction defense); quarantine is transient: the candidate is normally deleted immediately, incident mode may retain it only in a non-loadable restricted directory for at most 24 hours and ten candidates, exposing only sanitized metadata.

Stop at the first failed stage and record a neutral stage/result: (1) authorize administrator, apply limits, stream to a bounded temp archive; (2) structure pass; (3) safe extraction with actual counters and containment/reparse checks; (4) exactly one expected plugin root/layout and bops-plugin.json (ambiguous roots and lifecycle metadata rejected); (5) bounded manifest through the existing PluginManifestValidator; (6) stable identity/version, comparing operation/route id when supplied, never the archive filename; (7) require the existing detached bops-plugin.sig.json; (8) existing PluginPackageSignature canonical-content verification over staged content (no new digest/signature format); (9) signature publisher equals manifest publisher and query existing local publisher/key trust; (10) fail closed for missing/invalid signature, mismatch, unknown publisher/key, revoked key or untrusted publisher (revocation is an additive local trust-store status); (11) existing host/SDK/manifest compatibility (declared dependencies informational, not a resolver); (12) declared capabilities and maximum risk validated against manifest semantics and host policy - installation cannot widen package trust, actual tool RiskLevel, host policy or delegation authority; declarations are not grants or a sandbox; (13) metadata-only structural inspection of the entry assembly/type (construction, provider methods and registration only at explicit enable); (14) under the per-plugin lock recheck ETag, identity, publisher continuity, version transition, collision and state eligibility; (15) only then commit-eligible. Replacement requires the same manifest id, a different version, publisher/key continuity (a change rejects unless an explicit local key-rotation continuity record exists) and a target that is InstalledDisabled, ActivationFailed or RecoveryRequired - an enabled plugin must first be explicitly disabled (single-active-generation model, no silent execution of the new version, no force unload or simultaneous versions).

column2: Decision: atomic install and generation roles
column5: The atomically replaced PluginStore record is the authoritative commit marker; roles are distinct: CurrentGeneration (committed installed version; need not have ever activated), ActivationLkgGeneration (most recent generation that successfully completed activation; changes only after successful activation, never by validation/install/commit/disable/activation failure), TransactionRollbackGeneration (transient reference to what was Current immediately before the replacement began, used solely to restore it) and CandidateGeneration; an atomically written lifecycle journal (operation id, plugin id, each generation/digest with role, phase oldMoved|candidatePromoted|storeCommitted) is written before each non-idempotent rename and removed only after store commit; roles are never inferred from timestamps or version numbers; first install = atomic rename of validated staging then write InstalledDisabled (failure before store commit leaves unreferenced material that recovery deletes/quarantines, never activates); replacement = validate, lock and recheck ETag, record the old final as rollback, move it aside, promote the candidate, write the new InstalledDisabled record (failure before promotion keeps rollback as current; after promotion before commit restores rollback, treats the candidate as uncommitted and preserves ActivationLkg; unprovable restoration = RecoveryRequired registering neither; after commit the new generation stays committed and disabled); a successful install/replace never enables or promotes the candidate to ActivationLkg; recovery restores the rollback generation (B), not the activation LKG (A) merely because A is LKG; retention is bounded to current, activation LKG when distinct, one active rollback and one active candidate (a physical generation can fill several roles), the activation LKG retained 30 days and not deleted until a later generation activated and retention permits.

At startup and before any new mutation recovery is serialized with the plugin lock: unreferenced old upload/staging deleted or bounded-quarantined never loaded; final directory matching the store digest/generation is the current committed install (only persisted Enabled is considered for activation); interrupted replacement or a candidate final alongside a prior current restores TransactionRollbackGeneration as InstalledDisabled, deletes/quarantines the candidate, preserves ActivationLkg and never auto-enables; store references absent/mismatched material or two plausible currents = RecoveryRequired with bounded evidence and nothing registered; store committed before activation completed = InstalledDisabled needing a fresh explicit enable.

Enable is a separate administrator transaction accepting only a verified compatible committed InstalledDisabled generation with explicit confirmation that the named version will execute IN-PROCESS, using the existing PluginManager/PluginHost activation and restricted service boundary, success atomically recording Enabled and incrementing the ETag; Disable is administrator-only and idempotent, uses existing unregistration and collectible context release and persists InstalledDisabled, and where the registry cannot genuinely unregister a provider it returns a sanitized refusal and stays enabled rather than lying; a failure in construction, discovery, registration or activation persistence unregisters every plugin-owned tool/Skill added, unloads the context, records sanitized ActivationFailed, increments the ETag and never reports enabled; there is NO automatic re-enable of the activation LKG (it would execute code without fresh confirmation) - explicit administrator recovery restores the selected ActivationLkg as InstalledDisabled and a separate explicit enable is required; transition table: Install/Replace/Enable/Disable/Recover preconditions (matching ETag, confirmation) and idempotent already-enabled/already-disabled.

One keyed asynchronous lifecycle lock per manifest id serializes install/replace, enable, disable and recovery (no global lock; multi-process access unsupported); every mutable plugin resource exposes an opaque monotonic ETag, M6 requires If-Match for replace/enable/disable/recovery and identity-bound If-None-Match:* for creation, the final check performed while holding the key before promotion or activation, stale/missing preconditions giving a deterministic conflict/precondition response and deleting/quarantining the validated staging candidate with no mutation; a durable lifecycle operation record is atomically reserved at request admission (before archive parsing or identity discovery) under the provisional scope (NodeId, ActorIdentity, IdempotencyKey) in Pending/InProgress state (128-char key bound, bounded retention, plugin id and operation kind are intent not key uniqueness), only its owner executes, concurrent same-scope requests join/wait/replay and never begin a second transaction; the record stores a deterministic canonical intent fingerprint (operation kind, known plugin identity, expected ETag/precondition, activation confirmation, normalized body, and for upload the SHA-256 of the received archive bytes plus the validated manifest identity/version - a request fingerprint, not a signature, raw bytes not retained); same key + same intent replays the one logical result, same key + different intent (operation, archive digest, identity/version, ETag, activation intent, any canonical input) is a deterministic idempotency conflict with no second mutation; followers arriving before the fingerprint is known still join the in-progress reservation; ETag optimistic concurrency and idempotency are separate controls and idempotency never bypasses a stale-state failure.

Cleanup removes temporary archives after extraction outcome, staging after commit/rejection, quarantine after 24 hours/ten candidates and obsolete role material only when activation-LKG/transaction/recovery retention permits; cleanup failure never un-installs or changes a committed generation (it is observable/auditable for retry); audit records upload/install attempt, validation stage/result, signature/trust result, install/replace commit, enable, disable, activation failure, recovery, stale-precondition refusal and idempotent replay with plugin id/version, safe publisher/key category, operation, prior/new state, outcome, actor, node, correlation and idempotency metadata - NEVER archive bytes, signatures/private keys, trust-store contents, credentials, arbitrary payloads, stacks or absolute local paths.

M6 extends /api/plugins (no parallel surface) with administrator-only archive install/replace, explicit-confirmation enable, disable, recovery and bounded operation/status projection; the API owns authorization, existing CSRF/antiforgery handling for browser mutations, request-body bounds, Idempotency-Key, ETag transport, rate limit and sanitized HTTP mapping (stable sanitized categories for validation/trust/compatibility/risk errors, conflict/precondition for stale state); the lifecycle backend owns archive validation, signature/trust, compatibility, in-lock concurrency check, atomic commit, activation cleanup and recovery; the API must not duplicate trust logic and the public projection excludes paths, journal data, raw exceptions, signature material and trust-store data.

The UI extends the existing catalog (persisted vs actual loaded state, bounded validation outcome, publisher/signature/trust, compatibility, dependencies, capabilities, declared/effective risk, recovery availability, sanitized failure stage), may upload and initiate enable/disable/recovery, sends ETag/idempotency key, prevents obvious double-submit and refreshes stale state; it CANNOT decide authorization, signature validity, trust, compatibility, risk ceiling or transition legality; it must show an explicit confirmation naming plugin and version before enable (including after update); stale state refreshes the authoritative catalog, never a blind retry; installation never implies activation.

An enabled plugin executes in-process with bOps host process privileges; signature and local publisher trust establish publisher/artifact provenance and are NOT a sandbox; AssemblyLoadContext, manifest capabilities, declared risk and restricted service construction do not confine malicious assembly code; no process isolation is claimed; the lifecycle is product-neutral and local with no edition, billing, SKU, token format, private provider or business distribution rule.

Controlling boundary per threat: zip slip/rooted paths, symlink/junction escape, collisions, archive bombs, malformed manifests, signature substitution, unknown/revoked publisher, SDK/dependency confusion, privilege/risk widening, lifecycle races, idempotency replay, crash during install, partial activation, malicious trusted code (explicit confirmation + host-privilege warning), audit leakage.

Rejected: a second upload loader/signature validator/trust store; automatic activation after install/update; in-place replacement of an enabled plugin; automatic activation-LKG re-enable after failure; permanent rejected-archive storage; validating paths only after extraction.

M5 implements only the lifecycle service as an extension of PluginManager/PluginStore on the current manifest, signature, trust, registry and load-context boundaries (state model, same-volume paths, exact validation sequence and numeric limits, metadata-only inspection, atomic promotion/journal/store marker, generation-role/recovery rules, per-id locking, ETag/idempotency, transition table, cleanup); not M6/M7, remote sources, deletion, a new signing/trust format, dependency resolution, sandboxing or force unload; later additive work is lifecycle state/version/ETag, sanitized projection, If-Match/Idempotency-Key/confirmation transport and a local publisher-key revocation status.

column5: Accepted 2026-09-25 (operator decision, with amendments below); amends ADR-0014 (what plan and replan calls send); carries the ADR-0022 note for three additive Abstractions members (ModelToolCall.ToolNameError, ModelToolCall.ArgumentsError, PlanStep.UnexecutedToolCalls); governs HARDEN-1.

A real task failed with HTTP 400 because canonical dotted tool names (fs.size) were sent verbatim as OpenAI function names (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$, enforced depending on the routed backend); further defects found: the plan/replan calls offered every tool, orphaned tool results in multi-call history, malformed argument JSON silently becoming {}, explicit null members in requests.
column12: Incident rationale; resulting rules are in the Decision rows.

column5: Canonical tool names never change (identity in Runtime, Policy, Audit, PlanStep, plans, UI, logs); an alias exists only inside one provider adapter for one request, invisible above IChatModel; each request builds one ToolWireNames map over the union of offered tools and tool names in history assistant turns, a pure ordinal-order function with no randomness: a name already matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ maps to itself; any other gets the readable alias (every char outside the set -> '_'); if a readable alias collides with any other name's alias every non-verbatim name in the collision group uses the injective alias (chars [A-Za-z0-9-] kept, every other char including '_' and '.' as '_' + two uppercase hex digits per UTF-8 byte: a.b -> a_2Eb); the finished map is verified (regex, <=64 chars, all distinct) else building the request FAILS CLOSED with a ModelProtocolException naming the canonical names and nothing is sent.

A tool-call name in a response is looked up EXACTLY (ordinal) in that request's alias map and replaced by the canonical name before the ModelToolCall leaves the adapter; a name NOT in the map - including a string that equals a real canonical tool name - is never passed through: the adapter returns a ModelToolCall with ToolNameError set and the runtime rejects it as UnknownTool without resolving or executing anything (a model cannot bypass the alias contract with a canonical-looking name); the JSON-schema fallback path has the same closed rule (valid only if exactly the canonical name of a tool offered in that request); the helper is one internal file (Wire/ToolWireNames.cs) owned by the OpenAI-compatible package and linked into the Anthropic package, no new public API or package, no aliasing in Runtime or other core assemblies, and every future adapter exposing native tool calling must use the same map for definitions, history and response names.

OpenAiJsonContext and the Anthropic context use DefaultIgnoreCondition=WhenWritingNull so requests omit content, tool_calls, tool_call_id, tools, tool_choice and unused block members when semantically absent (per spec), scoped to those two serializer contexts only.
column12: Serializer-level wire detail of two adapters; extracted to a short technical reference.

column5: The runtime still executes ONE tool call per step (D-007); the assistant turn records EVERY call the model emitted, in order; the first is executed; every other call receives a tool-result turn with the truthful text "Not executed: only one tool call is executed per step. Ask again next step if still needed." wrapped as tool output and never represented as success, so each tool_call_id refers to a call in the immediately preceding assistant turn; PlanStep gains optional init property UnexecutedToolCalls (ToolCall stays the executed call) so persisted state rebuilds the model turn without provider-specific ResponseJson, RebuildHistory on resume builds exactly the live turns, and unexecuted calls are never executed, never audited as tool calls and never invent a result.

ModelToolCall gains optional init ArgumentsError and ToolNameError (fixed vocabulary, no argument content or request data); an OpenAI argument payload: JSON object (including "{}") = valid; absent or JSON null member = explicit empty object (required-parameter validation still applies); "" or whitespace, syntactically invalid JSON, or valid non-object JSON = MALFORMED with ArgumentsError set - a present-but-blank payload is never treated as no arguments; a malformed call is returned with Arguments=Empty (placeholder, never executed) and before policy and before any execution the runtime treats a non-null ArgumentsError as a validation failure recorded and audited like type-validation failures (policy is not evaluated as if valid arguments had been supplied); the JSON-schema fallback treats a non-object arguments value as an unparseable reply taking the existing single retry; a malformed call echoed in history sends {} with the result stating what was wrong.

CreatePlanAsync and ReplanAsync (and their parse retries) build the ModelRequest with an EMPTY AvailableTools so adapters send no tools and no tool_choice and the reply cannot be a native tool call; planning instructions carry a compact text catalog of the tools the task may use (the same ToolViewFor(delegation) view, so a delegated task sees only its envelope), one line per tool in ordinal order (canonical name, risk, first sentence of description, bounded), no parameter schemas, prompt text not an executable surface; step calls unchanged offer native tools aliased under §1.

Rejected: renaming canonical tools; naive '.'->'_' (a.b and a_b collide so one tool could execute in place of another); failing on any collision; hash-suffixed aliases (probabilistic); aliasing in Runtime (wire restrictions are per-provider); the helper in Abstractions, a new package or duplicated per adapter; passing an unmapped response name through (operator); treating a blank payload as no arguments (operator); omitting unexecuted calls from history (operator); reconstructing them from ResponseJson; executing all calls (D-007); throwing ModelProtocolException on malformed arguments (the model can correct next turn); tool_choice none on plan calls.

No request contains a function name outside the regex; Policy, approval, verification, audit, plans and UI keep canonical names and aliases never cross IChatModel; three additive optional properties and no migration; an unknown wire name or malformed argument object is a recorded, audited, model-visible failed step that consumes a step, never repaired or executed; plan/replan requests are much smaller; live and resumed history identical; the deterministic strict fake provider double is the required gate for any future change to an adapter's request shape.

Accepted 2026-09-30 (operator decision); amends ADR-0013 (text not edited, pointer added); governs HARDEN-2; operator amendments: 402 = QuotaExceeded and 413 = ContextOverflow only on explicit context evidence (D-3), the overall budget always wins and a Retry-After not fitting both the maximum delay and remaining budget ends the call (D-5), the sanitizer is NOT public API (D-6), a launcher backstop transition IS audited by a narrow dedicated event (D-7), the field is ModelAttempt not Attempt (D-8), malformed plan output is recorded and audited as MalformedResponse (D-9).

A provider timeout (TaskCanceledException from HttpClient's default 100 s) matched no handler: no audit event, no ModelCallRecord, no terminal status, the task stayed persisted Running with no executor; failures were unclassified and retried inside adapters (100/200 ms, ignoring Retry-After) invisibly to the runtime; the reason was not actionable; the launcher had no terminal backstop; duplicate keys in plan JSON escaped as ArgumentException; AgentRunner.CallModelAsync is the ONLY caller of IChatModel.CompleteAsync.
column12: Incident rationale; resulting rules in Decision.

column5: CallModelAsync runs each attempt under its own timeout CancellationTokenSource (runner's TimeProvider) linked with the caller's token, cancelled after min(Agent:ModelCallAttemptTimeout, remaining call budget), awaiting model.CompleteAsync(request, attemptToken).WaitAsync(attemptToken) so an adapter ignoring its token cannot hold the loop; OperationCanceledException while the CALLER's token is cancelled is a genuine cancellation and propagates unchanged (never converted into a failure); any other OperationCanceledException from an attempt is a model-call failure of kind Timeout, recorded, audited and subject to retry; adapters map their own transport timeout to ModelProtocolException kind Timeout; the try/catch classifying a failure surrounds ONLY the adapter invocation - the runtime's bookkeeping after a successful call (metering, success record/audit, plan-shape check) is outside it so a failure there is never classified as a model failure, never records a second attempt and never triggers a retry (no second billable call).

Provider-neutral ModelFailureKind {Unknown, Transient (500/502/503/529), RateLimited (429 without quota evidence), Timeout (attempt/transport timeout, 408, 504), Unreachable (no response: DNS/socket/refused/reset/TLS), Authentication (401; 403 unless structured error says otherwise), QuotaExceeded (402 or structured exhausted quota/credit), InvalidRequest (400/404/405/409/413/422 and other 4xx without context evidence), ContextOverflow (4xx whose structured code or sanitized message EXPLICITLY identifies a context/token limit; a 413 without such evidence is InvalidRequest), MalformedResponse}; classification happens ONLY in provider packages - the runtime never parses a provider body and never names a provider; additive init members: ModelProtocolException.FailureKind (default Unknown), RetryAfter (never negative), ProviderStatusCode; ModelCallRecord and ModelCallAuditEvent gain FailureKind, ModelAttempt, RetryDecision, RetryDelayMs, ProviderStatusCode (audit properties write-when-null-ignored so old events deserialize and the hash chain format is unchanged); ModelRetryDecision {Retry, NotRetryable, AttemptsExhausted, BudgetExhausted, RetryAfterExceedsLimit} where every value except Retry marks the terminal attempt; ChatModelOptions.RequestTimeout/DefaultRequestTimeout (150 s); HTTP 200 with a root-level structured error object is classified from the embedded provider error code (never both success and failure; ProviderStatusCode carries the embedded code).

Adapters make exactly ONE HTTP attempt per CompleteAsync and throw a classified ModelProtocolException (the transport retry loops are removed so every attempt is recorded and audited and one policy governs every provider); the only exchange allowed inside an adapter is the JSON-schema fallback's corrective re-ask (content-level, not transport; a transport failure in either leg throws immediately); IChatModel documentation says adapters must not retry transport failures.

CallModelAsync is a bounded loop over the attempts of one logical call: only Transient, RateLimited, Timeout and Unreachable are retried; Authentication, QuotaExceeded, InvalidRequest, ContextOverflow, MalformedResponse and Unknown are NEVER retried (NotRetryable); at most Agent:ModelCallMaxAttempts (3) attempts; the whole call ends within Agent:ModelCallBudget (300 s) which ALWAYS wins, each attempt timeout = min(Agent:ModelCallAttemptTimeout (120 s), remaining budget); backoff before retrying after failed attempt n = min(ModelRetryMaxDelay (30 s), ModelRetryBaseDelay (1 s) × 2^(n-1)) × (0.5 + 0.5 × jitter); Retry-After above ModelRetryMaxDelay ends the call (RetryAfterExceedsLimit) rather than sleeping, otherwise the delay is max(RetryAfter, backoff); a delay that would leave less than one second of budget ends the call (BudgetExhausted); the wait uses the caller's token (cancelling during a wait is cancellation); empty-final-response re-asks and the plan/replan corrective re-ask are SEPARATE logical calls and never nest in each other's counting; a delegated role's deadline can be overrun by at most ModelCallBudget; failed attempts consume no tokens.

Every attempt, successful or failed, writes its own ModelCallAuditEvent and appends its own ModelCallRecord (a later attempt never replaces an earlier one's evidence) carrying ModelAttempt (1-based), its own DurationMs and for a failure FailureKind, ProviderStatusCode, the sanitized ErrorMessage, RetryDecision and RetryDelayMs; ADR-0013's invariant becomes: every model call ATTEMPT produces exactly one ModelCallAuditEvent; the terminal failure of a task is the last attempt's event; a failure audit is written with the caller's token (a cancelled write is cancellation).

Provider packages own provider-specific parsing and extract only bounded safe fields (OpenAI-compatible: error.message/code/type, metadata.provider_name, metadata.raw message, previous_errors counts; Anthropic: type and message; a non-JSON body contributes only the status; NEVER user_id or other identifiers, is_byok, request content or headers); the shared provider-side implementation is one internal linked file; the runtime never parses a provider body and applies its OWN internal defence-in-depth redaction and bounding to every text it records, audits or shows; redaction replaces with [redacted]: Bearer tokens, sk-/sk_-shaped keys, api_key|apikey|token|secret|password|authorization|user_id followed by ':'/'=' and a value, opaque tokens of >= 32 chars mixing letters and digits, e-mail addresses; a reason is bounded to 500 characters; the sanitizer algorithm is NOT public API; ModelCallRecord.ResponseJson/RequestJson unchanged (bounded by MaxModelPayloadCharacters) and still stripped from the default API view.

A failed logical call ends the task through BuildFailed (synthetic step "Model protocol failure", status Failed, every attempt's ModelCalls attached) with a runtime-built provider-neutral operator reason chosen by kind (Authentication: check credential; QuotaExceeded: quota or credit unavailable; RateLimited; Timeout; Unreachable: check provider URL and network; Transient; InvalidRequest; ContextOverflow; MalformedResponse; Unknown), the attempt count and the sanitized reason; no new TaskState field.

column5: TryParsePlan parses with AllowDuplicateProperties=false and treats ArgumentException as a parse failure, so duplicate keys at any depth never throw out of the runner; a plan/replan reply that does not parse is recorded and audited as a failed attempt of kind MalformedResponse with NotRetryable (usage and bodies kept), with no transport retry on top; the existing single corrective re-ask is a separate logical call, and if it is malformed too the task continues with an explicit empty plan step by step.

column5: AgentTaskLauncher.TryRunDetached is the final containment boundary of the API host: cancellation of the launcher's own token = Cancelled; any other exception (including an OperationCanceledException the launcher did not request) is logged at Error and AgentRunner.ContainEscapedFailureAsync re-reads the latest persisted state and ONLY if still Running persists Failed with a synthetic step "Unexpected runtime failure" (type and redacted bounded message); a terminal state is never replaced and an unreadable state is not written; the backstop never throws out of the detached task; the transition is audited by the narrow TaskExecutionFaultAuditEvent (taskExecutionFault: timestamp, node, task, step index, actor, ExceptionType, bounded sanitized Reason; never stack traces, bodies, credentials, headers, prompt content or tool secrets), written only when the transition happened; the general lifecycle audit is ADR-0040's.

Keys: Agent:ModelCallMaxAttempts 3, ModelCallAttemptTimeout 00:02:00, ModelCallBudget 00:05:00, ModelRetryBaseDelay 00:00:01, ModelRetryMaxDelay 00:00:30, ModelProvider:RequestTimeout 00:02:30 (explicit outer transport guard replacing the implicit 100 s); AgentRunnerOptions.Validate rejects incoherent values (attempts < 1, non-positive timeout/budget, negative base delay, max below base) and hosts additionally require ModelCallAttemptTimeout < RequestTimeout, failing fast naming the keys (CLI at start, API at first model resolution before any task is persisted); an incoherent configuration fails closed.

column5: Rejected: retries inside adapters with an attempt count on one event; runtime classification from HTTP status; 402 as Authentication and every 413 as ContextOverflow; a public sanitizer; no audit for the backstop; retrying ContextOverflow, MalformedResponse, QuotaExceeded or Unknown (resending the same request cannot fix them); honouring any Retry-After however long; converting genuine cancellation into Failed.

A model timeout is audited, recorded and ends the task Failed with an actionable reason and cannot leave it Running; an unexpected launcher exception leaves Failed (audited) and never overwrites a terminal state; up to ModelCallMaxAttempts audit events per logical call; a malformed plan reply is a Failure event of kind MalformedResponse; worst-case latency rises to ModelCallBudget; adapters classify every failure they throw; public surface grows additively; out of scope here: resume semantics, orphaned Running display, cross-provider fallback (ADR-0045) and context compaction.

Accepted 2026-09-30 (operator decision); amended by ADR-0051 (refusal rows 6a-6e, journal-aware acquisition, fenced administrator orphan recovery with no orphan resume, §5.2/§6/§9/§10 additive changes); amends ADR-0017 and ADR-0018; operator amendments: a persisted Running task is NEVER ordinarily resumable (an absent local executor does not prove no other process is running a tool call, fencing cannot undo an external side effect, no force-orphan-resume), the atomic transition is an additive capability interface ITaskTransitionStore that no store may emulate with load/check/save and without which resume fails closed, the counter is ExecutionAttempt never Attempt, origin is explicit persisted metadata with no text heuristic (legacy rows Unknown = refused resume_origin_unknown), the resume 202 only after the atomic transition AND launcher admission (a non-admitted attempt is contained Failed and answered 503), the resume note is withdrawn.

Eleven defects: any status accepted for resume, 202 before anything persisted, zero-plan resume throwing after the 202, MaxSteps resuming into zero work, synthetic failure steps consuming the cap, tokens reset on resume (budget bypass), no lifecycle audit, role tasks resumable outside their envelope, duplicate/concurrent resumes across processes (unconditional upsert), orphaned Running indistinguishable from executing, stale writers overwriting newer state; relied-on unchanged rules: approvals never persisted (ADR-0022 §6), policy/entitlement/verification on every step, history reconstruction identical (ADR-0038).

column5: TaskState.ExecutionAttempt (1-based): initial execution = 1, each accepted resume increments by exactly one in the same atomic write that sets Running; a refused or lost resume never increments; legacy rows load as 1; PlanStep.ExecutionAttempt (int?, null = 1) records which attempt produced a step while PlanStep.Index stays globally monotonic; ExecutionAttempt is distinct from ModelAttempt and no member is named plain Attempt; no AgentTaskStatus value is added and "Interrupted" is a view label, never a persisted status.

Additive init-only TaskState members: ExecutionAttempt, Accounting (TokensUsed, LifetimeSteps, LifetimeReplans), Origin (Unknown 0, Ordinary 1, Delegated 2; set by the runtime only, no request DTO can set it), DelegationId, DelegationRole, TerminalReason (Kind plus ModelFailureKind for a model failure; null while Running), ResumedAtUtc, ResumedBy; nullable ones omitted from JSON when null; the terminal reason carries no free text.

ONE pure runtime function TaskResumePolicy.Evaluate(task, options) used by the API, the CLI and the task view (no host re-implements a status check) with ordered first-match refusal: (1) Origin Delegated task_delegated, (2) Origin Unknown resume_origin_unknown, (3) Running (whether or not an executor here holds it) task_running, (4) Completed task_completed, (5) PolicyBlocked task_policy_blocked, (6) any other status task_status_not_resumable (fail closed for a future status), (7) token budget exhausted against the cap configured NOW, (8) lifetime steps exhausted, (9) ReplanLimitReached with lifetime replans exhausted; resumable otherwise: Failed (any kind, runtime failure or no plan), Cancelled, MaxStepsReached, ReplanLimitReached, BudgetExceeded; rows 7-9 apply to every resumable status so an accepted resume always has at least one step and one token of headroom - a resume that could not progress is refused, never accepted as zero-work; BudgetExceeded is resumable only when an administrator configured a MaxTotalTokens above tokens used.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; SaveAsync is an upsert guarded by WHERE execution_attempt <= excluded.execution_attempt.

column5: API resume sequence: load (404 if none); evaluate policy, refusal = 409 {code,message} audited ResumeRejected; store lacks the capability = 501 transition_unsupported; build the next snapshot (Running, ExecutionAttempt+1, ResumedAtUtc/By, TerminalReason null, Accounting materialized once) and TryTransition(next, loaded.Status, loaded.ExecutionAttempt) - false = 409 resume_conflict, nothing written; audit ResumeAccepted; submit to the launcher; the launcher admits (a free slot and a registration keyed by task id AND attempt) = 202 describing the accepted transition; not admitted = the runtime transitions (Running,N+1) -> Failed with TerminalReason NotAdmitted and a synthetic "Execution not started" step, audits ExecutionTerminal and answers 503 executor_unavailable with Retry-After: 5 - never 202, never left Running; after a 202 a reader observes Running for the accepted attempt or a terminal state written by that same attempt, never the stale pre-resume state; the CLI runs steps 1-5 then the attempt in-process with the same refusal codes (printed, non-zero exit).

Exactly one resume can win a given (status, execution attempt): two concurrent resumes = one 202 and one 409, one new attempt, no duplicate detached execution, not relying on the in-memory launcher registry; the execution attempt is a FENCING TOKEN: with a transition-capable store every write by an executing attempt is TryTransition(state, Running, itsAttempt) (the first write of attempt 1 is the transition or TryCreate when no row exists); a failed write means superseded - the executor stops, writes nothing more and audits ExecutionSuperseded; this covers per-step and terminal saves, the zero-plan re-plan, the launcher cancellation write, the ADR-0039 backstop and admission containment - no terminal path is unfenced; fencing protects PERSISTED state only and cannot undo an in-flight external side effect, which is why Running is never ordinarily resumable; no lease, heartbeat or forced orphan resume exists (future ADR); without the capability resume is refused and only attempt 1 can exist.

Launcher cancellation re-reads and transitions (Running, thatAttempt) -> Cancelled (TerminalReason Cancelled) then audits ExecutionTerminal, never overwriting a newer attempt or any terminal state, after the runner persisted (fenced) its in-memory accounting so tokens already spent are not lost; the ADR-0039 backstop transitions only (Running, thatAttempt) -> Failed (RuntimeFailure), still writing TaskExecutionFaultAuditEvent plus ExecutionTerminal.

Steps: per execution attempt Agent:MaxSteps (15) and lifetime Agent:MaxLifetimeSteps (60); replans: per attempt Agent:MaxReplans (3) and lifetime Agent:MaxLifetimeReplans (12); tokens: lifetime, never reset (Agent:MaxTotalTokens); an attempt runs at most min(MaxSteps, MaxLifetimeSteps - LifetimeSteps) executable steps and the lifetime cap ALWAYS wins (terminal MaxStepsReached with TerminalReason LifetimeStepLimit or StepLimit; likewise ReplanLimit/LifetimeReplanLimit); the loop bound is the explicit per-attempt counter, never Steps.Count; tokens accumulate in Accounting.TokensUsed across attempts and a resume never adds headroom, only the configured cap can; Validate rejects MaxSteps < 1, MaxLifetimeSteps < MaxSteps, MaxReplans < 0, MaxLifetimeReplans < MaxReplans naming the keys; delegated roles keep envelope budgets and a role task has a single attempt.

Lifetime steps count executable steps (tool-call or proposed, and a final-response step); SYNTHETIC failure steps (Model protocol failure, Unexpected runtime failure, Execution not started) are recorded but never counted against step budgets; lifetime replans count accepted revisions after revision 0 (a zero-plan resume creates revision 0, not a replan); tokens are prompt+completion of every model response reporting usage; Accounting is updated in memory and written with every save (a crash loses at most the step in flight; cancellation loses nothing already counted); for a row without Accounting the runtime derives deterministically from persisted history only (TokensUsed = sum of reported usage over every ModelCallRecord in Plans and Steps - a lower bound; LifetimeSteps = non-synthetic steps; LifetimeReplans = max(0, Plans.Count-1)), materialized by the first authoritative write and never recomputed.

Every terminal save carries TaskTerminalReason: Completed, StepLimit, LifetimeStepLimit, TokenBudget, DelegationBudget, ReplanLimit, LifetimeReplanLimit, PolicyBlocked, ModelFailure (with ModelFailureKind), EmptyResponse, RuntimeFailure, Cancelled, NotAdmitted; existing synthetic steps keep their descriptions and observations.
column12: ADR-0014 adds AttemptDurationBudget; ADR-0051 adds mutation kinds.

column5: A resumed task with no plan re-enters planning as the new execution attempt (CreatePlanAsync revision 0) instead of throwing; a planning failure ends that attempt Failed through the normal fenced path, never an escaped exception.

The runtime sets Origin when it creates a task (API launcher row and RunAsync = Ordinary; RunDelegatedAsync = Delegated with DelegationId and DelegationRole from its first save); no request can set it; TaskResumePolicy and ResumeAsync refuse Delegated before any other check so no host resumes a role without its envelope - the only role resume path is POST /api/delegations/{id}/resume; a row without the field is Unknown and refused (no goal/prompt/text heuristic; audit evidence could prove Delegated but never Ordinary) - ordinary resume of pre-ADR tasks is deliberately given up rather than reopening the delegation bypass.

column2: Decision §9 API view and HTTP contract
column5: POST /api/agents/tasks/{id}/resume: 202 {taskId, status, executionAttempt, executing, resumable, resumeBlockedReason} for the accepted transition, 404 unknown id, 409 {code,message} for every §3 refusal and resume_conflict, 501 transition_unsupported, 503 executor_unavailable with Retry-After: 5 only when the launcher did not admit the acquired attempt (409, not 503, for a running or concurrently resumed task); start's capacity 503 gains the same body; DELETE unchanged and audited ExecutionTerminal/Cancelled; the task view keeps every existing property (model bodies stripped) plus the §2 fields (accounting shown effective), executing, resumable and resumeBlockedReason from TaskResumePolicy ("Interrupted" = Running && !executing, not resumable, no status added); /events emits on step count, status OR execution attempt change and ends at a terminal status.

TaskLifecycleAuditEvent (taskLifecycle; hash-chain format unchanged) with stages ExecutionStarted (runner; also role tasks with Delegation correlation), ResumeAccepted, ResumeRejected (refused, lost transition, or missing capability; not for 404), ExecutionTerminal (runner, launcher cancellation, backstop, admission containment: every terminal write) and ExecutionSuperseded; every resume request for a stored task produces exactly one ResumeAccepted or ResumeRejected; fields: base ones, Stage, ExecutionAttempt (always), Origin, PriorStatus, Status, TerminalKind, RefusalCode and a budget snapshot (TokensUsed, LifetimeSteps, LifetimeReplans, MaxTotalTokens, MaxSteps, MaxLifetimeSteps, MaxReplans, MaxLifetimeReplans); never the goal, prompts, model or tool payloads, refusal message text, credentials or stack traces.

No runtime-authored resume note turn is added because history rebuilt on resume must be identical to live history (ADR-0038); telling the model about an earlier attempt belongs with context management.

Every resumed step goes through policy, entitlement, approval and verification exactly as a first-attempt step; no approval is carried across attempts or processes (ADR-0022 §6) and a step needing approval asks a currently authenticated approver again.

Rejected: resuming an orphaned Running task; a default ITaskStore.TryTransitionAsync member; MaxSteps as a lifetime cap with no resume of MaxStepsReached; a fresh token budget per resume (the C-09 bypass); a row-version column; json_extract preconditions; identifying legacy role tasks by goal prefix or audit-log scan; an "Interrupted" AgentTaskStatus; resuming a role task with its stored envelope from the task endpoint.

Resume either makes real progress from a persisted audited transition or is refused with a code and reason; a 202 is always backed by a persisted Running of a new attempt that a launcher admitted; tokens cannot be reset by resuming; role tasks cannot be resumed outside their envelope; pre-ADR tasks are no longer ordinarily resumable; orphaned Running is distinguishable in the API and not recoverable without its own ownership design; additive public surface and behavioral changes (per-attempt MaxSteps/MaxReplans, ResumeAsync requires a stored task, SaveAsync refuses a superseded attempt); tasks.db gains one column.

column5: Acceptance table D-1..D-10 restating execution attempt naming, ordered resumability table, ITaskTransitionStore with fencing and no orphan resume, lifetime defaults 60/12, accounting shape, synthetic steps never counted, HTTP contract, lifecycle audit, explicit task origin and the withdrawn resume note.

Accepted 2026-10-02 (operator decision through the HARDEN-7 gate, with independent-review corrections); governs the system.stability part of HARDEN-7; accepted with the ADR-0032 HARDEN-7 amendment whose modes, coverage, completeness and schema-version sections it uses; its §6 (evidence time) and §7 (identity and correlation) are normative for system.crashes as well; completeness is ToolResultCompleteness (ADR-0022 HARDEN-6).

The evidence for "why has this PC been freezing" (16 Kernel-Power 41, >=200 WHEA-Logger errors, 5 bugchecks) existed but no typed tool surfaced it; the capability must stay inside the safety model: read-only, typed, bounded, no query language, no caller-chosen provider or event id, no dump content, no extra privilege, honest about what it could not see and which timestamps are occurrence times.

system.stability is a Read tool with no VerificationSpec contributed by System.Windows and System.Linux (A8) with manifest, argument reading, category table, aggregation, bucketing, coverage evaluation, ordering, bounds, JSON and audit summary in System.Core and only collection per OS (manifests identical apart from Platforms); every provider name, event id, journal match and message pattern is a constant of the OS package, none named by the core and none from the caller.

Only optional windowDays (1-180, default 30; window [now - windowDays×1440 min, now] UTC) and limit (1-200, default 50, bounds groups) rejected by the runtime from manifest constraints, never clamped, unknown arguments rejected; there is no mode (aggregate-only), no category filter (the eight categories are fixed and their totals always returned) and no argument naming a provider, event id, channel, journal field, message text, path or query; the output budget is fixed; the manifest description states the read-only scope, the eight categories, typed occurred/reported times, coverage, that a category count is exact only when its status is available, a lower bound when partial and null when unavailable, that 0 is trustworthy only when complete is true, that counts are evidence records not to be summed into an incident count, and that per-crash detail is system.crashes and raw records system.events.

Eight categories in fixed order (unexpectedShutdown, kernelCrash, kernelFault, hardwareError, displayFault, storageError, memoryExhaustion, minidump), all listed on both platforms with applicability: applicable (typed evidence collected), notApplicable (the platform has no typed evidence for it and bOps does not infer one), notCollected (related evidence exists that this version does not read; absence of findings means nothing; detail says where to look); detail is fixed package text <=256 chars.

Windows reads only through EventLogReader with an XPath built from package constants and the window (event data read by field name inside the package; no XML leaves it): Kernel-Power 41 (BugcheckCode as canonical hex, PowerButtonTimestamp -> powerButton) and EventLog 6008 for unexpectedShutdown; WER-SystemErrorReporting 1001 for kernelCrash; WHEA-Logger for hardwareError with corrected/uncorrected severityClass; Display 4101 and Application WER 1001 LiveKernelEvent with P1 in {117,141,193} for displayFault (graphics-stack fault evidence, NOT proof of a reset; 0x1a1 is a win32k watchdog hang signature, not display evidence, left to system.crashes as kernel-live-dump); disk 7/11/51/153, stornvme 129, storahci 129 for storageError; kernelFault and memoryExhaustion notCollected; boot context from EventLog 6005/6006 reported only in context and never counted as instability; minidump inventory of %SystemRoot%\Minidump resolved from the Windows folder (never an argument or environment variable), top level only, names matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}$ ending .dmp, reparse points not followed, other entries skipped (source partial), only name/size/last-write read (the file is NEVER opened), fileNameLocalDate is descriptive file metadata not an occurrence time; missing directory notApplicable, unreadable one unavailable ("usually requires elevation") making the result partial.
column12: Provider/event-id tables are tool specification (guide); the constraints (constants only, never opened, reparse points not followed, displayFault not proof of reset) are carried by C04:stability-contract and C04:time-semantics.

column5: One source linux.journald.kernel by one journalctl invocation started directly (UseShellExecute=false, LC_ALL=C, TZ=UTC, no pager/colours, every value its own ArgumentList item; --lines=10000 --output-fields=MESSAGE,_TRANSPORT _TRANSPORT=kernel, not --dmesg which restricts to the current boot); each MESSAGE is matched against fixed ordinal case-sensitive prefix rules in order (first match wins; unmatched ignored): panic -> kernelCrash; Oops:/BUG:/kernel BUG at/general protection fault -> kernelFault; mce and EDAC CE/UE -> hardwareError with corrected/uncorrected/unknown; Out of memory: Killed process and Memory cgroup out of memory -> memoryExhaustion (process name 1-64 chars else null); all kernel-transport records are occurred; unexpectedShutdown notApplicable (journald has no typed unclean-shutdown record and bOps does not infer one from missing messages), displayFault/storageError/minidump notCollected, kernelCrash carries the detail that a panic is visible only if it reached the persistent journal; an identity outside adm and systemd-journal makes the source partial so every Linux zero is untrustworthy and the result not complete.
column12: Message rule table is tool specification; the no-inference and visibility-gap rules are carried by C04:stability-contract.

column5: Windows: 5,000 records per Event Log source (so one category's flood cannot hide another), minidump enumeration stops at 256 entries; Linux 10,000 kernel records; hitting a ceiling makes the source partial, the result truncated and sets examinedFromUtc; every read of one call including coverage probes shares one 20-second bound (shorter than the 30 s default tool timeout), a read stopped by it makes its source partial, cancellation stops native reads promptly; unreadable or malformed records are skipped and make their source partial and values failing their pattern become null, never a guess; coverage stores: windows.channel.System backs every windows.stability.* source except displayFault.wer (backed by windows.channel.Application), windows.minidump is a directory store, Linux linux.journald backs linux.journald.kernel.

schemaVersion 1 JSON (status, complete, truncated, window, bucket, coverage, sources, categories, context, timeline, groups, minidumps): status rules over sources (notApplicable excluded), truncated when a ceiling/time bound/limit/byte budget cut anything, complete and Completeness per ADR-0032 §6, notApplicable/notCollected categories never affect status/complete/Completeness; category status derived from its sources and count (exact when available, lower bound when partial, null when unavailable - never 0, 0 for notApplicable, null for notApplicable/notCollected applicability) computed before limit and the byte budget; unknown evidence is never represented as absence of evidence; context boots/cleanShutdowns null when unavailable and lower bounds when partial; a group carries no hint, query or pre-built argument set for another tool; minidumps list at most the 16 newest files with counters following the same exact/lower-bound/null rule (missing directory = 0); strings bounded (code <=32, component <=128, detail <=256, file names <=128) and either pattern-matched or null with NO message text anywhere; the result is at most 32,768 UTF-8 bytes (groups removed from the end, then minidump files; the envelope always fits - a formatter that cannot fit it is an internal error caught by tests, never a silently shortened envelope).
Worked example of a partial schema-1 result.
column12: Illustrative example; the schema is specified in the guide.

column5: timestampKind is occurred (by documented source semantics the native time is when it happened) or reported (when the system recorded/processed/wrote evidence, possibly later); WHEN bOps CANNOT ESTABLISH an occurrence time it is reported and a reported time is never relabelled, displayed or aggregated as occurred; table: Application Error 1000 and Report.wer EventTime (all kinds except BlueScreen), EventLog 6005/6006, corrected WHEA, Display 4101, disk/stornvme/storahci, Linux coredumpctl and kernel journal = occurred; WER 1001 (processing), Report.wer BlueScreen EventTime (written after the reboot), Report.wer without EventTime (file time), WER-SystemErrorReporting 1001, Kernel-Power 41, EventLog 6008, uncorrected/unknown WHEA, minidump file times = reported; a minidump name's MMDDYY is returned only as descriptive fileNameLocalDate (local calendar day, never converted to UTC, never an occurrence time, never used for window, bucketing, ordering or first/last seen); nothing is promoted in place of an unproven occurrence time; merged crash primary time precedence: Report.wer EventTime, Application Error 1000 time, earliest WER 1001 time, with reportedUtc = earliest WER 1001 time when the primary is occurred; aggregation never mixes kinds (timestampKind is in every system.crashes and system.stability aggregation key; timeline rows are per category AND kind); system.events groups carry record times and no timestampKind.

Exact native identity (same channel and record id = one record, within a call); a crash's identity is the set of WER report GUIDs its records carry (Application Error 1000 IntegratorReportId; WER 1001 ReportId; Report.wer ReportIdentifier/IntegratorReportIdentifier), used only if they parse as a non-zero GUID and normalized lower-case D; records whose identity sets intersect transitively are ONE crash with fields by the stated precedence and repeated WER 1001 records of one report count once; a record without a usable GUID is NEVER merged and bOps never correlates by time proximity, process name, code, bucket, message text or similarity - a possible duplicate is reported (uncorrelatedCount) and not removed; system.stability counts evidence records not incidents: related records sharing no identity stay separate (a Display 4101 and a LiveKernelEvent 141 of one TDR are two records; a Kernel-Power 41 with a BugcheckCode and the System-log 1001 are two records) and the manifest says counts must not be summed into an incident count.

Group key (category, provider, eventId, code, component, severityClass, timestampKind) compared ordinally (null is a value) with count, firstSeenUtc, lastSeenUtc; minidump forms one group; order by category, count desc, lastSeenUtc desc, then key fields; bucket width derived deterministically from windowDays (1-2 hour, 3-31 day, 32-180 week; UTC alignment; Monday for weeks) never chosen by the implementation or caller; timeline one row per (category, timestampKind) with counts of exactly bucket.count integers; result deterministic for given native records and now.
column12: Grouping and bucketing are tool specification (guide).

column5: Coverage is the ADR-0032 §5 object over the §4 stores and complete/Completeness follow ADR-0032 §6; a non-elevated Windows identity normally cannot read the minidump directory so that source is unavailable, status partial and the result Partial, never Complete (elevation is not requested); displayFault reads the Application log so a request longer than its history makes coverage.state partial even when System reaches back further; the minidump directory store never changes coverage.state; category counts of 0 are trustworthy only when complete is true and a category whose sources could not be read has count null, never 0.

system.events answers "what did this log record" (record-time groups/rows with messages), system.crashes "what crashed or hung" (one record per crash, typed codes and time, dump references in raw mode), system.stability "is the machine stable" (category totals, signatures, timeline, minidump inventory; no messages, application/module names, process ids, report ids, WER buckets, dump references or user-mode crashes); two deliberate overlaps (bugchecks counted in stability kernelCrash from the System-log 1001 and listed by crashes from the WER report with a reported EventTime; display live dumps 0x117/0x141/0x193 in displayFault while crashes lists every LiveKernelEvent incl. 0x1a1) stated in both manifests and served by one package-internal normalizer so the tools cannot classify one record differently; the model must not add counts across the two tools.

Read-only; no elevation requested and no identity change (unreadable = unavailable or partial, never empty or escalated); no PowerShell, wevtutil, shell or WMI; no argument can carry a provider, event id, channel, journal field, message pattern, path or query (there is no event query language); dump files enumerated for name/size/time only, never opened, read, parsed, hashed or uploaded; no raw event XML or journald field bag and no message text in the result; bounded records, bytes, strings, duration and output size; native text reaching the result (component, file names) is untrusted data matched against a fixed pattern or dropped; the result carries no hint, pre-built argument set or suggested call for another tool (it cannot steer a follow-up query); the audit summary (status, complete, truncated, windowDays, per-category applicability/status/count, context counts, per-source name/status, coverage state and store name/state/oldest) never holds a group component, a minidump file name or directory, a message or a native field and telemetry carries no result content.

New tool at schemaVersion 1 additive to both System packages and the conformance suite (stability assertions run on real Windows and Linux); no Abstractions change (existing ToolParameter constraints, ToolCallResult.Completeness, IToolAuditSummaryProvider); contract types are package-local in System.Core; no policy/runtime/persistence/audit-schema/adapter change; the core names no provider, event id, journal match or path.

Rejected: documenting the tuples for system.events (it failed, F-10); caller-chosen categories/providers/event ids (a query language); folding categories into system.crashes; a fixed bucket width; buckets in the group key; correlating Report.wer in stability to upgrade LiveKernelEvent times; inferring Linux unexpected shutdowns; pattern-matching GPU/block messages on Linux now; parsing minidumps; PowerShell/wevtutil/WMI; correlating display faults, shutdowns and bugchecks into incidents by time proximity (fuzzy matching turns a hypothesis into a count); a displayReset category including 0x1a1; a per-group drillDown hint; treating the minidump file-name date as the occurrence day.

One bounded typed first call over up to 180 days; Windows and Linux share one contract without false parity (notApplicable/notCollected instead of a reassuring zero; unreadable = null not 0); a non-elevated Windows host is Partial (honest); incidents can appear as several evidence records and HARDEN-9's rule must treat them as related, not independent; adding a category, provider tuple, Linux rule or bucket width needs an amendment and a schemaVersion bump when the shape changes.

Evidence-driven correction: a BlueScreen (kernel-bugcheck) Report.wer EventTime is written after the reboot (0x50 08:45:27Z vs Kernel-Power 41 08:44:37Z, 0x1e, 0x3b examples) so it is reported, while LiveKernelEvent and application reports stay occurred; the primary-time precedence is unchanged and nothing is promoted in its place; system.crashes kernel-bugcheck groups carry timestampKind reported and reportedUtc null.

R1 displayFault category (0x1a1 excluded); R2 unreadable counters are null and partial counters lower bounds; R3 drillDown removed; R4 occurredLocalDate replaced by descriptive fileNameLocalDate with minidump times reported; R5 plan/packets/D-037 reconciled; R6-R12 implementation obligations in the packet.

Accepted 2026-10-03 (operator decision after independent review); amendments in the body: delegated Diagnostic structured output (2026-10-03), PRE-5 evidence-grounded final synthesis (2026-10-09), AF-05G step-diverse selection (2026-10-11), AF-05H deterministic evidence disclosure replacing the §6 model re-ask (2026-10-11); HARDEN-11 gap closed by ADR-0044 §16-17; governs the runtime part of HARDEN-9; builds on ADR-0022 HARDEN-6, ADR-0032 HARDEN-7/HARDEN-9 and ADR-0041 (§6 time, §7 identity, §10 boundary); D-038 summarizes it.

In task 88f97dda the agent answered from a 0% CPU sample, a memory reading and a free-space figure without weighing them against the historical evidence it had partly collected and without saying that two sources were partial and one truncated; HARDEN-7 fixed the evidence, this ADR fixes how it is used.

column2: Context: what HARDEN-7 left in place
column5: Verified baseline: the three typed tools' schemas/modes/coverage/completeness; ToolCallResult carries Outcome, FailureKind, Completeness and there is NO typed coverage field (a coverage mismatch reaches the runtime only as Completeness.Partial); tool output is cut to Agent:MaxObservationCharacters (4,000) before entering history while evidence tools emit up to 32,768/65,536 bytes; the persisted step layout (Description equals the manifest name on a resolved tool, 'Denied' for every pre-execution rejection with only unknown-tool classified Validation, Result.Output complete, Observation = truncated output plus optional verification suffix, WrapToolOutput never persisted, the final answer a step with Description 'Final response').
column12: Verified baseline of the code at the time of the ADR (HARDEN-7 output); the resulting rules are in s4-s7 and the present state is verified in code.

column5: It is NOT an inference engine: deterministic code establishes, labels and bounds evidence; what is added is (1) a standing rule telling the model how to weigh and describe evidence, (2) the runtime telling the model, from facts only the runtime holds, for which steps the requested result was not obtained or only partially available, and (3) a final answer that states those limitations; the model interprets, the runtime makes limits impossible to miss, nothing is rewritten.

Four bounded pieces each where the boundary rules put them: evidence rule in bOps.Runtime appended to the base system prompt (product- and platform-neutral so the core may carry it, A1); limitations digest in bOps.Runtime from persisted steps using only typed ToolCallResult fields and persisted step metadata (the core never parses package JSON); final-answer disclosure check in the runtime final-response path; excludeSources in System.Core and per-OS collectors; there is NO new tool, shared reasoning layer, relation or confidence field in any package output, cross-tool correlation code, runtime-initiated tool execution or Abstractions change.

Five classes: Observed (what a tool result states incl. deterministic aggregates and exact-identity merges), Derived (follows deterministically from observed evidence under stated preconditions: at least N from a lower bound, the digest steps, occurrence bound of an event from its own reported time, order of different events only under the clock preconditions of §8), Hypothesis (temporal proximity, co-occurrence, frequency, similarity, patterns, non-derivable order; stated with support, contradiction and what would confirm it; never presented as observed, derived or a cause), Attributed cause (a causal relation a source record itself states, reported as that record's attribution; nothing else - correlation, order, proximity, frequency, co-occurrence, absence of other evidence, partial coverage or hypotheses ruled out - authorizes a cause) and Unknown (not collected, unavailable, outside retained history, not applicable, null count, truncated/shortened or not visible, excluded - never zero, absence or health); bOps has no product contract that verifies a causal fact so the model NEVER states 'X caused Y' as its own conclusion.

Deterministic code normalizes, classifies, bounds, identifies, aggregates, buckets, labels time kinds, reports coverage/status/completeness, removes caller-named noise sources with an echo, lists steps whose requested result was not obtained and (formerly) checked once for the disclosure heading; the model chooses evidence/mode/horizon, relates evidence across tools in time, forms/ranks/tests hypotheses and writes the answer incl. the Evidence limitations section; EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN inference (forbidden to the model by the rule; no code produces it): a reported or record time as occurrence; an order between different events without the §8 preconditions; proximity/order/frequency/co-occurrence as a cause; a record's attribution restated as the model's own conclusion; an empty/partial/unavailable/truncated/shortened/excluded/notCollected/notApplicable/null result as zero, absence or health; any result as proof something did not occur; a lower bound as an exact count; adding counts across overlapping tools; two records as one incident without a tool-established identity; a single current sample as a historical trend; anything before a store's oldestAvailableUtc as known; a descriptive local date as an occurrence time; EXPLICITLY NOT in code: confidence scores/percentages, causal or relation fields, hypothesis ranking, summaries of findings, post-processing of the model's text.

A fixed paragraph appended to AgentRunner.SystemPrompt so every plan, replan and step call carries it, stating clauses E1 observation vs inference; E2 current vs historical (a single sample is not a trend); E3 bounded evidence (partial/unavailable/truncated/shorter-than-requested/not fully visible is a bounded observation and counts are minimums); E4 absence (no result proves something did not happen; the strongest statement is that no matching records were observed in the readable sources covering the requested period and filters and only when the result says it is complete; not collected/not available/outside retained history/excluded/not applicable are unknowns never zero); E5 time (record vs occurrence; a recording time shows only that the thing happened no later than that time; order different events as a fact only on one comparable clock with no clock change or restart between them and a gap larger than the precision of the times - two seconds when unstated - else only a hypothesis); E6 correlation (closeness never proves a cause; do not add counts of tools that say they overlap); E7 cause (never your own conclusion; a record's own stated reason is that record's statement, otherwise hypotheses with evidence for/against and what would confirm); E8 disclosure (when the runtime lists evidence limitations the final answer contains a section whose heading is exactly the English `Evidence limitations` on its own line whatever the answer's language; per listed step it names the tool and what it reported as partial, missing or cut, or says it was not visible; with none listed no such section - no empty or boilerplate one); constraints: at most 2,000 characters, no identifier-shaped tokens (no token with '.', '_' or '/' between letters/digits, no camelCase/PascalCase, no letter-digit mix), no name from a fixed deny-list of operating systems, products, providers, log stores, event sources and symptom words, ordinary words (complete, partial, coverage, truncated, reported) allowed, no example from the incident; digest template and re-ask instruction are runtime-authored texts outside this rule.

Digest lists the steps for which the requested result was not obtained or only partially available (evidence reads and actions alike, a failed non-Read action listed without registry lookup): from the task's persisted steps of all attempts in ascending Index considering only steps with a ToolCall and a Result, a step is listed when (1) Completeness is Partial or Unavailable, (2) Outcome is not Success and FailureKind is not Validation, (3) Outcome is not Success, FailureKind is Validation and the step is not superseded, (4) the result is shortened: Outcome Success, Output non-empty and (Observation ?? '').StartsWith(Output, Ordinal) is false (persisted data only so identical live and on resume and independent of the current MaxObservationCharacters); the ONLY supersession rule: a resolved-tool Validation failure at step i is superseded when a later step j has the same ToolCall.ToolName (ordinal) with Outcome Success (an earlier success never supersedes a later failure); an unknown-tool rejection (Description 'Denied' with FailureKind Validation; 'Denied' is a reserved description token so registering a tool named Denied fails) is never superseded, always listed as the fixed token '(unknown tool)' and never uses the caller-supplied name; non-validation failures are NEVER superseded (over-disclosure preferred to a silently dropped limitation); entries are `- step <index>: <tool> — <facts>` with tool = canonical name when <=128 chars of letters/digits/./_/- else '(tool name omitted)' and facts in order completeness / outcome+failure kind / observation shortened from N characters, never containing Output, ErrorMessage, Observation text, arguments or any tool/model text; ascending index, newest 16 entries plus one fixed line counting earlier unlisted steps, entry <=256, fixed text <=512, digest <=4,608; versioned template (first line) with markers <<<BOPS_EVIDENCE_LIMITATIONS>>>/<<<END_BOPS_EVIDENCE_LIMITATIONS>>> appended to the STEP system prompt after the plan section (not plan/replan prompts) with one fixed sentence that it is authored by bOps from typed results; WrapToolOutput neutralizes both markers in tool output so a tool cannot forge a digest; byte-identical for the same persisted steps and rebuilt on every step call so a resumed attempt sees the same digest.

column5: Deterministic detector: split into lines; skip fenced code blocks (opened by >=3 backticks or tildes after <=3 leading spaces, closed by >= as many of the same char; an unclosed fence runs to the end) and tab/4-space indented lines; normalize each remaining line (trim; remove one leading ATX prefix of 1-6 '#' followed by space/tab; one trailing ':'; one surrounding pair of ** or __; one trailing ':'); a heading when equal to `Evidence limitations` under OrdinalIgnoreCase (so plain, with colon, #..######, bold, underscore-bold, EVIDENCE LIMITATIONS are headings; 'There are no Evidence limitations', inline code, a closing-# ATX heading and the phrase inside a fence are not); the heading stays English on purpose (a stable technical marker making enforcement deterministic in every language; the section's content may be in the answer's language - a conscious UX trade-off).

What may be said per evidence state: Complete = observed values for the requested period and, for an empty result, at most "no matching records were observed in the applicable, readable sources covering the requested window and filters", never that the event did not occur; Partial truncated = lower bounds and nothing about unreturned records; Partial unreadable source = that source unknown; Partial coverage partial = only [max(examinedFromUtc, oldestAvailableUtc), requestedToUtc] observed, before it unknown; coverage unknown/directory stores = reach unknown, a directory inventory describes files present now; Unavailable = nothing known and no negative statement; Unspecified = no negative statement supported; notApplicable/notCollected/null = unknown never zero; a runtime-shortened observation = what the model did not see is not visible to it; an excludeSources source = not looked at, never 'no events from that source'; a result that says it is partial is partial as a whole; no bOps result establishes that something did not happen and no HARDEN-9 component computes absence.

HARDEN-9 preserves ADR-0041 §6 exactly and adds no time and no promotion: occurred(A) <= reported(A) for one event; BlueScreen Report.wer EventTime stays reported and Kernel-Power 41, minidump times and the file-name date never substitute for an occurrence time; system.events record times are described as 'the event record is timestamped at T' and never promoted; relations between DIFFERENT events require ALL clock preconditions shown by evidence: one comparable clock domain (the same host, D-001); normalized UTC instants (a local date is never an instant); no clock adjustment known between them and no restart between them (no boot/shutdown/unexpected-shutdown evidence in the interval and the interval not left uncertain); a difference exceeding the coarser precision (two seconds when not stated); derivation table: occurred vs occurred = order and interval (never causation); reported A < occurred B = A before B; reported A >= occurred B = nothing about occurrence order; reported vs reported = order of reporting only; record time A vs any B = order of the record only; local date vs instant = nothing; when any precondition is not met or shown the order is NOT a derived fact and may only be a hypothesis input.

Identity exists only where a tool established it (system.crashes report-GUID merges; exact native record identity within one call); no identity key spans tools and HARDEN-9 adds none; a temporal relation between records of different results is the model's derived fact (only under §8 preconditions) or hypothesis, stated with both time kinds, never a merge, count adjustment or identity; overlap declared by tools may be described as 'probably the same incident' only as a hypothesis and counts are never added; causality follows §2; no correlation by proximity, name, code or similarity anywhere in code.

HARDEN-9 acquires no evidence: the runtime never executes a tool on its own and the digest uses only steps the model chose; aggregation uses only the HARDEN-7 mode (no aggregate argument, no second switch); bounds: evidence rule <=2,000 chars constant, digest <=4,608, re-asks <=1 per original answer, relations/groups/candidates/confidence values computed by HARDEN-9: 0, evidence records read: 0 new, excludeSources <=8 entries × 128 chars ≤ 1,024.

The digest does not breach S5: raw tool-result text never modifies system/runtime instructions (it reaches the model only inside the delimited tool-result turn); tool text never enters the digest (no Output, ErrorMessage, Observation, argument or model text); typed metadata the runtime already extracted may ONLY select fixed runtime-authored tokens (a completeness/outcome/failure-kind value selects its enum name; integers are step indexes and lengths; the tool label is a resolved canonical name passing a fixed shape check or a fixed token) and never changes the goal, tool list, policy or budgets - a tool declaring Partial can at most cause a fixed limitation line; the evidence rule and the re-ask instruction are constants; the model's original answer is placed in a re-ask only as an assistant turn, never inside a runtime-authored turn; digest markers are neutralized in tool output; no new read capability, dump access or query surface.

Three kinds of statement stay distinguishable without new audit types: tool observation (ToolCallAuditEvent with Outcome, FailureKind, Completeness), deterministic derivation (the digest is a pure function of persisted steps, reproducible and not stored again), model interpretation (ModelCallAuditEvent per call); a tool call returned by a re-ask is not a task tool call and produces no ToolCallAuditEvent; the final step's Description takes fixed values (Final response; ...re-ask accepted; ...re-ask result not used) recognized by ONE shared runtime predicate: a step is the final-response step only when its Description is exactly one of the fixed markers (ordinal) AND its ToolCall is null; the final step's ModelCalls are reconstructed by logical call (a record with ModelAttempt 1 or null starts a new logical call); telemetry spans carry bops.evidence_limitations (entry count) and bops.evidence_disclosure_reask, never content.

Contract classification table (no new tools, no Abstractions change, runtime prompt rule + digest + final-step markers required, additive Agent:EvidenceDisclosureRetries, system.events excludeSources, description-only fix, schemaVersions unchanged; typed coverage field/list type/relation fields/persisted disclosure field/model-call kind deferred); shared runtime pieces are platform-neutral and only the native exclusion differs by OS (E4 handles the notApplicable/notCollected asymmetry, no new parity); HARDEN-7 N-2 mandatory item: the system.crashes manifest states a BlueScreen/kernel-bugcheck Report.wer EventTime is reported while application and LiveKernelEvent times stay occurred; the digest is built from persisted steps so compaction does not change it and a compacted step is not a limitation by itself; HARDEN-9 detects and discloses observations shortened under the 4,000-character budget and does not change that budget.
