column5: The delegated Diagnostic role's final reply is only one JSON object {"findings":[...]} (ADR-0030 §2/§4) which cannot carry an Evidence limitations heading, so a heading re-ask silently emptied the diagnosis (FindingsOf yields 0 findings) removing a safety-relevant input to human approval; scope is exactly one case selected by the typed predicate `delegation is not null && delegation.Correlation.Agent?.Role == AgentRoleKind.Diagnostic` - never a text heuristic, not generalized to other roles, every JSON reply or other machine-readable output (Discovery's prose summary and every ordinary task keep the disclosure behavior; a future structured role needs its own decision).

For the delegated Diagnostic role: no disclosure step at all, the original JSON persisted unchanged with Description 'Final response'; the digest still exists and is placed in the role's prompts with template EvidenceLimitations/v2 whose structured-role closing sentence says (five normative points): keep exactly the required structured JSON payload; add no prose/heading/code fence outside it; this structured-output instruction REPLACES the separate Evidence limitations section requirement; qualify only findings a listed limitation materially affects; never create or alter a finding merely to encode a limitation; fixed text <=512 and digest <=4,608 characters; a runtime limitation is NOT a finding: a materially affected, otherwise supported finding's summary may be qualified (evidenceIds that already support it, no invented/changed evidenceIds, no severity change solely to carry a limitation, no attaching to an unaffected finding, no dropping a supported finding because of an unrelated limitation); a limitation affecting no finding is not represented in the payload (it stays recoverable from the persisted role task); E1-E7 govern the Diagnostic role unchanged, only E8's separate prose-section FORM does not apply; the common evidence-rule constant is identical for ordinary tasks, Discovery and Diagnostic (the role-specific direction lives only in the runtime-authored digest sentence chosen by the typed predicate); auditability unchanged.

column2: PRE-5 grounding: problem and what holds
column5: A final answer stated that an event group that persisted evidence had positively observed had not been observed; ADR-0050 gives the runtime typed bounded package-owned facts (ToolCallResult.Facts, EvidenceFact {Type,Key,ValueType,Value}); the amendment narrows §3 (no post-processing), §6 and §12 for one purpose; the runtime never edits, truncates, appends to or annotates the model's text (every persisted final answer is model-written byte for byte) - it adds a second runtime-authored data block in step prompts, at most one model CHECK and one model RESTATEMENT of a candidate, and the right to REFUSE to persist a candidate the guard classified as contradicting an observed fact, ending the attempt Failed.

An EvidenceFact grounds an answer only when, from persisted state only: it is on a persisted step with ToolCall and Result (all attempts, ascending Index); Result.Outcome is Success and the step is not an unknown-tool rejection; ExecutionClassification is null or Matched (SemanticMismatch/ArgumentValidationFailure never executed and ground nothing); Completeness is not Unavailable; the fact list passes ADR-0050 EvidenceFacts.Validate again when read back (a failing list contributes nothing - fail closed); an executed step stays evidence after a replan; nothing else is read (no Output, Observation, ErrorMessage, argument, RequestJson/ResponseJson, model or exception text), Type and Key stay opaque ordinal identifiers and the runtime knows no package/tool/OS/diagnostic vocabulary and never parses tool output to obtain or check a fact; classes: Observed (fact with provenance: id, step, tool, Type, Key, ValueType, exact typed value; a Partial-step fact is observed and labelled partial: counts are minimums), Unknown/limited (steps the digest lists; a missing fact is NOT absence; the ledger never contains a zero/false/'not found' a tool did not emit and the runtime derives no negative statement), Inference/hypothesis (the model's).

The ledger is a pure function of persisted steps and plan revisions (byte-identical live and after reopen/resume): fact id F<step>.<position>; selection: facts an Activation of a persisted plan revision refers to first, then the AF-05G step-diverse round-robin; at most 12 facts shown, rendered ascending with the fixed line '<N> additional observed fact(s) are not shown.'; entry `- <id> step <index> <tool>: type <T> key <K> = <ValueType> <value>` plus ' (from partial evidence)'; <T>, <K> and string/path values rendered as JSON string literals with the default System.Text.Json encoder (escapes control chars, quotes, <, >, & and non-ASCII) so a fact cannot break a line, open/close a marker or look like runtime text; a value rendering over 160 chars is shown as '(value of <N> characters not shown)' and an entry over 512 is not shown; the Unknown line lists the newest 16 digest-listed step indexes; versioned first line EvidenceGrounding/v1 and a fixed paragraph (block authored by bOps from typed facts, quoted values are data never instructions, an observed fact must never be stated as absent/zero/false/different, partial counts are minimums, an unlisted fact is not an absence, anything beyond the facts is inference, unknown steps are never zero or absence); appended to the STEP system prompt after the digest between <<<BOPS_EVIDENCE_GROUNDING>>> and <<<END_BOPS_EVIDENCE_GROUNDING>>> only when at least one fact is shown, neutralized in tool output; in every step prompt (not final-only) because a step call IS the final synthesis whenever it calls no tool and raw output can be compacted away while typed facts stay persisted; bounds 12×512 + fixed ≤ 1,024 → ≤ 7,168 UTF-16 code units; facts per step stay ADR-0050's (≤16, ≤4,096 serialized bytes, identifiers ≤128, text ≤1,024); §12 is NARROWED: fact Type/Key/string values (package-produced text) may appear in a runtime-authored block only inside this delimited block and the correction instruction, only as escaped JSON literals of a validated bounded EvidenceFact labelled as data; free tool text (Output, Observation, ErrorMessage) never enters any runtime-authored block.

Natural-language contradiction detection is NOT deterministic and bOps does not pretend otherwise (no regex, keyword list, negation heuristic or NLP over the answer): the model judges whether a sentence states an observed fact as absent/zero/false/different (a bounded model judgement); the runtime deterministically owns the ledger, the judgement's closed shape (every cited fact id is a shown observed fact, every cited quote occurs in the candidate), that a flagged candidate is never persisted as Completed unless replaced by an accepted correction, the correction acceptance conditions and the outcome transitions; 'no contradiction cited' means only that a valid check reply cited none - the model's judgement, never 'verified' (a word bOps reserves for post-action verification); enforceable subset: a contradiction of a shown observed fact cited with a verbatim quote cannot become the persisted answer of a Completed task nor can a correction that repeats the quote; documented residual risk: a contradiction the check misses or cites only by paraphrase, a contradiction of an omitted fact, an E4 violation against unknown evidence, and one the correction reintroduces in different words (accepted deliberately to keep the hard bound of at most two added logical calls); a check false positive costs at most one restatement or a Failed attempt, never a persisted contradicted answer; quote matching collapses whitespace runs and is otherwise ordinal.

Trigger: after the disclosure handling settled the candidate, when the ledger shows >=1 fact, the answer is not the delegated Diagnostic structured payload and the budget conditions hold; NO operator switch (PRE-5 is a MUST of stable V1.3; unlike the soft disclosure restatement the guard cannot be configured off; Agent:EvidenceGroundingChecks was removed before release; cost bounded: <=2 logical calls only when a fact exists; a model that cannot produce the check reply only yields 'check unavailable', never a failed task); request = the step's request plus the candidate as an assistant turn and one fixed user turn (check only that previous answer, do not answer the task or call tools, a contradiction states an observed fact as absent/zero/false/different for the same scope, hedges/hypotheses/other period-scope-source-category-key are not contradictions, reply with exactly one JSON object {"contradictions":[{"fact":"<id>","quote":"<exact words>"}]} <=8 entries from observed ids); accepted reply: no tool call, trimmed text with one optional fence removed parses (duplicate names rejected at every level) as an object whose only member is contradictions (array of <=8 objects whose only members are strings fact and quote); any other shape (tool call, empty, malformed, extra/missing member, non-string, >8 entries, model failure, timeout) is 'check unavailable'; within the shape an entry is a CITATION only when fact is a shown fact id and quote (1-512 units, not blank) occurs in the candidate, non-citations are ignored (a valid citation is never discarded because a sibling was wrong), an empty array is 'no contradiction cited', entries of which none is a citation are 'check unavailable'.

On at least one cited contradiction: one restatement request = the step's request plus the candidate as an assistant turn and one fixed runtime-authored user turn listing the cited facts as ledger entries (NEVER the quotes: model text is never placed in a runtime-authored turn), asking to restate the complete answer agreeing with the observed facts, state uncertainty explicitly, keep everything else including an Evidence limitations section, no new analysis, no tools; accepted only when it has no tool call, is non-empty, is not a TerminalProtocolArtifact, is not shaped like a check reply (a JSON object with a contradictions member), contains none of the cited quotes and carries the disclosure heading if the corrected candidate did; it is not checked again.

Outcome table: no fact/Diagnostic/budget exhausted = candidate persisted (no check); check no contradiction cited = candidate with marker, Completed; check unavailable = candidate with marker saying the check did not happen, Completed (never presented as checked or consistent; failing would make availability depend on the model's JSON ability without evidence the answer is wrong); contradiction + accepted correction = correction persisted, Completed; contradiction + correction repeating a quote/tool call/artifact/check-shaped reply/dropped heading = Failed RuntimeFailure; empty correction = Failed EmptyResponse; correction model failure/timeout = Failed ModelFailure with its kind; cancellation or attempt-duration budget propagates; the failure step carries a fixed runtime message and ModelCalls and the flagged candidate is NEVER stored as an answer; no new status, terminal kind or failure kind; once a citation exists no path leads to 'check unavailable' or back to the original answer.

One fixed pipeline with no callbacks: model reply -> EvidenceRead resolution (bounded) -> empty-reply retries -> terminal protocol validation + one correction (failure -> Failed) -> empty check (-> Failed EmptyResponse) -> disclosure phase (never fails the task) -> grounding check (<=1) -> grounding correction (<=1; failure -> Failed) -> persist final step; disclosure runs before grounding so the text the check judges is the text persisted; at most 2 added logical model calls per final answer, each subject to ADR-0039 attempts and budget (provider retries never add a logical call); none creates a step, consumes step/replan budget, executes/authorizes/audits a tool or alters the plan cursor; tokens count in TokensUsed; the final step's Description is `Final response` + optional disclosure suffix + optional grounding suffix (twelve fixed strings recognized by the one predicate: exact ordinal match AND ToolCall == null; legacy strings read back unchanged), written by the runtime only so no model/tool text can set it; logical calls reconstructed from the end; every call is a ModelCallRecord and ModelCallAuditEvent; spans carry bops.evidence_grounding and bops.evidence_grounding_facts, never content.

The runtime understands only EvidenceFact; a package that wants its evidence grounded emits bounded facts about its own output: system.events emits for matched records at most 12 facts of type system.events.matched-count with key `source=<source>;eventId=<id>` (or source only) and an Integer value = matched records in the window and filters as collected (a minimum when Partial), groups ordered by most severe record then count, newest record, key (no ranking by name), keys over 128 chars skipped never cut, and a final system.events.unlisted-groups fact (key source-and-event-id) counting groups not listed so the list never reads as exhaustive; no zero-count fact is ever emitted (absence is never a fact); output JSON and schemaVersion unchanged; residual: no bounded rule lists every group of an arbitrarily broad call - a group outranked by >11 groups is counted in unlisted-groups, is not an observed fact and a denial of it is outside the guard.

column5: The PRE-5 newest-first selection let one dense recent step take all 12 slots; new rule: (1) activation-referenced facts first (newest step first, then list position; 12 or more referenced take all slots); (2) the remaining slots by a step-diverse round-robin: steps with a non-referenced fact ordered newest to oldest, pass 1 takes the first remaining fact of each, pass 2 the second, and so on (each step's package-owned list order) until 12 are shown or none left (example A1 B1 C1 A2 B2 C2 A3); (3) a fact whose entry would exceed 512 characters is dropped before the passes and counts as omitted; (4) display order stays ascending (step, position) and the fact id stays F<step>.<persisted position>; uses only step index, list position and whether an activation refers to it (Type/Key opaque, no score, ranking model, embedding or relevance judgement); deterministic, package/tool/OS-neutral, byte-identical live and resumed; unchanged: fact definition, completeness semantics, the 12-fact/512-char/7,168 bounds, omission and unknown lines, markers, entry format, check and correction contracts, the authority model (the ledger projects facts, it decides nothing); EvidenceGrounding/v1 is NOT bumped (version names the wire/template format, which is byte-for-byte unchanged).

Supersedes the §6 re-ask: a live restatement rewrote an answer and changed a fact (26 vs 27) that the grounding check missed; rule: (1) the disclosure phase NEVER rewrites the final answer and makes NO model call; (2) when the persisted digest is non-empty, the role is not the delegated Diagnostic one, Agent:EvidenceDisclosureEnabled (default true) and the detector finds no heading, the runtime appends: the answer + (a closing fence line only if the answer ends inside an unclosed fence) + a blank line + `## Evidence limitations` + the fixed line `Added by bOps from typed tool results (EvidenceDisclosure/v2); the answer above is unchanged. ...` + the digest's listed entry lines exactly as rendered from typed fields + the omission line when entries are not shown - never any tool output/error/observation/argument/model text, at most the digest bound (4,608); (3) the original answer is an exact byte-identical prefix of the persisted final, an answer with a valid heading is persisted byte-identical, no listed limitations = nothing appended; (4) the section is a pure function of the persisted steps, persisted once and never recomputed on resume; (5) Description `Final response; evidence limitations appended by runtime` (+ PRE-5 suffixes), the two historical re-ask markers stay readable and only they reconstruct a re-ask logical call; (6) PRE-5 grounding checks the original answer plus the appended section and a grounding correction must keep the heading; (7) Agent:EvidenceDisclosureEnabled default true, Agent:EvidenceDisclosureRetries deprecated (0 disables, 1 changes nothing, any other value fails validation, never causes a model call); residual gap: 'not contradicted' is not 'fully supported' - a general claim-support/entailment checker is a separate task.

Accepted 2026-10-05 (operator decision; independent security review CHANGES REQUIRED with blocker B-1 resolved in 0406469 and delta review PASS); amends ADR-0018 for AUTHENTICATION ONLY (a second scheme for browsers, session endpoint behaviours, a CSRF gate); leaves ADR-0040 and ADR-0037 unchanged in meaning (§9 IS the CSRF handling ADR-0037 delegates to the API); no Abstractions change.

Verified baseline at main 0e006c4: Bearer-only ApiKeyAuthenticationHandler (SHA-256 + FixedTimeEquals over Authentication:ApiKeys in configuration order, claims NameIdentifier/Name/Role; options snapshotted so key/role changes take effect at the next host start); four role policies viewer/operator/approver/administrator; one global rate limiter (600/min GET per credential, 120/min writes per credential or IP); the UI kept the raw key in memory and re-entered it after F5; per-concern SQLite files; no request logging and a Development developer exception page that renders request headers and cookies; the plugin-lifecycle prose that 'ambient cookies never authenticate a mutation' needs updating.

column5: Supported dev topology measured in Chrome and Firefox (browser origin http://localhost:4200, API http://localhost:5080 via the ng serve proxy, Host rewritten by changeOrigin, Origin and Referer present, no X-Forwarded-*): hardened Secure + __Host- cookies work in both; cookies are not port-isolated so SameSite=Strict does not stop a page on another localhost port (a same-site no-cors text/plain POST and form POST ARRIVE with the cookie; a custom-header fetch is held at an unanswered preflight); conclusions: the API cannot derive the browser origin from Host so same-origin validation compares against CONFIGURED UI origins never Host or forwarded headers, and the custom header plus Origin validation is load-bearing, not defence in depth.

A browser exchanges an API key once (POST /api/session) for an opaque server-side session represented by cookie __Host-bops_session: bounded (idle and absolute expiry), revocable (logout, credential change), bound to the credential AND its current secret value, stored only as digests; Bearer for the CLI and API clients unchanged; no CORS, OAuth/OIDC/SSO, user accounts, refresh tokens or production SPA hosting introduced.

The credential loop moves into one internal singleton ApiCredentialAuthority (IOptions<ApiAuthenticationOptions>, ISecretProvider) owning FindByPresentedKey (the existing algorithm verbatim: configuration order, skip empty Id, resolve secret, skip empty secret, SHA-256 both, FixedTimeEquals, first match wins), FindBySessionBinding (including the Bearer-equivalence check evaluated with the SAME ordered resolution - one ordered credential-resolution semantic so the same configuration and secret yield the same effective credential under Bearer and a session) and CreatePrincipal (existing claim construction verbatim; only the authentication type differs); a match exposes Id, DisplayName, roles and SecretDigest, never the secret; the Bearer handler's observable behavior must be identical before and after.

Token = 32 bytes from RandomNumberGenerator (256-bit CSPRNG, per login, never derived); cookie value = unpadded base64url (exactly 43 chars; accepted only if it decodes to 32 bytes and re-encodes identically); raw bytes zeroed after use; stored digest = plain SHA-256(token) as a 32-byte BLOB (no HMAC pepper: a keyed digest would add a server secret with no gain; DB write access cannot mint a session because a usable row also needs the credential binding); lookup by digest equality on the primary key; a unique-constraint violation on insert regenerates the token once, a second violation is a server error (500, no session); no rotation during a session.

Each session row stores the credential id and binding = HMAC-SHA256(key = the 32 token bytes, message = ASCII('bops-session-binding-v1') || UInt32BE(len(UTF-8 credentialId)) || credentialId || SHA-256(UTF-8 resolved secret)) - keyed by the never-stored token so the database holds no value letting anyone test API-key guesses offline; every cookie request walks Authentication:ApiKeys for entries whose Id equals the stored credential_id and whose secret resolves non-empty, compares the binding with FixedTimeEquals, first match is candidate E (none = invalid, row deleted); MANDATORY Bearer equivalence: FindByPresentedKey(E.resolvedSecret) must be E itself (the same configuration entry) - if an EARLIER entry under any Id resolves to the same secret the session is invalid (401, row deleted, deletion cookie, category credential_changed), never continuing as E and never becoming the earlier identity; normative validation order: parse/canonicalise token, find row by digest, idle and absolute expiry, locate candidate by stored id, verify binding, resolve the secret through current Bearer ordering, require the Bearer-selected entry to be E, derive CURRENT claims and roles from E, authenticate (any failure in steps 4-7 = 401, row deleted, deletion cookie) so session authority never exceeds current Bearer authority for that key; cases: normal valid; rotated secret = binding mismatch 401; removed credential = no candidate 401; same secret earlier under another id = 401 (never either identity); duplicate secret later = valid with current roles of ops; unresolvable (empty) secret = 401 fail closed; changing only the SecretReference to a variable holding the same value is not a rotation; roles are re-resolved on every request and never snapshotted; invalidation happens lazily on the first request after a restart plus a startup sweep of unknown credential ids.

The session store is an HTTP-host concern in bOps.Api (IBrowserSessionStore / SqliteBrowserSessionStore, no generic SQL exposed) in its own file BrowserSession:FilePath (default sessions.db; WAL, busy_timeout 5000, synchronous=FULL so a logout 204 survives a crash, owner-only mode on Unix; deleting sessions.db while stopped revokes every browser session - an operator kill switch); table browser_sessions (token_digest BLOB PK, credential_id, credential_binding, created_at/last_seen_at/absolute_expires_at as UTC Unix ms) with NOT stored: raw token, API key, any secret digest, Authorization header, cookie string, the keep-signed-in choice, a revocation flag (revocation is deletion), user agent or IP; PRAGMA user_version 0 -> create schema and set 1, 1 -> open, greater than 1 -> refuse to start naming the file; concurrency fails closed (logout linearizes at the validation read, touches monotonic, touch UPDATE re-checks expiry so it cannot resurrect a session, login supersede is one transaction, a FindAsync exception propagates and never authenticates while touch/cleanup failures are logged and do not change the outcome); NO caching - every cookie request reads the store so revocation is effective at the next request; bounded cleanup on startup (expired, then unknown credentials), opportunistically after a login at most every 5 minutes, and per session when found invalid; no hosted background service.

Defaults idle 60 min, absolute 12 h, touch granularity 60 s (fixed); a session is expired when now >= absolute_expires_at, or now >= created_at + AbsoluteTimeout(current configuration), or now >= last_seen_at + IdleTimeout(current configuration) - equality is expired; lowering AbsoluteTimeout shortens live sessions after a restart, raising it never lengthens them; absolute expiry NEVER slides; last_seen advances only when a request authenticated with the session, passed the CSRF gate, was not rate-limited and passed authorization (reached the endpoint), by a conditional UPDATE that re-checks idle and absolute expiry; requests rejected with 401/403/429 (incl. a CSRF rejection) never extend idle; polling requests keep an open tab alive up to the absolute lifetime so idle expiry protects closed/abandoned browsers, not an unattended open dashboard (a client-declared 'background request' header was rejected as advisory).

Cookie __Host-bops_session, HttpOnly, Secure ALWAYS (no switch to disable it in any environment), SameSite=Strict, Path=/, no Domain (required by the __Host- prefix); default a browser-session cookie (no Max-Age/Expires); keepSignedIn:true sets Max-Age = floor((absolute_expires_at - now)/1000), no Expires; deletion via Response.Cookies.Delete with identical attributes emitted (a) by DELETE /api/session for a cookie-authenticated or invalid-cookie request and (b) on every 401 challenge issued by the session scheme for a request that presented the cookie, never on other responses (a login response never carries two Set-Cookie lines for the name); server-side idle and absolute limits bound a cookie restored by a browser.

Three schemes: bops (default policy scheme forwarding all operations to the scheme chosen by ForwardDefaultSelector), bops-api-key (unchanged Bearer handler calling the authority) and bops-browser-session; fixed selector precedence decided from the request before any credential is checked: any Authorization header (even empty) -> Bearer; else a Cookie containing __Host-bops_session -> session; else Bearer (unchanged anonymous behavior): an explicitly supplied Authorization header ALWAYS decides - a valid Bearer wins over a cookie and an invalid/empty/non-Bearer value with a valid cookie is 401, NEVER a silent downgrade, and with Bearer the cookie is neither looked up, touched, deleted nor CSRF-checked; session handler steps (exactly one cookie pair, canonical token, row by digest, expiry, credential checks, principal + request feature) all failing with one constant message; challenge = 401 empty body plus the deletion cookie when a cookie was presented; authorization is untouched (the four policies apply identically whichever scheme produced the principal, no endpoint names a scheme) and the global limiter keys on NameIdentifier so Bearer and cookie share a bucket; pipeline order: UseExceptionHandler, UseAuthentication, UseBrowserSessionCsrf, UseRateLimiter, UseAuthorization, UseBrowserSessionTouch, endpoints.

Applies only when the effective authentication is the browser session AND the method is unsafe (anything except GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE); Bearer requests are never checked; the gate runs before rate limiting, authorization, model binding and any body read, so a rejected request has no effect and no body (e.g. a plugin archive) is consumed; both conditions required else 403 {"code":"csrf_rejected",...} with Cache-Control no-store, no cookie change and no idle extension: (a) exactly one X-bOps-Request field whose value is exactly the string '1'; (b) same origin against the CONFIGURED BrowserSession:Origins (canonical (scheme,host,port) tuples): if at least one Origin field exists there must be exactly one comma-free value, not 'null', parsing as http(s)://host[:port] with no user-info/path/query/fragment, whose tuple equals a trusted tuple and Referer is NOT consulted even if Origin fails; only if NO Origin field exists exactly one Referer field parsed as absolute http/https URL without user-info whose tuple (path/query ignored) equals a trusted tuple; neither = reject; canonical comparison: lower-case scheme, Uri.IdnHost lower-case ordinal host (no suffix, wildcard or DNS resolution), default-port equivalence; localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] are DIFFERENT origins; Host, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto and Forwarded are NEVER read; the UI must set no Referrer-Policy that makes the browser send Origin: null.

Login: anonymous, rate-limited, steps in order: origin gate always (whatever the scheme; failure = 403 csrf_rejected without reading the body or validating the key so a foreign origin learns nothing); Content-Type application/json (charset utf-8) else 415; at most 4,096 bytes enforced while reading else 413; shape {apiKey, keepSignedIn?} with source-generated metadata, unknown/duplicate members and trailing content disallowed, apiKey trimmed as Bearer trims, bad shape 400 (parse failures never log the payload or exception message); FindByPresentedKey no match = 401 invalid_credential (an already presented session stays valid and no cookie changes); the matched credential must hold viewer else 403 viewer_role_required; create token/digest/binding/row (if exactly one syntactically valid cookie value was presented its digest is the supersededDigest, inserted and deleted in one transaction; a failed login never revokes anything); opportunistic cleanup; 200 with {id, displayName, roles} and the cookie, never the key, token, digest or binding; login needs the origin gate because a same-site page on another localhost port could otherwise log the operator into a key of the page's choosing; there is no CORS policy and none may be added.

GET /api/session/me (viewer policy; same body) works with Bearer or cookie; expired/revoked/rotated/removed/malformed/absent = 401 with an empty body plus cookie deletion when a cookie was presented, never saying why and never containing key/token/digest/binding; DELETE /api/session requires an authenticated principal: browser session (CSRF passed) = delete row idempotently + deletion cookie + 204 (replay -> 401); Bearer = 204 with no server change and no Set-Cookie (a Bearer request NEVER revokes a browser session even if it also carried a cookie); unauthenticated/invalid cookie = 401 from the challenge.

Policy bops.session-login on POST /api/session only, partitioned by RemoteIpAddress (never a credential or body), fixed window 10 requests per minute, QueueLimit 0, counting every request reaching the middleware for this endpoint (successful or not) except those already rejected by the global CSRF gate; rejection 429 with Retry-After (whole seconds rounded up), Cache-Control no-store and body {"code":"rate_limited",...}; fixed constants not configuration; identical for valid and invalid keys with a uniform 401 so neither path enumerates credentials.

Additive BrowserSession section with invalid values failing startup (never clamped, eagerly validated): Origins (comma-separated scalar string so hierarchical configuration cannot merge array indices and silently retain an extra trusted origin; default http://localhost:4200; 1-8 entries of exact scheme://host[:port]; https, or http only for localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]; no duplicates after canonicalization), IdleTimeout (default 1 h; 5 min-1 day; whole seconds; <= AbsoluteTimeout), AbsoluteTimeout (default 12 h; 15 min-7 days), FilePath (default sessions.db); there is NO key to disable Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, the __Host- prefix or the CSRF gate; login-limit numbers, token size, touch granularity and cleanup interval are constants.

column5: The raw API key, the raw cookie value and the token bytes must not appear in any API response body/header (other than the login Set-Cookie), application or structured log, the audit log, exception messages, sessions.db, browser localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB, URLs or history, or Angular state after login completes (the digest and binding are not logged either); mechanisms: no request logging of bodies/Authorization/Cookie (any future request logging must exclude them); fixed messages for every AuthenticateResult.Fail and error body (no exception text on the login path); an explicit exception handler in EVERY environment as the outermost middleware (a problem body with no request data) so the Development developer exception page cannot render Cookie/Authorization into a body page script could read; log events carry no secrets (session created with credential id and persistent flag, login rejected category only, session revoked category: logout/superseded/expired/credential_changed/credential_removed); authentication events are host-channel logs not audit events (an audit-schema change is an Abstractions change needing its own decision).

AuthService state machine initializing/authenticated/unauthenticated/session-expired/unavailable with the key NEVER held (the token signal is removed; the key is a function argument dropped when the login request completes; the Login component clears the field whatever the outcome; no storage API called); boot GET /api/session/me (10 s timeout) via an app initializer so stores see the final status; 401 at boot = unauthenticated (no 'expired' message), status 0/429/502/503/504/5xx/timeout = unavailable with retry; login failure messages by status; the interceptor treats a request as a bOps API request iff its URL is relative and starts with /api/, NEVER sets Authorization, adds X-bOps-Request: 1 to unsafe bOps API requests, relies on same-origin fetch for the cookie, and is the ONE place turning a 401 received while authenticated into session-expired (idempotent); logout sends DELETE with the header and 204 or 401 means signed out, any other outcome stays authenticated with an error (the UI must not pretend the server session ended); pendingWatch is preserved across interceptor-first expiry and the selection cleared only on a deliberate sign-out.

The selected task is durable UI state in the dashboard URL (/dashboard?task=<uuid>; a task id is not a secret and every read is authorized server-side): written by selectTask/start/resume with replaceUrl, removed by clearSelection or a 404; read once on init after boot (canonical UUID that differs from the store selection -> selectTask(id), which fetches the task and starts the watch with expectedAttempt = snapshot.executionAttempt if Running; a malformed value is removed and ignored); terminal task shown without a watch; interrupted task watched with the Interrupted presentation; 404 shows the gone error and removes the parameter; the watch is a dashboard view (F5 elsewhere restores the session and that page, not a watch).

Threat to mitigation table: key theft from persistence, key in URL/history/logs, token theft by script (HttpOnly), token and binding at rest, API key guessable from the database, database write -> forged session, session fixation, cross-site and same-site CSRF, cross-origin use (no CORS), login CSRF, brute force (10/min + global limiter + uniform 401), replay after logout, key removal/rotation, stale or escalated privileges, session/Bearer authority divergence, unlimited lifetime, persistent cookie outliving the session, database growth, Bearer regression, Bearer->cookie downgrade, cookie tossing, Host-header spoofing, secret logging, store unavailable; residual risks: the shared localhost cookie jar across ports (CSRF blocked, token disclosure to a malicious local listener not) and XSS in the UI (acts as the operator while the session lives but can no longer read the long-lived key).

Normative 30-row matrix of Authorization/cookie/method/header combinations and their effective scheme and result (valid Bearer wins; invalid Bearer with valid cookie = 401 no downgrade; cookie + unsafe method needs valid origin; missing/foreign/null/malformed Origin = 403; Referer fallback only without Origin; HEAD/OPTIONS exempt; expired/revoked/removed/malformed cookie = 401 with deletion; login origin gate/415/401/200/429; logout via session 204, via Bearer 204 without touching the session; secret-reassignment cases D/E).

Implementation test obligations: session creation, rate limiting, every row of §17, Bearer regression, expiry with a fake clock, revocation, Bearer equivalence (cases D/E), CSRF for each unsafe method incl. plugin lifecycle and settings mutations, persistence, secret leakage scans, configuration validation, UI tests, E2E-8 Playwright flow (Chromium and Firefox, traces/video/HAR off because they record the cookie) and manual cookie-attribute evidence with the value redacted.

Additive public contract (session endpoints, the bops-browser-session scheme, the BrowserSession section, sessions.db) with no change for Bearer clients; unsafe cookie-authenticated requests need X-bOps-Request: 1 and a configured origin and the UI must be opened at exactly a configured origin (not 127.0.0.1:4200); every unhandled exception yields a problem body without request data in every environment; residual risks: shared localhost cookie jar, open polling tab until the absolute limit, in-flight requests complete after logout, rotated-key rows persist unusable until presented or expired, key/role changes still need a host restart exactly as for Bearer.

column5: Accepted 2026-10-05 (operator decision after independent review PASS, blockers 0, N-1..N-13 incorporated, operator decisions A-E); amends ADR-0030 §1/§3 (which roles a delegation requires; what the root is derived from), ADR-0031 §1/§5 (the table applies to the roles the request requires; 'a role with no profile denies delegation' becomes 'a REQUIRED role') and ADR-0018 (two read-only endpoints); closes the ADR-0042 HARDEN-11 gap (typed limitation metadata) and decides its FindingsOf follow-up; implemented and merged via PR #77; N-1, N-5 and N-7 were mandatory Phase-1 obligations.

Verified baseline: the fixed four-role pipeline and RiskCap(Read) for all but Remediation; the root derivation needed every role profile (summing steps/tokens/durations) so a diagnosis-only request still needed a mutation-capable Remediation/Verification grant (primary defect F-14); per-step enforcement already holds read-only roles to Read (non-Read tool without a Skill scope refused, tool outside AllowedTools refused, Critical refused); the policy loader refuses a whole delegation section when any part is malformed and hosts fall back to AllForbidden; a policy file without defaults forbids every risk level (S3), so a delegation-only generated file would forbid all tools; GetAvailableManifests lists only available tools; CapabilityManifest.InputSchema was declared but never read; the API start binder accepted duplicate JSON keys; the Delegations UI took free-text Skill/Capability and sent no input; FindingsOf accepted duplicate keys and threw only on later access; EvidenceOf typed no failed/denied/shortened evidence; TaskResume refuses Delegated origin first; the plan approval provider builds the view from PlanApprovalRequest.

column5: The request shape is ONE boolean: whether DelegationRequest.Remediation is set (for a stored run DelegationRun.Remediation) and nothing else contributes (not profiles, model, packages, Skills, plugins, API/CLI/UI or configuration); diagnosis-only = Discovery + Diagnostic required, Remediation and Verification not required; remediation (DryRun true or false) = all four required; ONE canonical selector RequiredRoles(shape) owned by the runtime's role-requirement table, called by the reducer, runner and readiness evaluator (API/CLI call the evaluator, the UI renders the API answer; none carries its own role table); invariants: subset of the pipeline in pipeline order, total and pure, Discovery and Diagnostic always present, Remediation ∈ Required ⇔ Verification ∈ Required ⇔ remediation shape; a NOT-required role needs no profile, its profile is not looked up, contributes nothing to the root, receives no budget reservation and never begins (an absent or valid profile for it can neither block nor widen the run; a malformed one may make the whole policy fail to load under the existing fail-closed loader); a remediation request is unchanged and fail-closed (all four profiles must satisfy the ADR-0031 table, PrepareCheckAsync runs before any model call, a missing or unusable R/V profile still ends the run Denied before Discovery); a dry run stays a four-role remediation shape; BeginRoleAsync refuses a role not in RequiredRoles(stored shape) (the run ends Failed 'role not required by this request', audited) as defence in depth.

Root(request, profiles, now) = Narrow_request(Build({profile(r): r ∈ RequiredRoles(shape)})) where Build is the existing construction (union of sets, highest capped risk and blast radius, saturating SUM of steps/tokens/durations, deadline now+Σduration); the per-role start proof iterates RequiredRoles only; the diagnosis-only root additionally has Skills and Capabilities FORCED EMPTY (it never prepares a Capability so removing the authority is a pure reduction): root MaxRisk <= Read, tools only the union of D/D, budgets the sums of D/D, and R/V profiles can never widen anything nor make the root fail; the remediation root is exactly today's four-role construction with no dimension relaxed; the root is persisted (DelegationRun.RootEnvelope) and never re-derived on resume (a pre-ADR stored run keeps its four-role root and its stored request decides whether later roles begin, so a stored diagnosis-only run never begins Remediation, and configuration changes can never turn a diagnosis into a remediation); child ⊆ parent ∩ profile ∩ request and every ADR-0031 cell are unchanged for every role that runs.

PROPERTY R (read-only diagnosis): for every request with Remediation == null no tool whose manifest risk exceeds Read is executed by the run, whatever the profiles contain (mutation tool names included), whatever names appear in request/profile sets, whatever the model proposes and whatever tools packages register later; the boundary is the envelope and the role risk cap, not the UI, in layers each sufficient for the step path: selector (only D/D begin + BeginRoleAsync guard); root (MaxRisk <= Read, no Skill/Capability); reduction (min(parent, profile, request, RiskCap(role)), RiskCap Read for both); per-step enforcement (CheckStep before IPolicyEngine.Evaluate refuses any non-Read tool without a Skill scope and any tool above min(envelope.MaxRisk, RiskCap), audited Forbidden 'Authority envelope:'; two real paths both refuse before policy and before ExecuteAsync - provider/model path may reject a never-offered tool earlier as unknown, direct/fake-model path is refused by CheckStep); no preparation (the runner never calls PrepareDelegatedSkillAsync for a diagnosis-only run); new packages (a later Read tool is allowed only if its exact name is in the envelope, anything else is refused; no wildcard, category or dynamic grant); generated read-only profiles are a stronger safe default, NOT the boundary.

DelegationSectionParser and the hosts' AllForbidden fallback are UNCHANGED: one malformed delegation profile - used by this request or not - invalidates the whole policy.yaml (S3; a half-loaded policy would be more permissive than what the operator wrote) so partial load is rejected and the remedy for a malformed unused profile is to fix or delete it; each host retains a policy load state NoFile (built-in SafeDefault) | Loaded | LoadFailed next to LoadedPolicy (the evaluator-facing three-valued type lives in bOps.Runtime; the loader's message stays host-side, kept for the host log and the local CLI and never sent over HTTP); each host logs the absolute resolved policy path and load state at start without logging contents; table: not-required roles are notRequired whether absent, valid or (policy LoadFailed) ; a required role is missing (absent), malformed (LoadFailed, profile for another role, or a well-formed profile the reducer refuses, with the reducer's dimension) or ready; the real start is Denied on Profile at the first non-ready required role; diagnosis-only with no Remediation/Verification profile is notRequired and never blocks.

column2: Decision §5 readiness is a runtime function
column5: A public readiness evaluator in bOps.Runtime (not Abstractions) takes the profile source, the policy load state, the request shape and an instant and is the ONLY thing API and CLI call: required = RequiredRoles(shape); per pipeline role notRequired / missing / malformed (LoadFailed, or profile for another role); for required roles with profiles it builds the §2 root and applies the reducer's own per-role step with a non-narrowing synthetic request (denied -> malformed with the reducer's dimension and reason, granted -> ready); the reducer is refactored so ONE loop produces per-role results and DeriveRootAttributed is 'the first non-granted role in pipeline order' (one reduction implementation, two projections; attribution on multi-fault inputs is deterministic pipeline order while grant stays grant and deny stays deny); role-independence lemma (each required role's state is its own); PROPERTY P5: readiness ready ⇔ DeriveRootAttributed grants for any request of that shape with non-narrowing authority, and a missing/malformed role makes the start Denied on that role with the same dimension (and same reason text for profile_missing and reduction_denied; for policy_load_failed the start reports the profile_missing text); what readiness does NOT evaluate (stated so P5 is not over-claimed): time races, a maintenance window not yet open, configuration changes after host start, request narrowing, the named change (Skill/Capability/target/environment is checked by PrepareCheckAsync at start), tool availability; operator decision E: readiness is profile / role-infrastructure readiness for a request SHAPE, never specific-request executability ('ready' = the required role profiles are usable for this type of delegation, not that a change is executable).

GET /api/delegations/readiness?remediation=false|true (default false; anything else 400 with a fixed message; Viewer; safe, no audit event, Cache-Control no-store, normal rate limiting): response {remediation, ready, policy noFile|loaded|loadFailed, roles (EXACTLY four entries in pipeline order with role, state, dimension, reasonCode, reason), profileDriftCount, evaluatedAtUtc}; EXACTLY four public states ready|missing|malformed|notRequired (operator decision B; malformed = present but not usable, UI label 'Not usable'); reasonCode is the stable snake_case machine field (ready, not_required, profile_missing, policy_load_failed, profile_for_other_role, reduction_denied); the set may grow and an unknown reasonCode is treated by clients as NOT ready (never fail open); reason is bounded (<=500) English text (the reducer's denial text for reduction_denied; for policy_load_failed the fixed 'policy.yaml could not be loaded; delegation is off until it is fixed (see the host log)' - the loader message is never sent over HTTP); ready == every role not notRequired is ready, clients use the field and never recompute it; the missing text is '{role} role: no usable profile is configured.' for readiness AND start ('usable' because start cannot tell absent from load-failed); errors 401/403/429/400 and problem responses never mention profiles.

Twelve deterministic example rows M1-M12 (fresh install, read-only D/D setup, all-four valid, policy load failure, reducer refusals such as Diagnostic maxTokens 0, Remediation maxRisk read, Discovery tools []) with the same non-ready role/dimension at real start (P5).

column5: GET /api/skills: additive, Viewer, safe, no-store, reads ISkillRegistry.GetAvailableSkills() ONLY (activated Skills; nothing from disabled/failed/uninstalled plugins and no plugin internals - no assembly, path, manifest file, signature or entitlement detail); Skill fields exactly skillId, package (host-stamped), trust (a Skill has no version or description - none is invented); Capability fields name, version, description, risk, supportsDryRun and inputSchema (CapabilityManifest.InputSchema projected field-for-field from ToolParameter in manifest order, null where absent); OutputSchema, RequiredPermissions, Timeout, Verification and RollbackDescription omitted; ordinal ordering; empty catalog = 200 with skills [].

The UI renders the form from inputSchema ONLY (no second schema), never clamping/trimming/coercing client-side; SERVER VALIDATION IS AUTHORITATIVE: a runtime-owned validator (the existing ValidateArguments/ViolatedConstraint lifted out of AgentRunner so tool arguments and capability input share one implementation) validates CapabilityRequest.Input against CapabilityManifest.InputSchema (unknown names rejected, required present and non-null, JSON-native type, AllowedValues, Minimum/Maximum, MinLength/MaxLength, MinItems/MaxItems; no clamping, no coercion) BEFORE Capability code in the shared preparation path for delegated AND non-delegated preparation (operator decision D: InputSchema is authoritative wherever that Capability is invoked - an intentional additive fail-closed tightening); a failure is a preparation Failed with a validation reason and a SkillRunAuditEvent refusal; it also runs at delegation start before any model call (API 400, CLI exit 1, no run created) and again in PrepareCheckAsync; MANDATORY (N-7): SkillRegistry validates every InputSchema at registration and refuses a blank or duplicate (ordinal) parameter name, an Enum with empty AllowedValues and every constraint inconsistency ToolRegistry refuses (wrong-type constraint, non-finite bound, negative length, minimum above maximum) as a deterministic bounded registration failure - no Capability with an invalid schema becomes active; SENSITIVE parameters (N-12): the submitted value of a Sensitive parameter never appears in any validation error, log, audit diagnostic, API/CLI/UI error (messages name the parameter and violated constraint only), while Capability input is persisted as PLAIN JSON in the delegation store like the rest of the request (no encrypted secret storage is introduced); API failure bodies 400 {message, code: capability_input_invalid|unknown_capability|malformed_json, parameter}.

Mapping of ToolParameterType to UI control and JSON value (String text/password-when-sensitive, Path, Duration, Enum select, Integer, Number, Boolean three-state, PathList list editor); optional empty fields omitted, never sent as '' or null; 'This capability takes no input.' for an empty schema.

column2: Decision §9.3 raw JSON and strict binding
column5: Raw JSON fallback only behind an explicit collapsed 'Advanced: edit as JSON' control with the SAME client checks and the SAME server validator (not a second unrestricted path); POST /api/delegations is bound with strict JSON (AllowDuplicateProperties = false) so a duplicate key anywhere including input is 400 malformed_json and never first- or last-wins, scoped to duplicate-key rejection only (no change to casing, unknown-member behavior or numeric binding); the CLI --input is parsed with the same strict options; the Angular raw-JSON mode detects duplicate keys BEFORE ordinary JSON.parse erases them and never silently normalizes.

The UI selects Skill then Capability from GET /api/skills (no free-text field in the ordinary form), the manifest drives the form and shows risk and supportsDryRun (dry-run disabled when unsupported); the API stays fail-closed for handcrafted clients (unknown pair = 400 unknown_capability, runtime Resolve still refuses at preparation); a catalog changing between load and submit fails safely (400 or the runner re-check or preparation - never running stale input) and the UI re-fetches the catalog after unknown_capability/capability_input_invalid.

bops delegate profiles init --read-only [--write [--overwrite]]: --read-only is MANDATORY (no other generation mode exists so it can never be mistaken for one that grants mutation; without it a usage error); default PRINTS the YAML to stdout with the resolved absolute policy path on stderr (the review step), never writes; --write writes the whole file to the policy path the CLI resolves for every other command (Policy:FilePath, default policy.yaml), atomically (temp file + create-new move; a file appearing in between fails and is left untouched), printing the absolute path and reminding the API reads the file only at start; never prints or logs an existing file's contents; an existing file is NEVER overwritten silently (--write without --overwrite refuses with exit 1, prints the delegation fragment for manual merge); bOps NEVER merges YAML (a structural merge cannot preserve comments/ordering/intent nor be proven not to add authority); --overwrite (only with --write) replaces an existing file ONLY if ALL hold: it loads via PolicyConfigLoader; its non-delegation configuration equals the generator's safe baseline (defaults equal SafeDefault; no tools/packages/skills entries); it configures no Remediation and no Verification profile; its Discovery/Diagnostic profiles equal the generator-owned defaults in every authority dimension except the tools list (only drift refreshed); the file is re-read and conditions re-checked immediately before replacement; the replacement preserves restrictive permissions/ACL where supported - otherwise refuse (exit 1), name the first failed condition, leave the file untouched, print the fragment; --overwrite exists only to refresh the tool list of a previously generated read-only file and can never discard a stricter default, tool override, package ceiling, Skill rule, narrowed budget or mutation grant; Before HARDEN-13 Settings writes persisted the provider/profile/credential but IChatModel, AgentRunner, DelegationRunner and launchers were singletons rooted in one model resolved once, so every change needed a restart; TaskState and DelegationRun persisted no provider configuration so a resume used whatever model the new process built; ExtraParameters persisted but controlled nothing (never effective, to be labelled persistedOnly, not live nor restart-required); ADR-0039 owns one attempt per adapter call and the runtime retry loop (only Transient, RateLimited, Timeout, Unreachable retry); ModelCallRecord/AuditEvent had no pinned primary, fallback ordinal or per-provider attempt, and a fallback must never disappear behind one successful final event.
column12: Baseline description; the resulting rules are in Decision.

column5: A Settings change to provider, model, endpoint or tool-calling capability must affect a SUBSEQUENTLY started execution without restart and must not change an execution in progress; a credential change is the deliberate exception and must affect the NEXT model attempt even in an admitted execution (rotation may revoke a compromised key); fallback must be explicitly configured, ordered, bounded and host-owned; the shipped OpenRouter / openrouter/free bootstrap stays intentionally non-deterministic and must never be presented as suitable for reproducible troubleshooting or remediation.

Persisted configuration (what Settings and configuration sources store, possibly shadowed by an environment override), effective configuration (ONE immutable validated EffectiveProviderConfiguration published by the API host: primary + ordered fallback chain, field provenance, monotonic generation, safe credential source/availability metadata, no credential value or historical credential reference; one atomic reference is the only source a new execution reads) and pinned execution configuration (the safe durable projection of one effective generation plus the execution's sticky fallback ordinal; non-secret provider and request configuration only; belongs to one top-level durable execution and never follows later Settings changes; credentials deliberately not pinned); the Settings API returns persisted values, effective primary/fallback descriptors, generation, per-field source (environment|settings|default) and whether a persisted value is shadowed, credential presence and source only (never plaintext, hash or historical version), whether a mutation was published or persisted-but-shadowed; the UI must not call a shadowed value 'active'.

An API-host singleton ProviderConfigurationCoordinator (internal host service, not Runtime, not plugin SDK) owns mutations and publication: short write gate; complete proposed state from one settings revision and one vault revision; validate without any provider network call; persist atomically; build the effective non-secret configuration and credential availability metadata; publish by ONE atomic reference replacement incrementing the generation; release the gate; a start reads the reference exactly once (wholly A or wholly B, never a mixed tuple; the credential is outside the tuple); no gate is held while building prompts, waiting for approval, calling a provider or running a task; SettingsStore gains a revision and in-process writer serialization (stale writes return conflict); the coordinator is the only API write path to either provider store while running; CLI vault rotation stays an offline operation requiring the API stopped; persistence precedes publication (failure = nothing published; a crash between rebuilds the snapshot deterministically at startup; no silent rollback); a credential-only mutation atomically replaces/removes the vault value and refreshes presence/source without rewriting an execution pin; a combined profile-and-key operation is serialized, validated, persisted before publication and never routes one provider's key to another.

If the real ModelProvider__Provider variable is set the environment owns the primary: the whole merged ModelProvider block is effective, Settings primary selection/profile is not consulted and Settings writes are persisted but reported shadowed (no generation increment unless they also change an unshadowed fallback); otherwise Settings selects provider/profile and a real environment variable for an individual field (BaseUrl, Model, SupportsNativeToolCalling, RequestTimeout) overrides only that field (one atomic tuple even with differently-sourced fields); THE BLOCK-LEVEL ModelProvider:ApiKeySecret IS PROVIDER-BOUND: it belongs ONLY to ConfiguredPrimaryProviderId (the merged IConfiguration value of ModelProvider:Provider after ordinary configuration/environment precedence and BEFORE any Settings active-provider selection) and for a candidate P: if P == ConfiguredPrimaryProviderId the secret reference is resolved first and a non-empty result shadows that provider's vault entry (null/empty falls back to P's current vault entry); if P != ConfiguredPrimaryProviderId the block-level ApiKeySecret is categorically ineligible and never read - only P's own provider-keyed vault credential is used; this applies equally to a Settings-selected active provider, every fallback candidate and every resumed execution (a credential of provider A is never sent to provider B; this NARROWS ADR-0029's 'effective active provider' wording; environment-only deployments are unchanged); the Settings view reports per provider whether a usable credential exists and its source (environment only for ConfiguredPrimaryProviderId, otherwise vault or none), never shows B using A's credential and shows B as persisted/shadowed when an environment override makes A effective; environment fallback entries, when present, own the whole ordered list, else the Settings list, else the shipped empty default; non-secret precedence is evaluated at every publication, credential precedence for the pinned provider at every attempt; environment variables are not polled (a process-environment change needs a reload/restart) while vault rotation/removal is visible to the next attempt.

column2: Decision §8 pinning scope and model lifetime
column5: The execution scope is the largest durable aggregate representing one operator objective - one ordinary TaskState, or one complete DelegationRun (Discovery, Diagnostic, the approval wait, Remediation, Verification, reconciliation and every role task); never a model call, an AgentRunner invocation, a role or an execution attempt (a role scope would let Discovery and Diagnostic disagree; an attempt scope would let Resume change the model; a call scope is the defect); at admission an internal host IExecutionChatModelFactory receives one effective non-secret snapshot and returns one execution-scoped IChatModel that owns the pinned candidate descriptors and uses a narrow host-owned current-credential resolver at each provider attempt; the host builds an execution-scoped AgentRunner (and one execution-scoped DelegationRunner over that runner for delegation); Runtime still sees exactly one IChatModel and resolves no services, provider ids, profiles or secrets; adapters must not capture a credential for their whole execution lifetime (the credential is bound per attempt); existing public AgentRunner(IChatModel,...)/IChatModel contracts stay usable by tests and non-API hosts.

column2: Decision §9 durable pin and late-bound credentials
column5: TaskState and DelegationRun gain an additive optional PinnedProviderConfiguration (old records: the first accepted resume captures the then-effective snapshot, AUDITS that migration, persists it before any model call and stays pinned); the durable projection contains only safe data (schema version, generation, primary and ordered fallback provider ids, base URLs, requested models, native-tool flags, request timeouts, relevant non-secret first-party request configuration - ExtraParameters stays persisted-only - field provenance, a snapshot hash and the current sticky fallback ordinal); NO credential plaintext, authorization header, credential hash, historical secret version or correlation identifier is stored in task, delegation, audit or Settings data; credentials are late-bound for EVERY model attempt from ADR-0029's existing authority for the pinned candidate provider and live only in attempt memory (rotation is immediately effective in new and running executions - preserving a rotated key for reproducibility would be a security defect); after restart Resume reconstructs the exact pinned non-secret configuration and resolves the current credential only when an attempt needs it; if the pinned provider package cannot instantiate the safe configuration or the pinned candidate's current credential is unavailable, Resume or the next attempt FAILS explicitly - it never substitutes current Settings and never needs a historical credential; an invalid current credential yields Authentication and cannot trigger fallback; scenarios: a running A/X task is unaffected by a change to B/Y (the next task pins B/Y); a resume after a model failure reuses the snapshot and sticky ordinal; a delegation keeps its snapshot across approval waits and resumes; key rotation applies to the next attempt on the same provider/model; key removal fails the next required attempt explicitly (missing credentials are not transient and cannot activate fallback).

Operator decision: OpenRouter / openrouter/free is the shared API and CLI bootstrap default - a zero-cost getting-started/evaluation/non-critical mode requiring an OpenRouter API key, intentionally a router alias whose ACTUAL model can change on every call and must stay visible through the existing requested/actual model-call and audit information; bOps must never imply it is deterministic; documentation and Settings must recommend an explicitly selected specific model for important troubleshooting, reproducible analysis and especially remediation and Settings displays 'The actual model may change on every call; not recommended for troubleshooting sessions.'; router selection happens inside a provider and the fallback chain is an administrator-owned cross-candidate recovery policy - the two must not share a name; Getting Started/operator documentation must state the key requirement, how to configure it in Settings, the non-determinism, the recommendation and that audit exposes the actual model when reported; C-20 is mitigated by disclosure, actual-model visibility, easy selection and the recommendation, not by making the bootstrap deterministic.

Canonical names: fallback chain, fallback candidate, FallbackChatModel ('router' refers only to router-mode provider behavior); configuration ModelProvider:Fallbacks is an explicit ORDERED list of already-registered providers with non-blank models (no secrets; endpoint and tool capability only from that provider's own pinned profile), at most THREE entries, duplicates and the primary tuple rejected, no cycle, discovery, implicit vendor or health-based insertion; empty or absent disables fallback; FallbackChatModel (bOps.Hosting) implements one IChatModel for the pinned primary and chain, is execution-scoped and serial and owns ONLY candidate selection and sticky state - AgentRunner stays the single owner of same-provider retry (attempt count, backoff, Retry-After, ModelCallBudget, ModelRetryDecision) and no retry policy moves into adapters; a narrow provider-neutral routing directive on ModelProtocolException (continue same candidate / advance / chain exhausted) plus a stable logical call id carries the handshake, preferring an internal contract and forbidding AsyncLocal service location or ambient mutable state; sequence: primary attempts 1..N, then fallback ordinal 1 attempts 1..N, ... stopping at success, a forbidden failure, exhausted chain, global budget or deadline, with an absolute ceiling of N × (1 + fallback count) and no candidate revisited; no reset of ModelCallBudget, attempt deadline, token/step budget or role budget on transition; a fallback transition does not wait for the failed provider's Retry-After but must leave MinimumModelAttemptWindow; handoff: AttemptsExhausted or RetryAfterExceedsLimit on an allowed kind advances if another candidate exists and the budget permits; BudgetExhausted stays terminal; a non-allowed kind is terminal regardless; ProviderAttempt (within a candidate) and FallbackOrdinal (0 primary, 1.. fallbacks) are two independent counters; a fallback candidate with no usable current credential fails as Authentication and terminates the logical call (no skipping to a later candidate, no foreign credential, no return to an earlier candidate, ordinal stays advanced); admission requires only a usable PRIMARY credential (a fallback credential may be a readiness warning, never a block; no background health checking); fallback is permitted ONLY after the candidate exhausted its same-provider retries with Transient, RateLimited, Timeout or Unreachable and forbidden for Authentication, QuotaExceeded, InvalidRequest, ContextOverflow, MalformedResponse and Unknown; future enum values default to forbidden until an ADR explicitly allows them; no HTTP status is interpreted by the chain.

Fallback is sticky for the EXECUTION SCOPE: on a candidate transition the later ordinal becomes the starting candidate for all subsequent calls in that task or delegated run, persisted before the next candidate is invoked; a later transient exhaustion may advance again but the execution never moves backward; a new task starts again from its newly effective primary (per-call stickiness would oscillate; process-global stickiness would leak one task's outage into unrelated tasks).

Save-time validation is local and deterministic: provider ids registered with exact canonical casing (validated against the registry with the existing case-insensitive semantics and stored in canonical spelling), model non-blank and bounded, BaseUrl an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URI, supported non-secret parameters valid, primary and fallback tuples unique and the chain bounded, a candidate newly activated or added to a chain that requires a credential has one currently resolvable through its own provider-scoped authority, the provider package can construct the adapter from the proposal; no live network request (an offline provider is accepted and fails at execution as Unreachable; a 401 is Authentication and never falls back); an inactive profile may be stored without a credential but cannot be newly activated or added to the chain until its credential is present; explicit removal of a credential is ALWAYS allowed as a security revocation (availability false immediately, new admission and the next attempt fail explicitly, the old value not retained); a rejected mutation never replaces the published generation and the system never silently keeps using the preceding configuration or credential while claiming the new state is active.

Every provider attempt remains one ModelCallRecord and one ModelCallAuditEvent with existing fields keeping their meaning (Provider = the candidate actually called, RequestedModel/Model, ActualModel as reported); additive optional fields PrimaryProvider, PrimaryModel, FallbackOrdinal, ProviderAttempt, ConfigurationGeneration and safe snapshot hash; a fallback transition is a new append-only ModelRetryDecision value Fallback (no renumbering) so the audit distinguishes Retry, Fallback, AttemptsExhausted and BudgetExhausted; no separate ActualProvider field (Provider already is the actual candidate; for router mode it is OpenRouter and ActualModel the provider-reported upstream model - bOps does not guess an upstream vendor); no event or record contains a secret value, historical version, credential correlation id, hash, header or Authorization data; configuration mutation audit records the resulting generation and effective-or-shadowed, never the value.

Controls: unconfigured-provider switch blocked by registry validation before publication; secret cross-routing blocked by the candidate-scoped resolver and the provider-bound ApiKeySecret; TOCTOU closed by the coordinator gate and one immutable publication (credential rotation independently atomic in the vault); no fallback after authentication/permanent failure (four-kind allow-list, future kinds fail closed); no loops (bounded ordered list, duplicate rejection, monotonic sticky ordinal); stale UI avoided via persisted/effective/pinned terminology; partial application avoided via complete-proposal validate/persist/publish; no API key in task/audit snapshot; authority and task semantics unchanged (snapshot selection is host composition only); retry multiplication bounded (max three fallbacks, per-candidate cap, one global budget); a delegation keeps one durable snapshot across approval waits; a malicious provider's routing directive can only advance within the host-pinned chain and cannot make a forbidden kind retryable.

Fifteen behavioral tests (live switch without restart, running task unaffected, key rotation/removal on an active execution, environment precedence and shadowing, no mixed tuple, fallback after exhaustion with audited attempts, timeout/unreachable fallback, no fallback for the six forbidden kinds, deterministic sticky non-cycling order, in-flight immutability, ordinary and delegated resume reconstructing the pin and refusing when unavailable, the bootstrap disclosure, explicit-model recommendation, stale writes conflict) and security regressions A-H with fake providers recording the credential they receive (Settings-selected provider never receives the block-level key; fallback isolation; environment primary override binding; missing fallback credential = Authentication; RetryAfterExceedsLimit advances; BudgetExhausted does not; audit transitions distinguishable; provenance never shows B using A's credential) plus deterministic E2E gates.

column5: Direct resume of a delegated role TaskState is refused or inherits the owning DelegationRun pin (never current Settings as a legacy ordinary task); the pin is persisted atomically with TaskState/DelegationRun admission before the first model call; the snapshot hash excludes the mutable sticky ordinal; credentials stay outside the immutable hash; a legacy unpinned resume is explicitly identified, audited and surfaced; an invalid or missing persisted provider on resume fails closed and an invalid persisted fallback at startup is an explicit visible state, never a silent drop; provider-id canonical casing is documented consistently with the case-insensitive registry.

Rejected: reloading the process-global singleton; making every model transient; resolving current Settings before every call; pinning per role or attempt; resolving endpoint/non-secret configuration live with the credential; persisting credential plaintext or an unkeyed hash; resuming under current Settings; fallback on all failures or on status codes; per-call or process-global stickiness; automatic discovery, health routing, cheapest-provider selection or vendor scoring.

Settings changes are live for subsequently admitted executions; active work keeps deterministic non-secret configuration across calls, approvals and resumes while key rotation/removal takes effect on the next attempt; the host gains the coordinator, execution factory, per-attempt credential resolution and FallbackChatModel with Runtime still vendor-agnostic and constructed with one model; additive optional fields on TaskState, DelegationRun and call/audit records (a routing directive may need an additive Abstractions type if an internal equivalent cannot preserve the one-attempt audit contract); fallback disabled by an empty list and no provider implicit; the disclosed non-deterministic bootstrap default stays; an exact resume can fail closed when the pinned package, configuration or current credential is unavailable (intentionally safer than silent substitution); acceptance and completion recorded (PR #82/#83).
