column5: ADR-0038 (plan/replan expose no native tools; first call wins and later calls persist as UnexecutedToolCalls), ADR-0039 (classification, bounded retry accounting, one corrective re-ask), ADR-0040 (ordinary Failed tasks stay resumable), ADR-0042/ADR-0014 HARDEN-8 (evidence persistence, bounded history, EvidenceRead) and ADR-0045 (execution-pinned provider configuration) remain unchanged.

ExpectedTool is a plan INTENTION, never a concrete call and never a source of arguments (the executor model still emits the actual ModelToolCall; policy, entitlement, approval, validation, execution and verification stay runtime-owned); for a normal executable step StepToolView = AuthorizedToolView ∩ exact(CurrentPlannedStep.ExpectedTool) where AuthorizedToolView is the existing ToolViewFor(delegation): exactly ONE native tool schema, ExpectedTool may only narrow authority never widen it, ordinal matching, and a missing/unavailable/unknown/unauthorized expected tool NEVER falls back to the complete catalog; the step prompt states that the single offered tool is the current plan step's tool to be invoked at most once (choosing another operational tool belongs to replanning, not executor-side search).

For newly produced plans every non-empty step is executable and must name a non-empty canonical expectedTool (an empty steps array means no further tool execution is planned); a persisted legacy plan or a candidate/current step without a usable authorized expectedTool must not expose the full catalog and the runtime requires replanning before another operational tool can execute; if the current plan has no remaining executable steps the runtime replans before executing another operational tool (a valid replan may be empty and the following call has no native tools and can produce the final answer).

ADR-0038 unchanged: execute only the first emitted call, persist later calls in UnexecutedToolCalls, preserve provider-valid history with not-executed results, and spend no corrective model call solely because multiple calls were emitted.

With Pcurrent the last accepted plan: ask for candidate Pc1; valid = commit; malformed or semantically unusable = the existing single corrective re-ask; valid Pc2 = commit; if Pc2 is still invalid do NOT create or append an empty replacement plan, keep Pcurrent as the last persisted accepted plan, retain model-call records, audit and token accounting and end the current execution attempt Failed through the existing model-failure terminal path with ModelFailureKind.MalformedResponse (ordinary tasks remain resumable, ADR-0040); a failed candidate never increments accepted plan history and never resets the cursor; preserving Pcurrent is for durable state/resume and does not authorize continuing indefinitely on a stale plan in the same attempt.
column12: Supersedes the empty-plan degradation of ADR-0014 for replans (and for the initial plan by AF-PLAN-01).

column5: Initial planning state machine not redesigned here (but subsequent execution may never regain the full catalog because routing information is absent); no duplicate suppression is added (residual duplication measured later); no Evidence Store, evidence-search API or new compaction (HARDEN-8 stays authoritative: complete Output persisted, history compactable, EvidenceRead/v1 bounded range reads, resume rebuilds from persisted state); no manual or automatic model selection by planner/replanner/executor/final response.

column2: Implementation boundary, validation, rejected alternatives, compatibility
column5: Local to AgentRunner step-view/replan control flow with no new planner service, provider-specific branch, persistence subsystem, public tool or evidence abstraction; validation by existing suites plus a real local-model run; rejected: keeping all tools visible, expected tool plus related-tool group, re-ask solely because of multiple calls, a failed replan becoming an empty plan, continuing indefinitely on the old plan, duplicate suppression now, model-per-role routing now, a new Evidence Store now; compatibility: no provider wire-format, manifest, persistence or status change and unusable routing fails closed through replanning.
column12: Packet scope and compatibility statements of a landed change.

column5: The single-ExpectedTool rule governs OPERATIONAL authority; internal control-plane functions may coexist because they grant no operational authority and execute no package operation: the only control function is runtime.evidence_read (typed arguments step, source, offset, length; read-only; the current task taken from the runtime context never from the model), declared by the runtime, never in the ToolRegistry, passing no policy/entitlement/approval, with the runtime. namespace reserved so no package can register a tool in it, offered beside the step tool only when persisted evidence exceeds MaxObservationCharacters; a control read never completes a planned step, never advances the cursor and spends neither the semantic correction nor the ADR-0047 argument correction, is audited as EvidenceReadAuditEvent, counts against the existing four-read limit and writes no PlanStep; same-turn rule: a response carrying a control read gets the read served and no other call of that response executes (each other call id answered Not executed, the model asked again with the evidence) so at most one operational execution per model turn is preserved; an unrecognised runtime.* name is a control protocol error (audited Malformed), never a package tool or final prose; the legacy EvidenceRead/v1 text directive converges on the same handler.
column12: Interacts with ADR-0052 evidence cleanup (E-EVID): exhausting the local read budget no longer fails the task.

column2: Amendment PRE-3B1: offered control views and terminal artifacts
column5: A control function is valid only when advertised in the model-call control view of that turn; a runtime.evidence_read call that was not offered is a control protocol error NotOffered (nothing read, no step written, cursor unmoved, no correction spent); runtime control/tool protocol artifacts (<tool_call>/<function=> markup or a serialized {name, arguments} call object as the WHOLE shape) are not valid user-facing terminal responses: the model gets one bounded terminal correction and if the artifact persists the task FAILS rather than completes; prose that merely mentions a function name is unaffected.

column2: Amendment AF-05H: a premature final replans
column5: A final candidate (a reply with no tool call) is accepted directly ONLY when the current plan revision has no unresolved executable step (the persisted PlannedStepPosition fold, after skipping steps whose conditions deterministically settle, has its cursor at or past the end; an empty or fully consumed plan completes as before); otherwise the reply is NOT completion: the paid call is recorded once on a runtime-authored non-tool bookkeeping step ('Premature final response; plan re-evaluation required') carrying the call's ModelCalls, a runtime-authored observation naming only the unresolved planned positions and catalog-validated tool names, no tool call/result/planned-step index (never evidence, never addressable, never a limitation, never a final-response step, consumes no planned step but counts as one step of the attempt) and the answer's text is not repeated to the replan; the replan is the normal governed replan of §4 (zero native tools, through the broker, audited, token-counted, against attempt and lifetime replan budgets, transactional) with a fixed trigger directive (the goal may already be achieved but unresolved executable steps remain: re-evaluate, return an empty steps array if no further operational work is needed, else the revised remaining plan); an empty replan {"steps":[]} is an accepted revision after which the next call offers no operational tool and the final it produces (a NEW call, never the earlier premature reply) completes the task; a non-empty replan continues execution; on resume the fold treats a bookkeeping step as ReplanRequired so a resumed attempt replans first with the same trigger; the unresolved suffix of a replaced revision is Superseded (never Failed while the replan is owed) and no new status is introduced; no planned tool is ever executed without a model call, MAF decides nothing about completion and the replan budget bounds a model that keeps answering early.
column12: The condition-skipping part ('steps whose conditions deterministically settle') uses ADR-0050 (Proposed): listed under C03 Pending D4.

column2: Amendment AF-05H2: early-final replan without a plan
column5: Only a replan triggered by a rejected early final whose reply was received and was not a plan is eligible (provider exceptions, other triggers, budgets, cancellation and accepted plans unchanged; a received output-limit ('length') reply is not retried at the same limit); the persisted plan continues at its UNCHANGED cursor only on a bounded runtime proof: the plan has the semantic contract, the early final is the latest step of the revision, the fold over earlier steps is coherent with an unresolved step and no spent correction pending, the pending step is unconditional with a registered read-only tool offered in the current view, every earlier tool call of every revision has a result, used a registered read-only tool and was not denied/timed-out/refuted, and every earlier failure is a validation-class rejection of the planned tool in the current revision resolved by a later matched successful call of the same tool at the same planned index (anything else refused; a validation failure corrected only in a later revision stays unresolved); anti-loop: a continuation must be strictly further along than any earlier continuation of the same revision (RepeatedWithoutProgress), after one output-limit replan was continued a later early final of that revision is decided by the proof directly with no reserved replan, paid early-final replans are reserved against attempt and lifetime replan budgets before the call and continuations are never charged; every evaluation is persisted on the early-final step as an additive EarlyFinalRecoveryDecision (accepted, typed reason, revision, cursor, blocking step, resolved validation steps, whether a paid replan was skipped), an acceptance writes a continuation record and the EarlyFinalPlanContinued lifecycle audit event, a refusal the EarlyFinalPlanContinuationRefused event with a stable snake_case code and then fails the attempt as a malformed-response model failure; a continuation GRANTS NOTHING (the model must still call the pending tool through validation, step authority, policy, entitlement, approval and the mutation journal; resume re-proves it against the current tool view and the journal admission still refuses an unknown mutation outcome); replan calls of an early final are kept on its step as EarlyFinalReplanCalls disjoint from its ModelCalls.
column12: 'Semantic contract', 'Matched' classification and 'unconditional' step are terms of ADR-0050 (Proposed): see C03 Pending D4; the authority and anti-loop clauses stand independently.

column5: A rejected initial plan is re-asked with the runtime's own validation problem (bounded to 512 characters) ahead of the standing format instruction (an output-limit-cut reply with no text gets an output-limit notice, with no empty assistant turn; the replan corrective re-ask carries the problem the same way); at most TWO corrections follow the first reply (AgentRunner.MaxPlanCorrections) and a correction leaving the identical problem ends the corrections; each call is recorded, audited and charged and the token budget is checked after every call; WHEN NO VALID PLAN RESULTS the attempt FAILS as ModelFailure/MalformedResponse with a synthetic failure step 'Planning failed: ... Last problem: ...' carrying the planning calls, no plan is persisted so a resume plans again (ADR-0040 §7) - superseding the empty-plan degradation of ADR-0014 and ADR-0039 §8 for the initial plan (an accepted empty plan is unchanged); framing only: the plan text comes from the first markdown fence holding a JSON object, else the outermost braces, with strict JSON, schema, expectedArguments, activation and discriminator validation unchanged; the empty-reply re-ask (EmptyFinalResponseRetries) tells an output-limited model to call the offered tool or answer without further deliberation, bound and EmptyResponse terminal unchanged.
column12: expectedArguments/activation/discriminator validation are 0050 terms (Pending D4).

column2: Amendment AF-TOOLROUTE-01: names, in-step correction, completed checks
column5: Cause analysis (a MAF-boundary mapper dropped ToolNameError/ArgumentsError on the history round trip so a rejected raw name later appeared as an ordinary canonical call, the step prompt contradicted itself when all steps were resolved, and the replan re-proposed five completed checks); rules: (1) LOSSLESS boundary: adapter rejections cross the MAF boundary as reserved AdditionalProperties (bops.toolNameError, bops.argumentsError) and return unchanged, so a rejected raw name never contributes to a request's alias map and a canonical tool keeps ONE wire name for the whole task - no alias, prefix or fuzzy match, ToolWireNames unchanged; (2) in-step name correction: a call refused by name while the current planned step's single tool is offered, as that step's FIRST deviation, is classified UnofferedTool (append-only persisted value) and keeps the step (the next call offers the same single tool with a fixed correction sentence; nothing runs; audited UnknownTool as before; policy never consulted); a second refusal or one after a spent ADR-0047/0050 correction replans; the persisted fold carries the budget (ToolCorrectionSpent) so resume continues identically; (3) with every planned step resolved the prompt says so (answer from evidence or propose the one new check needed, which will not run and leads to a replan) and the following replan gets a runtime-authored turn stating the plan was complete and the call was refused for that reason, not its name; (4) every replan prompt lists the task's completed read checks (successful, not partial/unavailable, not refuted, read-only, sensitive values redacted, bounded to 2,048 chars) and a replan step whose tool and complete expectedArguments equal one of them is a validation problem of the existing corrective re-ask ('Plan step N repeats completed task step K...'); any different argument, tool or an empty plan is accepted unchanged; this is NOT duplicate suppression (nothing dropped, merged or rewritten; mutations, failures and partial results never count) and a model that repeats after the correction fails the attempt as ModelFailure/MalformedResponse with the plan preserved; unchanged: adapters, policy, approval, entitlement, journal, audit schema, accounting, resume rules, EvidenceRead; MAF orchestration is not used for routing or replanning.
column12: Mapper/boundary losslessness also appears in C01:maf-boundary.

column5: Prompt wording and the lifetime of one temporary instruction only (no routing, budget, policy, approval, audit, accounting or tool-surface change): (1) a completed plan still offers no operational tool and the instruction no longer promises that a prose proposal makes the runtime ask for a revised plan - text is the final answer, an evidence limit is reported in the answer, and the one recognized channel for more work is a native call of a tool the plan or task already names (refused, audited UnknownTool, answered by the governed replan); nothing parses prose; (2) the step prompt no longer says a final answer is a way to proceed while steps remain - a reply without a tool call is not taken as the final answer and only makes the runtime re-evaluate the plan (AF-05H unchanged); the Knowledge control instruction sends the next reply to the step's operational call while one is offered and to the final answer only when none is; (3) recovery prompts (empty/content-free, output limit) ask for the step's operational call while its tool is offered and for the final answer otherwise, a recovery turn is removed from the logical call as soon as the retry is answered with something usable (an unusable retry keeps it and the failure rule still applies), retry budget unchanged; (4) the step prompt says only the current step's tool is offered, later steps' tools are offered in their own turns, and no other tool, URL or resource is to be invented or assumed; (5) the one terminal correction after protocol-artifact markup follows the request's tool surface (a native call without text markup while a planned step's tool is offered, a final answer from the collected evidence with its limitations when none is offered), same budget and same failure after a repeated artifact; the runtime guarantees exactly what it did before and a model's reaction to clearer text is probabilistic, checked only by live reruns.
Accepted and implemented 2026-10-07; refines (does not supersede) ADR-0046.
column12: Metadata.

column5: ADR-0046 made ExpectedTool binding for visibility but every executed step that did not replan advanced the cursor; since a plain tool failure deliberately does not replan (C8), an argument-validation failure consumed the planned step and the next request offered only the NEXT tool, so the model could no longer correct the tool whose arguments failed (live task 9711a641: sinceDays in raw mode, then a rejected not-offered system_crashes); the unknown-tool rejection is correct and stays - the defect is that a validation failure on the exact intended tool consumed the step.
column12: Incident rationale.

column5: When the current planned step has a usable ExpectedTool, the model called exactly that offered tool, the call reached runtime argument validation (including arguments the adapter reported malformed) and the result is Failure with ToolFailureKind.Validation: the failed step is persisted, audited and accounted like any step (full ToolCallResult, model calls, step and token budgets); the planned-step cursor does NOT advance and no replan happens; the next execution request offers exactly the SAME single native tool (no other tool added, the catalog never restored); the model sees the failure in its history and the step prompt adds one fixed sentence asking it to call the same offered tool once more with corrected arguments.

Valid arguments go through the normal runtime path (policy, entitlement, approval, execution, verification) and any outcome other than another validation failure on that tool consumes the planned step as before (deviations - denial, rejection, timeout, refutation - still replan); a SECOND argument-validation failure on the same planned tool gives no third attempt and triggers the existing replan with zero native tools, unchanged replan budgets and ADR-0046 §4 transactional replanning; any other tool name keeps exact ADR-0046 enforcement (not offered -> rejected as UnknownTool, a deviation that replans; no alias, fuzzy match or rewrite); the correction never increments a replan counter (only an accepted replan does).

column2: Decision §3 position from persisted typed data
column5: The cursor, the spent correction and 'replan required' are ONE runtime value (PlannedStepPosition), a pure fold over the persisted steps of the current plan revision oldest first, advanced by the same function in the live loop; a step is an argument-validation failure on the planned tool only when ToolCall.ToolName equals the current ExpectedTool (ordinal), ToolNameError is null (an unknown/not-offered call never qualifies even though its rejection also carries Validation) and Result is Failure/Validation; once the correction is spent, deviations are recognised from typed data and each requires a replan (a call of another tool or with a ToolNameError; a runtime refusal ToolFailureKind.Authorization assigned only by the runtime for policy/operator/envelope/entitlement denials; ToolOutcome.Timeout; PlanStep.VerificationStatus Refuted) - recording the requirement matters when the replan does not commit and the task is resumed; neither error text nor the step description is ever parsed and synthetic failure steps carry no plan revision and do not count; resume reconstructs: after a first validation failure the same step, its single tool and an already-spent correction; after a successful correction the following step; after a spent correction followed by a second failure or a deviation whose replan did not commit, the resumed attempt replans first before any operational tool is offered (triggered by the last persisted step of the stale revision); a record written before this ADR where a validation failure was followed by an executed call of another tool contradicts the one-correction rule so the runtime fails closed and replans first.

ADR-0046 step-scoped visibility, ExpectedTool as intention, runtime ownership of safety, first-call-wins and UnexecutedToolCalls, transactional replanning, EvidenceRead/v1, compaction, provider fallback, fail-closed resume, budgets and auditing of every validation failure are unchanged.

Rejected: a new persisted PlanStep field (typed data already identifies the case; PlanStep is part of the frozen surface); an in-memory retry counter (resume would reset it); treating every validation failure as a deviation; offering previous and next tool together; alias or fuzzy-matching names such as system_crashes.

A planned step can take at most two execution steps for argument validation, both ordinary budgeted audited steps; live and resume compute the position from the same persisted steps so a crash cannot reset or extend the correction; a resumed task whose plan already exhausted its correction spends one replan before offering a tool; no contract, manifest, wire format, persistence or status change.
Accepted and implemented 2026-10-08 (D-045).
column12: Metadata.

column5: bOps could list crash dump files but not look inside them; a kernel dump can contain sensitive kernel memory so analysis must not give the model a general-purpose local-file reader, a debugger console or a shell (S1, S11); package code depends only on Abstractions and its family library and the core must not name a package, tool or debugger (A1).

One new Read tool system.dump_analyze (platform windows) for Windows small kernel dumps (minidumps), kernel and complete memory dumps KD can open and LiveKernelReports kernel dumps; user-mode/application dumps, CDB, process.dump_analyze, dump generation and crash-control settings are out of scope; system.crashes and system.stability only MENTION it and never call it; one required argument path (Path, 7-260 chars) and NO parameter for a debugger command, symbol path, script, extension, timeout or output format; shared manifest/reader/DTOs/formatter/audit summary in System.Core with the gating capability name passed in by the Windows package so shared code never names a debugger.

The package owns capability windows.debugger.kd registered by the API and CLI composition roots (before the first RefreshCapabilitiesAsync, Windows only); the check only looks at files and launches, installs and downloads nothing; with no acceptable kd.exe the tool is absent from the planner catalog; the backend is Microsoft's command-line Debugging Tools (kd.exe engine, dumpchk.exe optional preflight) - DbgEng COM interop, WinDbg GUI automation, PowerShell, cmd.exe and a home-grown dump parser are rejected; deterministic bounded discovery: fully qualified PATH entries in order (at most 64), then Windows Kits\10\Debuggers\<arch> under Program Files (x86) then Program Files; a candidate must be a regular file, not a reparse point, with a version resource naming Microsoft; dumpchk.exe is used only from the chosen kd.exe's directory; nothing is installed automatically.

The policy denies by default: an accepted path is an absolute local drive path ending .dmp or .mdmp made only of letters, digits, space, '.', '_', '-' and parentheses, with no '/', no second ':' (alternate data stream), no control characters and no UNC, \\?\, \\.\ or \??\ prefix; after Path.GetFullPath it must lie strictly under %SystemRoot%\Minidump or %SystemRoot%\LiveKernelReports or be exactly %SystemRoot%\MEMORY.DMP; every existing component from the drive root to the file is checked with File.GetAttributes and ANY reparse point (junction, symlink, mount point) rejects (FileInfo.Exists is not used because it answers false when a parent cannot be listed); a missing file is not-found, an unreadable one access-denied (never reported as absence); the decision is made again immediately before DumpChk and again before KD (S11); a rejected path is a Validation failure and nothing is launched.

Each run is kd.exe -noshell -sins -y <symbol path> -z <dump path> -c <script> with every argument through ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList, UseShellExecute=false, no window, stdin closed; stdout (<=4 Mi chars) and stderr (<=64 Ki) drained concurrently; hard limit 10 minutes plus the caller's cancellation, the whole process tree killed on either; every _NT_* and DBGHELP_* variable and INIT removed from the environment; each run in its own empty bOps-owned working directory (so no ntsd.ini/tools.ini is picked up) deleted in finally; the source-controlled script is a fixed sequence of .bugcheck, !analyze -v, lm, !blackboxpnp and !blackboxbsd, each between per-run nonce markers (16 random hex chars so dump data cannot forge a section boundary), the dump path is never part of the -c string, and the script contains no memory display (db/dd/dq/dw/du...), no search, no .load, no script and no .shell; DumpChk runs first when present with the path as its only argument and a 60 s limit, only its exit status used (its exit-code semantics are unverified so a failed DumpChk does not stop KD): invalid only when DumpChk failed AND KD produced no evidence, partial with warning dumpchk-reported-problem when KD still produced analysis, warning dumpchk-unavailable when absent.

Operator decision: text-first parsing for V1 (the !analyze -xml structure is undocumented and no real output was available); the parser reads only text between exact nonce marker lines and takes from !analyze -v only an allowlist of documented fields (BUGCHECK_CODE, BUGCHECK_P1-P4, PROCESS_NAME, MODULE_NAME, IMAGE_NAME, SYMBOL_NAME, EXCEPTION_CODE_STR, FAILURE_BUCKET_ID, FAILURE_ID_HASH, BUCKET_ID) plus the NAME (code) header, Arg1-Arg4 and STACK_TEXT, with .bugcheck as the code fallback and lm for module ranges/symbol state; black boxes are reported as available plus bounded excerpt lines and device instance identifiers with undocumented layout not otherwise interpreted; the XML parser is deferred until real output is captured; versioned JSON schemaVersion 1 with limits (64 stack frames, 32 modules implicated first, 32 warnings, 2 KiB text fields, 64×256 black-box lines, 32 device identifiers, 4 KiB rawAnalysisExcerpt, whole result 32 KiB UTF-8) dropped in fixed order (raw excerpt, black-box lines, non-implicated modules, stack tail); rawAnalysisExcerpt appears only when no bugcheck code parsed and only from the fixed !analyze section; raw memory is NEVER emitted; a field the debugger did not print is null, distinct from an empty list.

status complete (every section closed, PDB-backed kernel symbols, a bugcheck code and a resolved module, no timeout/cut/DumpChk failure), partial (some evidence with a limitation), unavailable (failure not-found, access-denied, debugger-unavailable, timeout or debugger-failure), invalid (DumpChk failed and KD found no evidence); a missing black box or preflight is a warning and black-box available:false is absence of data NEVER evidence of health; a symbol problem is symbols.status partial/unavailable, never invalid; a timeout with nothing parsed is ToolOutcome.Timeout, after some evidence a successful partial result with failure 'timeout'; the analysis object carries qualifier 'debugger-attribution' and the manifest plus a fixed interpretation string state the attribution is NOT a proven root cause; the audit summary records aggregates only (status, failure, truncation, dump kind, bugcheck code, symbol status, DumpChk use, black-box availability, frame count) and never the path, frames, modules, device identifiers or debugger text.

The symbol path is fixed (srv*%LOCALAPPDATA%\bOps\Symbols*https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols); no argument can change it, -sins and the environment scrub stop a machine-wide _NT_SYMBOL_PATH from injecting another server and there are no credentials; no operator symbol path is added in V1; Microsoft public symbols do not cover third-party drivers (normally partial); downloading symbols is part of the analysis and the tool's risk is still Read.

Every tool runs under the single Agent:DefaultToolTimeout (30 s) and no manifest can declare its own timeout; a first analysis with a cold symbol download often exceeds it; this ADR neither raises the global default nor adds a per-manifest timeout (an Abstractions change needing its own ADR); on token fire the tool kills KD's process tree and the runner reports Timeout; operators who use dump analysis should raise Agent:DefaultToolTimeout (e.g. 00:05:00) as for Docker builds; a per-tool timeout declaration is a follow-up.
column12: Operator guidance (documented); the structural gap (no per-tool timeout) is recorded as a known limit in C02:dump-analysis.

column5: Rejected: DbgEng COM / native API; WinDbg GUI automation or PowerShell driving WinDbg (a shell or GUI command surface, S1); XML-first parsing of an undocumented shape; a model-supplied debugger command or symbol server (a generic execution surface); configurable extra dump roots (deferred); treating a failed DumpChk as decisive.

An LLM gets bounded delimited kernel-dump evidence for one approved dump without raw memory or a command surface; a host without kd.exe is unchanged (tool invisible); parser behavior against real debugger releases is NOT yet validated (synthetic labelled fixtures; first real validation after deployment); a cold-symbol analysis may time out under the default 30 s; two catalog tests became platform-aware (first one-OS-only first-party tool).
column12: Consequences of a landed tool; the validation gap is recorded as an implementation status note on C02:dump-analysis.

column5: Accepted 2026-10-08 (D-046), implemented in three sessions; amends rule B4 (ICapabilityProbe becomes a compatibility view) and ADR-0025 (Capability manifests gain prerequisite declarations); neither accepted ADR is edited.

Capabilities were booleans on CachingCapabilityProbe and an unmet one made a tool silently disappear; that cannot express registered-vs-available, optional dependencies (kd.exe required, dumpchk.exe optional), Skill Capability prerequisites, plugin-contributed checks or operator notification (logs are for developers, audit records actions, task evidence is model input - none is an operator inbox).
column12: Rationale; rules in Decision.

column5: Every Tool and Skill Capability has two independent facts: registered (loaded and validated) and available (its REQUIRED prerequisites are satisfied right now); a registered-but-unavailable component is never offered to a model and never resolves for execution; unsatisfied OPTIONAL prerequisites leave it available and degraded.

Additive Abstractions contracts: PrerequisiteDescriptor (stable id, display name, description, kind, operator remediation text, check timeout), IPrerequisiteCheck (one package-owned READ-ONLY cancellable check returning a PrerequisiteCheckOutcome with state, stable code, message, metadata - no id, no timestamp), IPrerequisiteProvider (optional interface a package entry point implements), PrerequisiteCheckResult (host-stamped id and CheckedAtUtc from TimeProvider), PrerequisiteState {Unknown, Available, Degraded, Unavailable, Error}, PrerequisiteRequirement, OperationalMetadata; a package never stamps its own id or timestamp (like A11); Unknown is host-internal (a check returning it is recorded as Error); an existing IToolProvider/ISkillProvider entry point may also implement IPrerequisiteProvider, discovered the same way for first-party packages and enabled plugins, registered under the host-assigned PackageId and unregistered with the package; no package-to-package resolution (A9): components reference prerequisites by string id only; a prerequisite id may be registered by exactly ONE package (a second registration is refused so a plugin cannot shadow a first-party check); ids match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}$ and codes ^[a-z0-9]+([.-][a-z0-9]+)*$ (<=64).

ToolManifest.Requires keeps its meaning and is by definition REQUIRED prerequisites; ToolManifest.OptionalRequires (init, default empty) and CapabilityManifest.Requires/OptionalRequires (init, default empty, constructor unchanged) are new; one id in both lists of a manifest or a blank optional id is refused at registration; the frozen surface is untouched (only lines added; Abstractions to 1.3.0-preview.3).

bOps.Runtime.PrerequisiteRegistry (host-owned, mutable, NOT an ICapabilityProbe) owns registration, execution, timeouts, caching and state; a check runs under a linked timeout (descriptor timeout, default 10 s, clamped 1-60 s) and a timeout, thrown exception or invalid outcome becomes Error with a fixed code (check-timeout, check-failed, check-invalid-result) and fixed message - exception text is NEVER copied (it can carry secrets) while caller cancellation propagates; what a package receives under ICapabilityProbe (A10) is PrerequisiteRegistry.AsCapabilityProbe(), a distinct read-only boolean view (Available/Degraded -> true; Unavailable/Error/Unknown and unregistered ids -> false) that cannot be cast to the registry or to the host-only IPrerequisiteRegistrar (never resolvable through RestrictedPackageServiceProvider); ICapabilityProbe and CachingCapabilityProbe are not removed or renamed and a host-side BooleanPrerequisiteCheck migrates existing boolean checks without behavior change; ToolRegistry and SkillRegistry snapshot the full PrerequisiteState from the host-owned IPrerequisiteStateSource (last recorded result, no I/O), or for an arbitrary probe true -> Available / false -> Unavailable: required Available available, Degraded available AND degraded, Unavailable/Error/Unknown not available; optional Available no degradation, any other state available AND degraded; a tool with unmet required prerequisites stays hidden (GetReadiness reports every registered tool; SkillRegistry withholds such a Capability from GetAvailableSkills and Resolve); a Capability with Requires but no probe/source FAILS CLOSED.

A system message is an operator-facing operational notice - NOT application logging, NOT audit (it proves nothing and is not hash-chained) and NOT model evidence (it never enters a model context); SystemMessage {Id, TimestampUtc, Node, Source '<kind>/<name>', Severity Information|Warning|Error|Critical (no Debug/Trace), Code (stable machine value), Message <=1,024, Metadata, optional TaskId/ComponentType/ComponentId}; OperationalMetadata holds <=32 entries, keys ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, values strings (<=512), numbers, booleans, null or arrays of <=32 strings, <=4,096 UTF-8 bytes serialized, and REFUSES keys whose normalized name contains password, passwd, secret, token, apikey, credential, privatekey, connectionstring, authorization or cookie and string values carrying URL user-info or a 'Bearer ' prefix (defence in depth: metadata must never carry a secret).

Checks do not write messages, transitions do: PrerequisiteTransitionRecorder compares each result with the persisted state of the same (node, prerequisite) by fingerprint state|code (none->Available: quiet; ->Unavailable: prerequisite.missing, Warning if any component requires it else Information; ->Degraded: prerequisite.degraded likewise; Unavailable/Degraded/Error->Available: prerequisite.recovered Information; ->Error: prerequisite.check-failed Error; same fingerprint: none; message text or metadata alone never emits); ONE message per prerequisite transition never per affected tool (metadata carries affectedComponents <=16 and affectedComponentCount); the state row and message are written in one SQLite transaction guarded by compare-and-set on the previous fingerprint so two concurrent identical observations write one message.

Messages and prerequisite state live in one node-local SQLite database owned by bOps.Memory (SqliteSystemMessageStore, user_version 1; a newer schema refused), never in audit.jsonl, task JSON or log files; SystemMessageQuery: optional inclusive FromUtc/ToUtc, exact Severity, case-insensitive Text contained in Message, combined with AND, ordered TimestampUtc DESC then Id DESC, KEYSET pagination with an opaque versioned cursor (never OFFSET), page size default 50 range 1-200; time-based retention PurgeOlderThanAsync default 90 days; archival and export out of scope.

The transition recorder uses the registered descriptor ('<DisplayName> is unavailable. <Remediation>', remediation <=600 and message <=1,024; the check's own free-text message is not copied into the inbox); RefreshAsync runs at most Prerequisites:MaxConcurrency (default 4, 1-32) checks at once, each once, ordered by id, a failing check is a result and caller cancellation propagates; PrerequisiteReadinessService serialises one cycle (registry refresh -> atomic transition and message records -> Tool and Skill snapshots) used by the API boot refresh, the periodic coordinator and the CLI one-shot refresh; API boot order: compose first-party providers and checks -> activate enabled plugins -> one full refresh -> only then accept work, and a missing ordinary prerequisite never stops the host (components stay registered, unavailable, with a Warning); periodic refresh is API-only (Prerequisites:RefreshIntervalSeconds default 30, 5-3600; the CLI has no timer); a plugin entry point implementing IPrerequisiteProvider is registered under the plugin's host-assigned id BEFORE its tools and Skills (a later failure rolls it back) and removed before its load context is released (model-provider plugin providers are not registered); API: GET /api/system-messages and GET /api/prerequisites (current-state projection, not a second store), both Viewer; retention SystemMessages:RetentionDays (90) purged at API start then every RetentionIntervalMinutes (360), never on insertion, deleting in batches of 1,000.

UNRECORDED IS UNAVAILABLE: the cycle order (check, record durably, then snapshot) is an invariant - when RecordAsync throws the host replaces that prerequisite's result in the registry (AddHostObservation) with Error and the host-authored code state-record-failed BEFORE any Tool/Skill snapshot, so required dependents are not available and optional ones degraded, the successful check result is not reused, the text is fixed (no exception text reaches state, messages or the API, logged server-side), other prerequisites still record, overrides are replaced as a set at the end of each cycle so a later successful record restores normal behavior, and if the message store itself is down nothing is written and nothing gains authority; DECLARED BUT UNREGISTERED is observable: declared ids (Requires and OptionalRequires of every registered Tool and Skill Capability, lower-cased) minus registered ids are recorded as host-observed Error/not-registered through the same recorder (persisted, deduplicated by fingerprint across refreshes and restarts, one message prerequisite.not-registered per prerequisite, Error if some component requires it else Warning, with no invented remediation), a later registered check transitions normally, and an id the state store could never hold stays unavailable, is logged and not recorded; PLUGIN LIFECYCLE refreshes immediately at the API boundary (not in bOps.PluginHost) - a successful non-replayed enable or disable runs one RefreshAsync before the response, a failing refresh is logged and changes nothing about the committed result; rejected, stale, unconfirmed, failed and replayed operations and recovery refresh nothing.

AgentRunner (additive optional ISystemMessageStore argument; no widening of the A10 package surface) writes one Warning (source runtime/agent, code agent.replan.threshold) when an ACCEPTED replan brings the task's lifetime count to Agent:ReplanWarningThreshold (equality, so at most once per task; default 3, capped by MaxLifetimeReplans only when unset; an explicit value must be 1..MaxLifetimeReplans); it carries task id, provider and model ids, counts and attempt - no goal, prompt, model reply, tool argument or output; best effort, bounded to 5 s, logged on failure and never fails the task, changes its state or triggers a retry.

/system-messages page reads GET /api/system-messages with From/To, Severity and Text filters sent to the server on Apply (AND-combined), Reset, newest first, 50 per page, keyset cursor navigation (Previous re-requests the cursor that produced the earlier page; no offset, no client filtering/paging), loading/empty/error states, severity as word+glyph+accessible label, expandable details with metadata rendered as escaped JSON text; no page for /api/prerequisites; SystemMessages:FilePath (default system-messages.db, relative to the working directory) unchanged.

column2: Decision s3.2 gate table and boundary

MutationOutcomeKind NotInvoked=0 (known not executed), Returned=1 (known executed, Success or Failure or contained throw; Failure may have partially applied, S7), TimedOut=2, Cancelled=3, Interrupted=4 (unknown), no outcome (unknown); settled iff the end was observed and the tool did not report a timeout, or never invoked, or verification confirmed; a tool-reported Timeout is unknown; a Failure is never relabelled safe to retry.

Every executed non-Read call is verified whatever its kind; for unknown kinds only Confirmed settles (known executed); Refuted/Inconclusive do not (R7: effect may still complete); for Returned verification is information and drives replanning as before.

TaskMutationState Pending=0, Settled=1, Ambiguous=2, Escalated=3, ReconciledDone=4, Abandoned=5; unsettled = Pending/Ambiguous/Escalated; Abandoned blocks resume permanently; OperatorAcceptedDone stays unknown but treated as executed; classification is one pure runtime function (MutationJournalPolicy), stores only persist and use it in predicates.

Key (TaskId, ExecutionAttempt, StepIndex) plus per-task monotonic Sequence assigned inside the intent statement; StepIndex alone is not unique across attempts; plan revision/planned index are context only, never used to match calls.

Intent holds TaskId, attempt, step, sequence, canonical ToolName, ArgumentsHash (SHA-256 over canonical arguments with Sensitive values replaced by the redaction marker), Risk, declared VerificationToolName, PlanRevision/PlannedStepIndex, IntentAtUtc; never raw or redacted arguments, ArgumentsFrom projection, credentials, output, error text, provider material, approvals or entitlement decisions; reconciliation arguments come only from the task's own recorded step, absence = verification unavailable (price of P8; windows C2-C6 always need an administrator).

Intent requires (Running,N) and a free key; Outcome requires an existing entry with no outcome and no reconciliation AND (Running,N) and in the same transaction replaces the task row with the step; Reconcile requires (S,N) with S not Running and expected unsettled states, all-or-nothing; Acquire requires no Pending/Ambiguous/Escalated/Abandoned entry and every named entry ReconciledDone with history unrecorded; Recovery is the existing TryTransitionAsync; SqliteTaskStore.TryTransitionAsync enforces the same predicate for any acquisition.

column2: Decision s9.6 approvals and policy after restart

Startup does nothing new: no recovery, verification, reconciliation, resume or write; detection happens on read in the task view; the only path from restart to a tool running again is recover, reconcile if needed, resume, then every gate.

ITaskMutationJournalStore : ITaskTransitionStore (TryRecordIntent, TryRecordOutcome, LoadWithJournal, TryReconcile, TryAcquire) is additive; each method atomic across threads and processes, never load-check-save, LoadWithJournal a consistent snapshot; fail closed decided once per task (Journaled if the store implements it else MutationsDisabled for life; a Journaled task on a store lacking it refuses resume and non-Read execution; no journal-unavailable-execute-anyway path).
SqliteTaskStore implements the capability; test doubles executing non-Read tools must implement it too.

Legacy (Absent) ordinary rows: resume refused mutation_journal_absent, recovery refused mutation_journal_absent, no intent invented; Completed/PolicyBlocked/delegated/unknown-origin keep the unchanged 0040 refusals.

Read calls never have an entry; a task interrupted during a Read, a model call or between steps has no unsettled entry and is resumable after recovery under 0040 rules; read-interrupted and mutation-outcome-unknown are different states with different codes.

Guarantees P1-P15: no non-Read begins without a durable intent; an intent without outcome never proves did-not-happen; ambiguous never auto-re-executed; proven/accepted-applied never re-executed by resume, recovery or reconciliation; approvals never reused; read-only work separately recoverable; late writes cannot authorize/settle/replay; no raw arguments or output in the journal; 0040 safety not weakened; nothing at startup; every write atomic and fenced; settled outcome never durable without its step; recovery/reconciliation never invoke a non-Read tool; without a usable journal no mutation runs; pre-F-25 rows never assumed safe.

column5: Accepted 2026-10-10 (D-048); research baseline main 2f961f7 and Microsoft.Agents.AI 1.24.0.

The product requirement is that bOps is built on MAF; the split is MAF owns generic agent infrastructure while bOps owns operational authority, safety, evidence semantics and recovery; MAF may influence what the model sees and never what bOps executes.

MAF is the reference framework and preferred implementation for conversation/message infrastructure, context construction, compaction, tool-result compaction, summarization, context-window management, context middleware and (where proven useful without weakening authority) function-call plumbing and future Coordinator sessions/workflows/memory; bOps keeps exclusive ownership of AgentPlan and revisions, exact step/tool authority and visibility, manifests and argument validation, RiskLevel, policy, entitlement, human approval, mutation journal, machine-side execution, post-action verification, EvidenceFact/completeness/limitations/grounding, TaskState/resume/fencing, unknown-outcome handling, audit semantics, provider pinning/fallback and task/model budgets; no MAF component may bypass these.

Project-owned IChatModel/ChatTurn/ModelToolCall/ModelRequest/ModelResponse/ChatModelDescriptor/ModelUsage remain public contracts in the dependency-free Abstractions; ADR-0001 no longer prohibits MAF inside the implementation: the public contract is not a Microsoft contract but the runtime implementation may use MAF.

Planning/replanning stays bOps-owned; HARDEN-8 BoundedHistory becomes migration/reference code while raw evidence and EvidenceRead addressability remain; every inference caused by a task incl. summarization uses the governed invocation path; MAF sessions/checkpoints do not replace TaskState, fencing or resume.

Delegation authority and entitlement stay bOps-owned; MAF summaries are context never evidence; provider selection, pinning and fallback stay bOps-owned; MAF cannot widen the operational tool surface; mutation journaling and reconciliation unchanged and MAF workflow/session state is no substitute for external-side-effect uncertainty.

MAF lives behind a dedicated non-SDK integration assembly (name not architectural) above Runtime; no MAF or Microsoft.Extensions.AI type in Abstractions; providers remain implementations of IChatModel; Runtime public surface does not require MAF types; the MAF package version is explicitly pinned (no floating ranges); experimental compaction APIs accepted because the dependency is isolated with a temporary deterministic fallback; MAF types must not leak into the plugin SDK.

Retry classification, retry attempts, Retry-After, attempt timeout, logical-call budget, provider fallback, model-call audit/records and cumulative token accounting sit behind a bOps-owned IModelInvocationBroker; every task inference (planning, replanning, step reasoning, final synthesis, grounding/final checks, evidence-disclosure correction, context summarization, future MAF reasoning) passes through it; MAF components needing IChatClient are adapted over the broker and MAF never owns provider credentials or its own retry/fallback; summarization counts toward model usage and token budget and is model-call audited.

BoundedHistory is not evolved into a second context framework; authoritative TaskState (plan/step, EvidenceFacts, grounding, limitations, history) feeds the MAF context layer then ModelRequest then the broker; projection/compaction is model-facing only and never rewrites persisted raw task/evidence state.

Generic compaction must not remove or summarize current execution authority: standing security instructions, current user goal, current plan revision, current planned step and ExpectedTool, semantic/argument correction state, current EvidenceGrounding and EvidenceLimitations, mutation-reconciliation notices and other runtime-authored state needed for the current call; they may live outside the compactable list but no generic strategy decides they are disposable.

The bOps/MAF mapper preserves roles, text, call IDs, tool names, arguments, multiple calls per assistant message, existing not-executed results, ordering and Unicode; a call and its result are an atomic group; mapping or compaction can never turn an unexecuted historical call into an executed one.

A runtime/host-side ModelContextProfile (ProviderId, ModelId, MaxContextTokens, ReservedOutputTokens, Source) is never guessed from provider family names; router models such as openrouter/free have unknown limits unless configuration or provider metadata supplies a conservative guaranteed value; each fallback candidate has its own profile and projection uses the currently effective execution-scoped candidate; unknown capacity fails conservatively; the profile is not part of the plugin SDK.

column5: History budget = context window - reserved output - system prompt reserve - offered tool-schema reserve - protected runtime-context reserve - safety reserve; no production trigger percentage is architectural; MAF token counts are estimates unless proven exact, provider-reported PromptTokens is authoritative after the call, telemetry compares both, and no hard safety guarantee relies only on an unvalidated estimate.

Pipeline order from lower to higher information loss: ToolResult, Summarization, SlidingWindow, Truncation; thresholds, budgets, recent-group counts and reserves are measured tuning values and MAF defaults are reference values not architecture.

column2: Decision s12.1-12.2 summarization selection and governance
column5: Summarizer defaults to the task provider/model; an operator may explicitly configure a summarization-only provider/model (an explicit data-egress choice) but bOps never moves summarization to another provider automatically; the call goes through the broker, is model-call audited, obeys timeout/failure containment, counts toward budgets and uses the normal credential path.

A summary is derived untrusted context never evidence (order: raw persisted evidence > EvidenceFact/completeness/verification > runtime grounding/limitations > LLM summary) and cannot create facts, change completeness/verification, activate conditional steps, satisfy policy/approval, settle a mutation or replace raw evidence; summarization failure restores the candidate history and continues deterministic compaction while cancellation still propagates.

runtime.evidence_read stays a bOps control-plane mechanism for exceptional exact drill-down; exhausting the valid read budget no longer terminates the task (supersedes the RuntimeFailure rule): valid exhaustion and malformed protocol are distinct, EvidenceRead is no longer offered for that logical call, the model continues with available evidence, ordinary step/replan/token/duration budgets remain the anti-loop guards, and exhaustion alone never owns the terminal state.

High-density tools (system.stability, system.crashes, system.dump_analyze, storage.health) expose bounded decision-relevant structured facts; packages own the fact vocabulary and the runtime stays opaque to domain keys; complete tool JSON is not mirrored into facts.

The operational tool surface stays bOps-owned: for a normal planned step the exact ExpectedTool plus runtime.evidence_read when eligible; MAF must not independently expose hosted web search, filesystem, shell/code execution, MAF skills, background agents, arbitrary function tools or extra package tools; extending that needs a future ADR through the bOps authority model.

Full HarnessAgent adoption is deferred; no bOps safety/authority responsibility moves to Harness without explicitly proving and recording the new boundary; ChatHistoryProvider, AgentSession and MAF workflow checkpoints do not replace TaskState, fencing, journaling or reconciliation; the V1.4 Coordinator may use MAF sessions/workflows/AIContextProvider/memory behind the same principles.

column5: registrationStatus is a statement about the host registry never events (registered: catalog enumerable and lists the name, Windows only; notRegistered: catalog enumerated, non-empty, no such name, Windows only; unknown: always on Linux, and on Windows when enumeration failed or returned no names); observedMatch is a statement about records read and is the only value confirming a name from data; caution is a pure function of the two (observedMatch true -> null; false+registered -> null; false+notRegistered -> noMatchSourceNotRegistered; false+unknown -> noMatchSourceUnverified), silent for registered, never saying the name does not exist; the dimensions are independent.

observedMatch = Matched(snapshot, query).Any(), the sequence behind observedEvents evaluated before grouping, limit and the byte budget and never read from events/groups/returnedEvents/returnedGroups; observedMatch == (observedEvents > 0) whenever sourceFilter is not null; its definition is the whole query (source with window, minSeverity, eventId, channel, text, excludeSources) and semantics says 'that kind' not 'that name'; no source-only definition (it would mean different things on the Windows native-filter path).

Windows reads the provider catalog once per call and shares it for source and excludeSources; registered -> existing native Provider[@Name] predicate, notRegistered/unknown -> no native predicate and the shared post-filter; ceiling, 20 s budget, XPath construction and truncated rules unchanged; failed enumeration is unknown and does not make a source partial; a notRegistered name with records gives observedMatch true and caution null; a historical name beyond the ceiling gives observedMatch false with noMatchSourceNotRegistered AND truncated true. Linux: registrationStatus always unknown, no journalctl/field query/switch added, matchedFields ["source","unit"]. Shared: package-local SystemEventSnapshot carries SourceRegistration (default Unknown) and SourceMatchedFields (default ["source"]) and Format builds sourceFilter; runtime core untouched.

Case rulings: budget worst case 3,058 B (raw) and 3,510 B (aggregate) of 4,096; historical provider never reported as nonexistent; a registered provider not publishing to the queried channels is registered/observedMatch false/caution null with semantics as the disclosure (LogLinks check is a later refinement outside this ADR); enumeration failure -> unknown with no exception to the caller and status/complete unchanged; partial windows: observedMatch false is never read as none exist when truncated, a source partial or coverage partial/unknown; aggregate: sourceFilter is envelope identical in both modes and observedMatch comes from pre-grouping records.

D1: registrationStatus, observedMatch and caution never alter status, complete, truncated, sources, coverage or ToolCallResult.Completeness (a notRegistered or unverifiable name does NOT make the result Partial); no inference of absence (complete true with sourceFilter means complete for events whose source matches requested); SystemEventFacts unchanged, no fact carries sourceFilter and no zero-count fact is ever added, the limitations digest does not see caution; the audit summary gains sourceFilter {registrationStatus, observedMatch, caution} without requested or messages, audit schema unchanged; sourceFilter contains no record or catalog text (requested is the caller's validated string, the rest closed sets or constants).

sourceFilter is part of the envelope the byte budget never cuts; measured worst case at the 4,096-byte minimum maxOutputBytes: envelope 3,058 B raw / 3,510 B aggregate with a 528 B object, typical about 390 B, +20 B for the null form; if the worst-case envelope exceeds 3,584 bytes or any combination reaches 4,096, implementation stops and returns to architecture rather than shortening the field; at the floor with every maximum, 586 bytes remain in aggregate mode and a 512-character sample message may be removed with truncated true.

Three layers so zero records is not read as certain absence: (1) in the result, the fixed English constant sourceFilter.semantics (SourceFilterEvidence.Semantics, 203 bytes, identical on both platforms, naming no domain or provider); (2) manifest sentences on the system.events description and the source parameter (best effort, may be shortened before the model sees it), optionally the same intent as display-only PlanningGuidance (ADR-0060); (3) docs/system-events.md explaining the object, the table and the reading rule; the runtime adds no instruction or heuristic.

D1 completeness not degraded; D2 first version has no similar-provider suggestions, aliases, fuzzy matching or hardware-specific mapping (the catalog only answers is this exact name registered and is never listed back, and strings/codes name no domain); D3 sourceFilter immediately follows excludeSources with verified envelope budget; approved correction: two independent dimensions instead of one verification enum.

Rejected: a merged verification enum, marking the result Partial, rejecting an unregistered name, suggestions/aliases/fuzzy matches, a hardware-specific mapping, a source-only observedMatch, a filter-free second probe, verifying on Linux via journalctl -F/systemctl, a LogLinks check (candidate follow-up), carrying the reading in an EvidenceFact or the runtime digest, omitting the key without a source, bumping schemaVersion, putting the explanation only in the manifest.
